title: Account Representative-Launch | 2027 Early Career Program - Detroit, MI
description:
As part of the TTI Inc. Career Launch Program, the Account Representative (Launch) will attend and participate in an intensive training program to gain knowledge through classroom and practical hands-on application in the Corporate office (North Fort Worth, TX). After completion of the program, the Account Representative (Launch) will transition into the Sales organization and be based in one of our branch office locations. The Account Representative (Launch) sells company products and services via telephone, internet, e-mail, and fax. Works in conjunction with Field Sales Representatives, Product Management, and Sales Management to increase customer penetration and sales opportunities. Success is measured by meeting defined sales objectives and performing all duties with a high ethical standard and exceeding all customer requirements.

Headquartered in Fort Worth, TX, TTI, Inc. is the world’s leading authorized distributor of passive, connector, electromechanical, and discrete components. Celebrating more than 50 years, this Berkshire Hathaway company is ever-growing and has over 100 locations in North America, Europe, and Asia! Join a winning team in a growing global organization!

Our Account Representatives Team:

  • Sells products and services offered by TTI. This includes, but is not limited to, product lines, AIM programs, quality, and value-added services. The sale is attained by building relationships and tailoring the sales approach to meet and inquire on the customers needs. This is measured through monthly sales reporting, quality objectives and regular management reviews.
  • Provides price and delivery quotes within customer timeline to customers within assigned geographic territory by working with the branch or corporate product manager and the manufacturers to get the most competitive pricing by utilizing communication by telephone, fax and email. The Account Reps success is measured by booking the business at the highest gross profit margin.
  • Processes the customer’s order by entering it into the sales database for quote processing and delivery schedules. Requires eye for detail, proof reading for accuracy, and maintaining quality expectations. Failure to process and review in a timely manner can result to a loss of parts and lead time with factories. This is measured by your customers on time delivery and RMA rate.
  • Expands product knowledge by utilizing all resources including product literature, factory representatives, product managers, sales managers, and other sales representatives to be able to discuss product options with customers and sell TTI strengths.
  • Participates in the TTI Total Quality process by following defined policies and procedures to maintain efficient sales cycle, following logical and systematic approaches, while the goal being to reduce sales errors and uphold quality to the highest level. This is measured by how many lines are shipped per salesperson and determined how many lines were on time and crossed checked for errors.
  • Increases customer account base by compiling list of prospective customer leads from various sources and makes cold calls. Number of new customers should grow based on this activity.
  • Provides management with information regarding sales, marketing techniques, new products, and market strategy by preparing forecast and activity reports on account territory.
  • Participates and attends sales calls with Field Sales Representatives to develop sales relationship and trust with the customer and TTI. Increased sales are result of good relationship sales.
  • If performing duties as a designated quality representative, processes and resolves discrepant issues identified within the job function in an expeditious manner by researching the issue, determining appropriate resolution and by providing disposition for nonconforming product to the appropriate parties.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned.

Education and Experience Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree with 0 to 2 years of experience in sales, customer service, or a related field (internship experience accepted).
  • Candidates must have graduated from a bachelor’s degree program within the past two years of the start of the Launch program.

What we look for:

  • Exhibits exceptional knowledge of company products and services.
  • Demonstrates persuasiveness, tenacity, and strong selling skills.
  • Possesses excellent verbal and written communication skills, including excellent presentation skills.
  • Exhibits strong analytical, problem solving and negotiation skills.
  • Must be organized and able to prioritize and manage multiple tasks.
  • Ability to calculate discounts, commissions, proportions and percentages.
  • Ability to write reports and correspondence proficiently and professionally.
  • Reads, analyzes, and interprets business periodicals, professional journals, technical procedures and government regulations.
  • Able to work with minimum supervision and make responsible decisions.
  • Possesses working knowledge of company policies, procedures and computer systems.
  • Ability to type 40 words per minute.
  • Knowledge of Microsoft Office applications (Excel and Word) at a basic level required.
  • Must be able to travel locally and domestically up to 50% as needed to visit branches, customers and partners.
  • Due to the 4-month duration of the program, 100% attendance is expected to help trainees maximize their learning experience, fully engage in key projects, and make a meaningful impact on their team and the organization.

This is a summary of the primary accountabilities and requirements for this position. The company reserves the right to modify or amend accountabilities and requirements at any time at its sole discretion based on business needs. Any part of this job description is subject to possible modification to reasonably accommodate individuals with disabilities.

This position requires use of information or access to hardware which is subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). To perform the position, you must be a U.S. Person as defined by ITAR. ITAR defines a U.S. person as a U.S. Citizen, U.S. Permanent Resident (i.e., ‘Green Card Holder’), Political Asylee, or Refugee.

Visa sponsorship is not available for this role. Only candidates authorized to work in the United States will be considered.

Total compensation for this position is a combination of base plus commission. Base pay is $55,000. A good faith, reasonable estimate of total compensation targeted for this vacant role is $70,000 to $80,000. The actual total compensation offered to candidate may vary from posted hiring range based on geographic location, work experience, education, and/or skill level, licensure, certifications or other business and organizational needs. Please note, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. TTI also offers a comprehensive benefits package including two CDHP plans and a PPO plan for medical/pharmacy, dental, vision, life, disability coverages, and paid parental leave. HSA and FSA offerings are available depending on the type of medical plan selected. Also, TTI offers a Safe Harbor 401(k) Plan with matching contributions and a wide variety of other benefits including a tuition reimbursement plan, vacation, fixed and floating holidays, PTO or sick time, bereavement, jury duty, and an employee assistance plan. A more detailed description of our benefit offerings can be found at: Benefits & Culture | TTI, Inc.

This will be posted for a minimum of 5 days.

What we offer our team members:

  • A great benefits package that includes (but is not limited to) Medical/ Dental/ Vision, 401(k)/Roth plan with matching, and Healthcare Savings Accounts.
  • Educational Assistance (Tuition Reimbursement).
  • Ongoing training throughout your employment with opportunities to participate in professional and personal development programs.
  • A strong focus on giving back to our communities through philanthropic opportunities.

Want to learn more? Visit us at Working at TTI, Inc.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer, and we support protected veterans and individuals with disabilities through our affirmative action program.

title: Curriculum and Materials Development Specialist
location: Cicatelli Associates Inc, New York, NY, US
description:
Reports To: Vice President, Curriculum Development

Employee Status: Full Time, Exempt

Office Location: We strongly prefer candidates who are able to work out of our New York City office location (505 Eighth Avenue, New York, NY 10018). We have a hybrid schedule of working 2 days in the office and 3 days remote. We are also open to candidates based elsewhere in the United States.

GENERAL STATEMENT OF RESPONSIBILITIES:

CAI is seeking a Curriculum and Materials Development Specialist to design innovative, evidence-based curricula, resources, and tools that strengthen health center systems and advance improved patient outcomes across the national Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) and Look-Alike network (Health Centers). This role supports CAI's National Training and Assistance Program (NTAP) for Clinical and Preventive Excellence, funded by the Health Resources and Services Administration, translating clinical and programmatic content into engaging, practice-ready improvement experiences and learning products. Key activities are summarized below.

MAJOR TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES (include, but are not limited to):

  • Bring an innovation mindset to materials development – researching and piloting new formats, tools, and technologies that make CAI's curricula, webinars, and e-learning more engaging, accessible, and effective for health center audiences nationally.
  • Strategically think through course design and take the lead on developing assigned curricula, webinars, and e-learning modules (trainer and participant manuals, playbooks, PowerPoints, storyboards), conducting research and partnering with content experts to become conversant in the subject matter and communicate current evidence and innovative practices effectively.
  • Write curricula, participant manuals, worksheets, and other materials that support learning collaboratives and technical assistance delivery to the national health center network.
  • Ensure all curricula and materials meet CAI's standards of excellence – grounded in adult learning theory and cognitive learning principles, reflecting current instructional design and educational technology best practices, and 508-compliant – through careful, detail-oriented quality assurance review, including of programmed modules.
  • Storyboard e-learning modules (Articulate Rise and/or Storyline), selecting interactive exercises and graphics that strengthen learning and application in real-world health center settings.
  • Partner with the Communications Department, content experts, and other instructional design colleagues at CAI to incorporate feedback and continuously improve curricula and storyboards.
  • Track and communicate shifting trends in curricula, webinars, and e-learning, advising CAI on the adoption of new formats and technologies that advance the quality and reach of its work with health centers.
  • Work with the VP of Curriculum Development to ensure projects are supported strategically by the Curriculum and Distance Learning departments in ways that support CAI's growth, reputation, and impact.
  • Uphold and demonstrate core CAI corporate values.
  • Other duties as necessary/assigned.

MINIMUM EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE AND OTHER SKILLS REQUIRED:

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in education, instructional design, public health, or another health-related field, and/or 4 years of experience in curriculum development, educational communication and technology, adult learning, instructional design, or a related program focused on adult learning and technology.
  • Strong editing and research skills.
  • Experience designing and developing innovative online training, in-person training, or webinars.
  • Knowledge of adult and cognitive learning theories.
  • Experience developing training products for health-related fields (trainer manuals, playbooks, toolkits, PowerPoint slides, storyboards for e-learning modules, live and animated video scripts, etc.).
  • Experience developing live virtual training using the functions of Zoom (e.g., annotate, polling, etc.).
  • Experience developing storyboards that are 508-compliant, to be produced in Lectora.
  • Experience writing scripts for 508-compliant live and animated videos for educational purposes.
  • Strong Microsoft Word and PowerPoint skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work both independently and as part of an interdisciplinary team in a fast-paced environment.
  • Detail-oriented, highly organized, and able to multi-task and manage multiple projects.
  • Familiarity with public health issues and the FQHC/health center landscape.

PREFERRED:

  • Expertise providing quality management support in a public health arena.
  • Project management and coordination experience.
  • Knowledge of training and professional development methodologies.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage complexity and prioritize multiple tasks.
  • Ability to work productively in highly collaborative settings while also functioning independently.
  • Demonstrated ability to interact professionally with culturally diverse staff, clients, and consultants.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

These physical demands are representative of the physical requirements necessary for an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the Curriculum and Materials Development Specialist’s job. Reasonable accommodation can be made to enable people with disabilities to perform the described essential functions of the Curriculum and Materials Development Specialist’s job.

While performing the Curriculum and Materials Development Specialist’s responsibilities, the employee is required to talk and hear. The employee is often required to sit and work at a desk for prolonged periods of time and use their hands and fingers to handle or feel. The employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, reach with arms and hands, climb or balance, and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times. Vision abilities required by this job include close vision.

This job description is intended to convey information essential to understanding the scope of the Curriculum and Materials Development Specialist’s position and it is not intended to be an exhaustive list of skills, efforts, duties, responsibilities or working conditions associated with the position. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

COMPENSATION:

The salary range for this position is $80,000 - $90,000, depending on experience.

CAI offers the following benefits:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Flexible Spending Account
  • Dependent Care Account
  • Transit Reimbursement Account
  • Life insurance - company sponsored up to $50,000
  • Short- and long-term disability insurance
  • Retirement plan after 3 months of employment
  • Semi-monthly payroll (the 15th and last day of each month)
  • Flexible and hybrid work schedules
  • Ability to work fully remotely up to 3 weeks each calendar year
  • Annual vacation and leave benefits:
    • 11 holidays
    • 2 floating holidays
    • 12 sick days
    • 15 vacation days per year for this role, increasing after 4 years of service
    • 1 cancer screening day
    • Bereavement leave
    • Jury duty leave

CAI is an equal employment opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Analyst - Demand Planning
description:
Working at Frontier Airlines

At Frontier, our mission is to Make Every Flight Count. That mission guides how we support our customers, our people and the operation every day.

As a Frontier employee, your work connects to more than a single role. Whether you’re supporting flights, helping customers, maintaining aircraft, leading teams or working behind the scenes, you help create a travel experience that is safe, reliable and built around value.

Our work is guided by our core values: customer first, safety always, operational excellence and one team. These values shape how we make decisions, support each other and deliver for the people who count on us.

Support for work, life and travel

Frontier offers benefits, programs and travel privileges designed to support eligible employees at work and beyond. Availability may vary by role, employment status, eligibility, location, schedule, applicable policies and current plan details.

Depending on role and eligibility, available benefits and programs may include:

  • Medical, dental and vision coverage
  • 401(k) retirement savings options
  • Paid holidays, vacation time and sick time
  • Travel privileges on Frontier Airlines and participating partner airlines, based on current program rules and availability
  • Buddy passes, based on eligibility and program rules
  • Travel-related discounts and employee discounts on select products, services and vendors
  • A hybrid schedule for eligible headquarters roles based in Denver, Colorado
  • Business casual dress options for eligible corporate and support roles
  • Employee support programs and resources, including the HOPE League, Frontier Airlines’ nonprofit organization

About Frontier Airlines

Frontier Airlines is a Denver-based airline serving destinations across the United States and select international markets. Our people support every part of the travel journey, from airport operations and flight crews to aircraft maintenance, customer support, corporate teams and more.

We’re focused on delivering meaningful value by making travel more accessible, practical and easy to personalize for our customers. Across the airline, our teams help support a safe, reliable and efficient operation while continuing to strengthen the experience for the people who choose Frontier.

What Will You Be Doing?

Develop, maintain, and execute forecasting and decision models through a strong combination of analytics, business intelligence, and trend analysis to accurately estimate long and short-range labor, material, tooling, and facility demand.

Essential Functions

  • Develop effective forecast models based on demand trends and patterns.
  • Shape demand to operational and material limitation.
  • Support management with risk assessments and mitigation activities.
  • Provide guidance to demand planning team as needed.
  • Propose and implement solutions to improve demand forecast accuracy.
  • Facilitate & manage monthly planning meetings to collaboratively develop consensus among stakeholder.
  • Communicate forecast and inventory estimations to management.
  • Monitor and report on important changes in forecasts, budgets, and business strategies.
  • Conduct monthly forecast maintenance.
  • Address demand-related issues in a timely and effective manner.
  • Assist other teams within Materials as needed to support the operation
  • Generate and authorize work orders in FMIS/TRAX.
  • Assist in planning and scheduling work to achieve compliance for all EO’s, EA’s and FCD issued by Engineering.
  • Complete review of all long term Other Deferred Maintenance (ODM) items for required manpower, skillset, equipment, parts and tooling.
  • Conduct coordination meetings to review manpower, materials and parts, tooling, equipment, skillset, and span time requirements with necessary departments
  • Perform other duties as assigned by the Manager of Line Maintenance Planning.
  • Establish, coordinate, and monitor Line Maintenance activities on a sliding window basis.
  • Communicate and coordinate efficiently with the following groups: Line Maintenance, Heavy Maintenance, Inspection, Engineering, Materials and Purchasing, Maintenance Control, System Operation Control (SOC) Managers, Aircraft Routers, and Maintenance Programs to ensure the success of maintenance planning Identify and de-peak material demands
  • Establish and optimizes a maintenance task schedule utilizing the TCI/MX Program intervals
  • Establish and optimizes material demands to meet LHT contract

Other Functions

  • Create statistical forecasts:
    • Gather, analyze and validate data
    • Execute statistical modeling
    • Review resulting statistical forecast model
    • Apply error analysis techniques to improve forecasting
    • Summarize/aggregate statistical forecasts
  • All other duties as reasonably requested

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, operations, supply chain or other relevant fields.
    • 4 years of direct demand planning analytic experience may be substituted for a degree
  • Minimum of 2-years experience in a demand planning/forecasting or statistical modeling, or similar experience.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of operations planning, inventory management, and procedures -Strongly preferred

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Proficient in common software - Excel (i.e. formulas, pivot tables, etc.), Tableau, Alteryx, Business Intelligence, or similar analytic software.
  • Strong mathematical and statistical knowledge.
  • Application of data aggregation and visualization.
  • Capability to multitask in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Communicates in a manner that is appropriate for audience; can “read the room” and adjust quickly if necessary, to make the most positive impact
  • Advises team and department with technical aspects, translate complicated technical information to a visual representation that non-technical users can understand
  • Proactive self-starter
  • Ability to handle time sensitive and multi-faceted projects
  • Must demonstrate behavior that portrays the company core values of Safety, Respect, Trust, Collaboration, Value, and Passion while communicating with personnel and acting on behalf of the company at all times
  • Ability to plan, implement and evaluate programs, direct and organize program activities, establish goals and objectives, train, plan and delegate the work of others.
  • Takes a lead role in facilitating discussions and resolving conflicts

Equipment Operated

Standard office equipment: PC Laptop, Printer

Work Environment

Typical office environment, adequately heated and cooled

Physical Effort

Light physical effort required by handling objects up to 20 pounds occasionally and/or up to 10 pounds frequently.

Supervision Received

General Direction: The incumbent normally receives little instruction on day-to-day work and receives general instructions on new assignments.

Salary Range: $72,000 - $96,331 - Please note: this role will close on or before 12/31/26.

Positions Supervised

  • None

Workplace Policies

Disclaimer: The above statements are intended only to describe the general nature and level of work required of the referenced position; they are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of individuals in this position. Please be advised that duties and expectations of this position may be subject to change.

Frontier Airlines, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer and, as such, is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability status, pregnancy, genetic information, citizenship status or any other basis protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

Frontier Airlines is a Zero Tolerance Drug-Free Workplace. All prospective DOT safety-sensitive employees are subject to pre-employment testing for the following drugs and their metabolites: Marijuana, Cocaine, Amphetamines, Opioids and Phencyclidine (PCP). Further, any DOT safety-sensitive job applicant who is found to have tested positive on any required drug or alcohol test at a former employer will be considered ineligible for employment with Frontier.

Colorado Residents: In any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information.

title: Translator
description:
Position Title: Translator

Site Name: Pediatrics

Location: Greenville, TX

Purpose of Position:

The translator works as part of the health center care team and assists the clinical team in the provision of primary health care. They will act as a member of the Care Team and work collaboratively with clinical and non-clinical staff to provide for the health and well-being of the patients. Employee will translate as needed in both the clinical and non- clinical areas, and be cross trained to work in the front offices.

Patient Relationships:

  1. When translating for a patient, the employee will ensure privacy and confidentiality, maintain the dignity of the patient, and ensure the patient understands all communications regarding care.
  2. Answers messages and phone calls efficiently and properly documents.
  3. Will work with front office team to assist with eligibility, registrations and other front office duties as assigned when not translating.
  4. Other duties as assigned.

Employee Relations/Team Support:

  1. Employee will also work as needed in the front office, registering patients in and checking them out, when their visit is complete.
  2. Actively participates in clinic staff meetings and other committees when designated.

Expectations:

  1. All patients will be treated with dignity and compassion.
  2. Employee will assist in providing care to patients without creating additional barriers for them.
  3. Employee will promote a positive attitude.
  4. Employee will maintain a professional atmosphere in the clinic, and promoting this Organization in a positive manner in the community.
  5. Ensure a safe environment of care for patients and staff.
  6. Employee is to be punctual, and aware of excessive absenteeism.
  7. Treat co-workers and patients with respect.
  8. Maintain a clean and organized workplace including exam rooms, office areas, and break room.
  9. Must be a team player with a commitment to the team meetings, as well as policies of this organization.
  10. Employee is expected to adhere to the Organization’s dress code and present to work in a professional manner.
  11. Employee should interact with patients in a patient centered manner to assure patient satisfaction has been provided during their visit.
  12. Will notify Practice Manager immediately when problems or incidents occur in the health center.

Performance Improvement:

Participates in the Organization’s performance improvement activities and performs duties in accordance with applicable standards.

Safety/Infection Control Activities:

Ensures an appropriate environment for the administration of health care by keeping work areas in a clean, safe, and orderly fashion.

Reporting Relationships:

The Translator reports to and is supervised by the Practice Manager.

Evaluation:

The evaluation of work performance will be on-going, and will be carried out by the Practice Manager, and will include the specific duties and responsibilities of this position description plus employee attitudes and general working behavior. Formal evaluation will normally be performed annually, but may be initiated at other times by the Practice Manager.

Qualifications:

  1. Graduated from an accredited high school or hold a GED.
  2. Must work as a care team member to promote quality care and excellence at every patient visit.
  3. Sufficient experience to carry out the duties of this position.
  4. Ability to relate with warmth and effectiveness to the patients and to the providers of the health center.
  5. Must be fluent in both English and Spanish.

Status:

This is FLSA non exempt.

This is an ADA negotiable position.

title: SENIOR JAVA DEVELOPER (HYBRID OR REMOTE)
description:
SENIOR JAVA DEVELOPER (HYBRID OR REMOTE BRAZIL)

Brazilian company hires for hybrid or remote position

Location: Brazil — candidates from any region

Only candidates already based in Brazil will be considered

Work Model: Hybrid for candidates living in state capitals and Remote for candidates living in countryside/cities outside the state capitals

Language Requirements: Advanced English — C1/C2

Seniority: Senior (6+ years)

About The Opportunity

Develop scalable, secure enterprise applications while collaborating with global teams. You will contribute throughout the software development lifecycle, combining strong Java engineering with systems integration and the use of AI to improve development practices.

Main Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain robust, scalable, and secure Java applications.
  • Translate business requirements into clear technical specifications.
  • Apply software engineering best practices, coding standards, and design patterns.
  • Build microservices and integrate systems using web services.
  • Work with relational databases and SQL queries.
  • Conduct code reviews and provide technical support to less experienced developers.
  • Diagnose technical issues and ensure application performance, reliability, and quality.
  • Participate throughout the SDLC, from analysis to deployment.
  • Use AI and emerging technologies to accelerate and improve development practices.

Mandatory Requirements

  • Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field.
  • English proficiency at C1/C2 level for international communication.
  • Extensive Java development experience and a strong background in enterprise applications.
  • Proficiency in Java, Spring, and Hibernate.
  • Experience with REST and SOAP web services.
  • Knowledge of microservices architecture.
  • Experience with relational databases such as Oracle and MySQL, plus solid SQL skills.
  • Experience or knowledge of Artificial Intelligence concepts and/or integrations.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong communication, collaboration, and ability to work in global environments.

Nice to Have

  • Financial services experience, particularly Wealth & Asset Management.
  • Familiarity with GenAI and prompt engineering.
  • Certifications in Java or related technologies.

Ideal Profile

An experienced Java developer who can turn business needs into reliable technical solutions. You combine enterprise development expertise with strong troubleshooting skills, support colleagues through constructive code reviews, and explore how AI can improve software delivery.

Questions for Candidates

  • What experience do you have developing enterprise applications with Java, Spring, and Hibernate?
  • Have you worked with REST/SOAP web services, microservices, and systems integration?
  • Which relational databases have you used, and how have you applied SQL in your projects?
  • What experience or knowledge do you have with AI concepts, integrations, GenAI, or prompt engineering?
  • Can you describe a performance or reliability issue you diagnosed and resolved?
  • Have you conducted code reviews, supported junior developers, and participated from analysis through deployment?
  • Do you have financial services experience, particularly in Wealth & Asset Management, or relevant certifications?
  • Is your English at C1/C2 level, and have you collaborated with global teams?
  • Where in Brazil are you based, and are you available for remote or hybrid work?
  • What are your current compensation, salary expectations, and availability to start?

title: Outreach Worker - 5204
description:
BronxWorks helps individuals and families improve their economic and social well-being. From toddlers to seniors, we feed, shelter, teach, and support our neighbors to build a stronger community. In all aspects of our work, we strive for the highest ethical and performance standards and are guided by the belief that people are to be treated with dignity and respect regardless of their present situation or past experiences.


Across our 60+ locations, we provide programs in a variety of service areas, including workforce development, children, youth, families, seniors and homeless prevention.


The BronxWorks Homeless Outreach Team (HOT) is a mobile unit that works with homeless individuals on the streets, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. Since 1995, we have helped street homeless people obtain appropriate services, move to safer environments, and get placed in permanent or long-term transitional housing. The team is composed of outreach workers, case managers and social workers and also partners with psychiatric and medical providers to connect clients with appropriate care.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Conduct persistent and compassionate outreach as part of a two-person team
  • Engage and build rapport with chronically street homeless individuals in the Bronx
  • Drive agency vehicles for mobile outreach work and to transport clients
  • Support licensed clinicians with mobile medical outreach
  • Maintain familiarity with social services and resources available within the agency and in the community; provide referrals as appropriate
  • Document all interactions with clients
  • Perform additional duties as assigned
  • To support 24/7 hours of operation, this position requires evening and weekend availability

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Candidate must have a valid driver’s license which has been held for at least 1 year; in the last 3 years, candidate must have obtained no more than 3 license violation points
  • Bilingual/multilingual preferred, but not required
  • Proficiency with computers, common office equipment, and basic typing skills
  • Strong interpersonal communication

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Ability to use a computer for prolonged periods
  • Ability to occasionally lift and/or move up to 10 pounds
  • Ability to stand, walk, or sit for long periods of time
  • Ability to bend and retrieve objects and/or documents
  • Ability to travel in the boroughs of New York City and its adjacent counties via public transportation
  • Ability to travel for a minimum of 1 mile within a reasonable amount of time and in all types of weather, including inclement weather, if required to conduct home visits and/or field work
  • TB Test required within the first 120 days of employment



BronxWorks is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive workplace. We consider qualified applicants without regard to any characteristics protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. Reasonable accommodations are available to applicants with disabilities and other legally protected needs. To request an accommodation during the application process, please contact hrbenefits@bronxworks.org

title: Customer Advocate Level I
description:
Position Summary

As a Customer Advocate, you will be supporting communication between MedRisk/SPNet’s network providers and referring adjusters and nurse case managers. You will report to the Customer Advocate Team Lead and/or Supervisor to help strengthen MedRisk/SPNet’s referral process, ensuring efficient workflow, while increasing customer satisfaction. Acting as liaison, the Customer Advocate tracks patient progress from the start of treatment, throughout treatment, and through to closure by obtaining relevant case updates from providers, including but not limited to dates of service, compliance, treatment notes, and continued authorization. They are responsible for maintaining the integrity of the case file and related documents and communicating professionally and effectively with the customer.

Primary Duties & Responsibilities

Level I:

  • Manage claims and monitor case status by confirming patient attendance with network providers, and addressing any concerns regarding compliance
  • Properly update all case related data to MedRisk’s database/platform
  • Track and relay authorization to our providers as directed by the clients with confirmations to the adjuster and NCM
  • Be knowledgeable regarding the client’s unique needs and respond appropriately
  • Build approachable, professional relationships with providers and referring customers.
  • Compliance with HIPAA and URAC guidelines
  • Employee is expected to work a minimum of 48 tasks daily

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree preferred; impeccable customer service skills with 2-3 years of experience preferred
  • Healthcare experience required; minimum of 1 year preferred
  • Experience working with a US company (PH specific)
  • Ability to work independently and multi task in a fast paced environment
  • Detail oriented
  • Excellent verbal & written communication skills
  • Basic knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook and Teams
  • Computer skills in Windows environment
  • Time management and strong organizational skills
  • Adaptability
  • Ability to receive constructive feedback
  • Strong work ethic
  • Competencies(choose at least 4)
  • Customer Focus
  • Comprehensive Computer Skills
  • Listening
  • Informing
  • Action Oriented
  • Ethics and Values
  • Priority Setting
  • Integrity and Trust

Working Conditions & Physical Requirements

title: Health Counselor
description:
The Community Service Society (CSS) is an independent, not-for-profit organization that has been at the forefront of public policy innovations that support low-income New Yorkers for more than 170 years. CSS’s Health Initiatives Department runs several statewide programs that help New Yorkers find and use their health insurance or otherwise access health care. In October 2018, CSS launched New York State’s first ombudsman program targeting the needs of people with mental illness and/or substance use disorder, Community Health Access to Addiction and Mental Healthcare Project (CHAMP). CHAMP operates statewide through a toll-free live-answer helpline and in partnership with eight community-based organizations and three specialist organizations. The goal of CHAMP is to help people with substance use and mental health care needs navigate and secure benefits through their insurance plans.


The CHAMP Helpline fields calls from people who need help getting and using health insurance coverage for substance use disorder and mental health care, serving not only those in need of care but also their family members, care providers, and other advocates. CSS seeks to hire a Health Counselor who will provide high-quality consumer assistance through the CHAMP Helpline to clients with mental health conditions or substance use disorder, their family members, and health care providers, helping them navigate the difficulties they may face in accessing care.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Respond to live calls from consumers, family members and providers on the CHAMP Helpline, including during extended Helpline hours (until 7pm) approximately once per week.
  • Assist with filing grievances, complaints, appeals, and provide hearing and/or appeal assistance to consumers contesting denials of health insurance coverage.
  • Assist consumers with filing grievances, complaints, appeals contesting denials of health insurance coverage.
  • Assist with document collection and evaluation for prior authorization requests, peer-to-peer reviews, and appeals.
  • Provide information, education, advice, and navigational services to consumers on how to successfully use health insurance and/or access care.
  • Maintain thorough case records of services provided, advice, appeals, and/or referrals.
  • Help identify systemic trends or practices that adversely affect consumers and work closely with senior CSS staff and other appropriate stakeholders.


Job Requirements:

  • Graduate degree in social work, health policy, public health, biology, or other relevant discipline preferred.
  • A minimum of one year's experience providing assistance to consumers and/or advocates on health insurance or health care access issues preferred; experience working with people with substance use disorders and/or mental health conditions strongly preferred.
  • Outstanding research, writing, and oral advocacy skills required, including excellent reading comprehension, organized thought, and the ability to speak, type, and write clearly, concisely, and persuasively; keeping detailed notes of all communications required.
  • Outstanding organizational skills and attention to detail required.
  • Excellent oral communication skills, including a genuine enjoyment of talking with people on the phone and the ability to project patience, competence, and care for others' concerns through both oral and written communication.
  • Customer service and written advocacy experience preferred.
  • Mission driven.
  • Written and spoken fluency in Spanish preferred.
  • Competency with Office Suite and Salesforce, along with research and data-based management skills, preferred.


Compensation: This position is represented by local 1199 SEIU with an annual salary of $85,395.00 including comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage provided by 1199. Community Service Society provides an employee benefit package including 403b retirement savings plan, defined benefit retirement plan, commuter benefit plan, EAP, and more in addition to a robust paid time off policy.


Additional details: Must be authorized to work in the United States.


Physical Requirements: Office work that requires sitting, use of a computer, answering phone calls, participating in virtual meetings, and other standard office functions.


CSS currently offers a hybrid work environment requiring on-site work at CSS’ office at least two days per week and three days per week of remote work. CSS will provide all equipment necessary to perform the job from home, but the employee must have their own wired internet connection.

title: Tandplejer søges til Tandlægehuset Køge
description:
Vores meget afholdte tandplejer flytter fra byen, og vi søger derfor en ny kollega til vores klinik i Køge centrum.

Vi søger dig, der:

  • har erfaring med almindelige tandplejeropgaver og lyst til nye udfordringer
  • kan lave overslag og behandlingsplaner – eller gerne vil lære det
  • har lyst til at lære at scanne, lave plast og bedøve, hvis du ikke allerede kan
  • er smilende og serviceminded og møder patienterne i øjenhøjde

Vi tilbyder:

  • 30–35 timer fordelt på fire dage. Har du brug for noget andet, er vi fleksible, så søg alligevel
  • Fleksible arbejdsrammer med gode muligheder for at få fri og holde ferie, når du ønsker det
  • Løn efter kvalifikationer og sundhedsforsikring
  • Efteruddannelse, kurser og faglig sparring

Hvem er vi?

Tandlægehuset Køge er en moderne klinik med fokus på høj faglighed, god patientkontakt og et godt arbejdsmiljø. Vi er 5 tandplejere, 4 tandlæger og 8 klinikassistenter. Omgangstonen er uformel, der er højt til loftet og kort vej til ledelsen. Vi spiser frokost sammen hver dag og
mødes også til sociale arrangementer, sommerfest og julefrokost.

Som tandplejer deltager du i personale-, tandplejer- og behandlermøder, så der er god mulighed for at sparre med dine kolleger. Du får også mulighed for at udvikle dig fagligt gennem kurser.
Klinikken har nye units med røntgen og intraoralt kamera samt Trios-scanner, OP og CBCT. Vi tilbyder lupbriller, fordi godt lys og forstørrelse hjælper os med at opnå de resultater, vi ønsker.
Snart indfører vi også AI som second opinion ved røntgendiagnostik.

title: Senior Data Analyst BSD City, Indonesia Regular Engineering & IT 2026.07.17
description:
Join Traveloka and channel your passion into a rewarding career

About Traveloka Traveloka is Southeast Asia’s leading all-in-one travel platform connecting millions globally with trusted, world-class experiences. With over 140 million app downloads and more than 40 million monthly active users, Traveloka stands as one of the most popular travel apps in the region.

Job Description

Job ID: MJ000257

About Traveloka

Traveloka is Southeast Asia's leading travel and lifestyle super-app. We connect tens of millions of travellers across the region with flights, hotels, experiences, financial services, and more — all from a single platform. Since our founding in 2012, we have expanded to eleven markets, processed billions of dollars in transactions, and built one of the most recognised consumer brands in the region.

We move fast because the region demands it. Southeast Asia is young, mobile-first, and growing faster than almost anywhere else on earth. We are not transplanting a Western playbook — we are writing a new one, from scratch, for a market that does not look like anywhere else — and we are calling for people who want to be part of that.

About the Team

The Travel Activities team builds the part of the trip people actually remember — attraction tickets, guided tours, cruises, and local experiences across Southeast Asia and beyond. Data is how we make sense of it. Each product category has its own funnel and the supply landscape is fragmented, so the numbers are never clean and the answers are never obvious. That is exactly where you come in.

As part of the data analytics team, you turn millions of bookings, searches, and partner feeds into decisions our commercial and product teams act on the same week. You design the metrics, build the dashboards people actually trust, and dig into why a category is moving — not just that it is. We are deploying AI to scale this faster. If you want your analysis to change what gets sold to real travelers, this is the place.

About the Job

As a Senior Data Analyst on Traveloka’s Travel Activities team, you are an expert individual contributor — no direct reports — who independently owns the toughest, most ambiguous analytics problems in your area, accountable for the analytical decisions you make and increasingly setting the standard others follow.

  • Own the analytics agenda for the Travel Activities business area, deciding which questions are worth answering and being accountable for the recommendations that follow.
  • Lead complex, custom analyses — causal inference, advanced segmentation, funnel optimisation — on problems that span your own and adjacent job areas and that senior leaders use to set direction.
  • Improve how experimentation is done for your area as part of project teams, raising the rigour bar on how hypotheses are framed and results are read.
  • Build the foundational dashboards, metric definitions, and pipelines that other analysts and business teams depend on, applying deep, well‑developed expertise built from theory and experience.
  • Persuade and convince senior stakeholders — GMs, Directors, VPs — of your reading of the evidence, even where the final decision rests with them.
  • Mentor and guide junior analysts and review their work to lift quality, without taking on line-management of a team.

title: Sr. Staff Product Engineer
description:
About SiTime


SiTime is the Precision Timing company.


Timing is the heartbeat of all electronics, ensuring performance, resilience and scalability. For decades, quartz devices, non-silicon technology, have kept systems in sync, but they struggle in harsher, more demanding environments. MEMS-based Precision Timing delivers greater accuracy, smaller size and resilience. Today, MEMS timing powers over 400 applications, including high-growth ones in AI datacenters, automated driving, industrial and humanoid robots, wearables and IoT.


Our semiconductor MEMS programmable solutions offer a rich feature set that enables customers to differentiate their products with higher performance, smaller size, lower power, and better reliability. With more than 4 billion devices shipped, SiTime is changing the timing industry. For more information, visit: www.sitime.com.


Job Summary

Timing Products Division (TPD) is seeking a Senior Staff Product Engineer to lead the development and production ramp of state-of-the-art mixed-signal timing products. This is a unique opportunity to provide end-to-end product engineering leadership, from product conception and NPI through qualification, production release, yield improvement, and end-of-life.

The Senior Staff Product Engineer will work closely with cross-functional teams including Design, Test, Quality, Operations, Applications, and external suppliers to ensure products meet datasheet specifications, customer requirements, and applicable JEDEC/AEC quality standards. The role will also lead test strategy, product qualification, BOM management, yield optimization, and resolution of supplier and customer excursions.


Responsibilities

  • Provide end-to-end product engineering ownership from product concept through end-of-life, with a focus on delivering high-quality products to customers.
  • Lead the definition and execution of ATE test, product qualification, and manufacturing strategies.
  • Drive new product introduction (NPI) and product release into manufacturing while ensuring compliance with stringent Tier 1 customer requirements.
  • Develop and maintain datasheets, automotive compliance documentation, and product-related technical reports.
  • Own product Bill of Materials (BOM) release and maintenance throughout the product lifecycle.
  • Lead supplier and customer excursion management, including root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and cross-functional resolution.
  • Drive yield improvement through statistical analysis, data mining, root-cause investigation, and implementation of corrective actions.
  • Monitor key product and manufacturing metrics, generate regular yield/performance reports, and communicate findings and improvement plans to product engineering teams and leadership.
  • Drive achievement of product engineering KPIs, including NPI execution and velocity, gross margin improvement, product quality, and failure-analysis cycle time.
  • Optimize PAT, SYL, SBL, SPC limits, and disposition strategies to protect product quality while minimizing unnecessary manufacturing waste.
  • Partner with design and test engineering teams to optimize product test coverage, DFT, manufacturability, and production robustness.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to product engineering team members and influence cross-functional technical decisions.

Qualifications & Requirements


Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in semiconductor product engineering.
  • Strong understanding of analog and mixed-signal circuits, common circuit building blocks, semiconductor device physics, test methodologies, and Design-for-Test (DFT) concepts.
  • Strong analog circuit background is required; experience with semiconductor timing products such as PLLs and clock generators is highly desirable.
  • Experience with ATE tester platforms such as Teradyne J750 or Advantest 93K.
  • Experience developing and executing semiconductor product test plans and manufacturing test strategies.
  • Experience developing qualification hardware and/or software.
  • Experience with common laboratory test equipment, including oscilloscopes, multimeters, DC power supplies, and related instrumentation.
  • Experience with product qualification and familiarity with JEDEC and AEC qualification standards and stress-test conditions.
  • Experience with yield management and statistical analysis tools such as PDF Exensio and JMP.
  • Demonstrated ability to use statistical analysis and data-driven methods to identify root causes and drive yield improvement.
  • Demonstrated experience managing supplier excursions and customer escalations through structured problem solving and cross-functional collaboration.
  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or a related field required; Master's or Ph.D. preferred.
  • English proficiency is required, including the ability to effectively communicate, collaborate, and perform job responsibilities in a professional business environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with mixed-signal timing products, including PLLs, clock generators, or related devices.
  • Bench characterization experience for analog and mixed-signal semiconductor products.
  • Experience with automotive semiconductor products and customer-specific quality requirements.
  • Experience with PAT, SYL, SBL, SPC, and statistical disposition optimization.

Desired Characteristics & Attributes

  • Strong verbal, written, and technical communication skills.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership and ability to influence cross-functional teams.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a data-driven approach.
  • Ability to work effectively with Design, Test, Quality, Operations, suppliers, and customers.
  • Strong ownership and accountability for product quality and execution.
  • Collaborative team player who thrives in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
  • Ability to mentor and develop less-experienced product engineers.


Compensation Range:


At SiTime, we believe great work deserves great rewards. We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive compensation package designed to attract top talent.


The annual base salary range for this role is $135,000 – $165,000. The final offer is determined by factors such as location, experience, education, and training.


In addition to base salary, this role is eligible for a quarterly bonus tied to the achievement of innovation goals—reflecting our commitment to recognizing meaningful impact. We also offer equity grants, providing a meaningful opportunity to share in the company’s future growth and success.


Benefits offered: 401k plan, health and wellness that includes medical, dental, vision, life, parental leave, legal services, and time off plans.

We treat each person fairly and we do not tolerate discrimination or harassment against anyone on the basis of any protected characteristics, including race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, pregnancy, political affiliation, protected veteran status, protected genetic information, or marital status or other characteristics protected by law. title: Strategic Analysis & International Operations - Paid Internship
description:
Strategic Analysis & International Operations Intern


Employment type: Paid, part-time internship (temporary)

Term: Spring 2027: academic semester; exact dates to be confirmed

Commitment: 10-20 hours per week

Work arrangement: Primarily remote, with scheduled coordination across international time zones

Pay: $22/hr.

Role Overview:

This paid internship gives a current undergraduate direct exposure to the research, analysis, coordination, and problem-solving that support international security and government-services operations. Each intern will be paired one-on-one with a senior business leader responsible for a geographic portfolio, client relationship, operational program, or cross-business priority. The role is designed to provide meaningful ownership rather than observation alone. The intern will manage defined workstreams, produce professional-quality outputs, and receive regular direction, mentorship, and feedback. Assignments will be tailored to business needs, the leader's portfolio, and the intern's interests and capabilities.

Key Responsibilities

Business Leader & Portfolio Support:

  • Work directly with the assigned business leader to research priority questions, prepare for meetings, capture actions, and follow through on agreed workstreams.
  • Maintain concise trackers, briefing notes, decision logs, contact research, and other portfolio-management tools.
  • Consolidate information from operations, risk, commercial, and other internal stakeholders into clear, usable outputs.
  • Coordinate with in-country or functional colleagues, when appropriate, to gather information and support defined projects.

Research & Strategic Analysis:

  • Conduct open-source research on countries, clients, sectors, competitors, partners, regulations, political developments, and operating environments.
  • Assess source quality, distinguish confirmed information from unverified reporting, and document sources so findings can be checked and reused.
  • Turn complex information into concise executive summaries, briefing notes, slide content, issue papers, and short outlooks.
  • Identify emerging developments, patterns, risks, and opportunities that may affect a portfolio or client program.

Operational, Risk & Commercial Support:

  • Support country and operational monitoring, incident logging, emerging-risk tracking, mapping, and recurring risk or management reporting where relevant to the placement.
  • Analyze public procurement material, client requirements, market developments, and competitor or partner information.
  • Contribute background research, compliance notes, capability content, and other inputs for proposals, presentations, and client discussions.
  • Maintain high accuracy, version control, and appropriate handling of commercially sensitive or operational information.

AI-Enabled Improvement & Data Support:

  • Support approved AI initiatives for research synthesis, reporting, knowledge management, tender analysis, and business-process improvement.
  • Identify repetitive workflows that may be improved through automation; help test prototypes, document processes, and measure practical value.
  • Validate AI-assisted outputs through human review, source checking, and quality control before information is used or shared.
  • Maintain structured information in tools such as Microsoft Excel, SharePoint, Power BI, mapping platforms, or other approved systems, depending on the assignment.

Learning & Development Outcomes:

  • Receive direct mentorship and practical feedback from an experienced international business leader.
  • Build an understanding of how security, risk, government-services, and commercial teams support operations in complex and high-risk environments.
  • Strengthen open-source research, analytical judgment, professional writing, data management, and executive-briefing skills.
  • Gain hands-on experience applying AI responsibly to real business workflows and evaluating the quality of AI-assisted work.
  • Develop cross-cultural communication, remote collaboration, time management, discretion, and accountability across an international organization.
  • Complete defined deliverables that can support an academic or professional portfolio, subject to confidentiality restrictions.


Candidate Profile

Required:

  • Current undergraduate student in good academic standing during the Fall 2026 semester.
  • Strong interest in international business, government services, security, geopolitical affairs, risk, operations, data, or applied AI.
  • Ability to commit 10-20 hours per week and manage assignments reliably alongside academic responsibilities.
  • Strong research, critical-thinking, and written communication skills, with the ability to present high-impact information first and write in concise U.S. English.
  • High attention to detail, sound judgment, intellectual curiosity, and willingness to ask questions when requirements or sources are unclear.
  • Working proficiency in Microsoft Office and the ability to learn new analytical, collaboration, or data tools quickly.
  • Professionalism, discretion, and ability to handle confidential or commercially sensitive information on a need-to-know basis.
  • Ability to satisfy the work-authorization and employment requirements applicable to the final work location and employing entity.

Preferred:

  • Coursework in international affairs, security policy, political science, economics, business, data science, computer science, geography, communications, or a related field.
  • Experience with open-source research, country or market analysis, data visualization, mapping, Power BI, advanced Excel, AI tools, or workflow automation.
  • International, cross-cultural, government, military, nonprofit, consulting, or business experience through work, study, volunteering, or student activities.
  • Foreign-language capability relevant to the portfolio, including Arabic, French, Ukrainian, Somali, Bahasa Indonesia, or another regional language.
  • Prior professional security experience is not required.

Working Arrangements & Professional Expectations:

  • The internship is expected to run during the Spring 2027 academic semester, with an anticipated commitment of 10-20 hours per week. The precise duration, schedule, and hourly compensation will be confirmed through the formal offer process.
  • Work will be planned around the intern's academic schedule. Because GWFS operates internationally, occasional scheduled calls may fall outside standard U.S. business hours; all such time will count toward the intern's paid weekly hours. This is not an on-call position.
  • The role is expected to be primarily remote. Travel is not required unless separately discussed, approved, and arranged in accordance with Company policy.
  • All work must be completed using authorized systems and in accordance with Company policies on confidentiality, information security, data protection, AI use, and professional conduct. Sensitive information must not be entered into unapproved tools or shared outside authorized channels.


Accountability:

The intern is accountable to the assigned GWFS business leader for the quality, timeliness, accuracy, and professional handling of assigned work. The placement will include regular one-on-one check-ins, a defined learning and work plan, and an end-of-semester performance review or university evaluation where required.

Assistant Coordinator, Brenau Doctoral Internship/Assistant Director Ivester House; Director of Psychotherapy Training, NGMC

Position Summary:

This faculty member will have a joint appointment with Brenau and North Georgia Medical Center, with 18.75 hours per week at each site. For Brenau, this faculty member will serve as the Assistant Coordinator for the Brenau Doctoral Internship housed in Gainesville, GA.

NGMC: The Director of Psychotherapy Training provides essential leadership and oversight of the psychiatry residency’s psychotherapy curriculum, ensuring compliance with ACGME requirements, maintaining high-quality education, and supporting resident clinical competence in the three ACGME core psychotherapy modalities (CBT, psychodynamic, and supportive/humanistic). This role ensures adherence to ACGME psychotherapy training standards, enhances resident competence and preparedness for independent practice, supports program reputation, resident satisfaction, and faculty development, and provides continuity and leadership in core educational initiatives critical to residency success.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • PhD/PsyD in Clinical or Counseling Psychology or a related field
  • Licensed as Psychologist in Georgia
  • Preferred three years of clinical practice, including in psychological assessments
  • Two years of experience in providing clinical supervision

Job Duties & Responsibilities:

Assistant Doctoral Internship Coordinator & Assistant Director Ivester House Clinic – Assist the Doctoral Internship Coordinator/Ivester House Clinic Director in running the internship and the clinic, including in the following areas:

  • Assist with planning and organizing the doctoral psychology internship run out of the Ivester House location of the Brenau Center for Counseling and Psychological Services.
  • Assist in recruitment and selection process for interns
  • Maintain awareness of internship requirements and communicate the requirements to all agencies involved in the internship; assist with ensuring compliance with training and APA/APPIC accreditation standards.
  • Maintain communication and contracts/MOUs with partner agencies, contribute to the evaluation of progress of interns.
  • Assist with planning and managing intern rotations across sites and verify qualifications of site supervisors; ensure that interns receive a high-quality and comprehensive training experience.
  • Provide clinical supervision to interns for their clinical work at the Ivester House and partner sites, including supervision of psychological assessments and clinical documentation.
  • Plan and manage required didactic training, including scheduling didactic trainers from partner sites.
  • Assist with managing program evaluation of internship collaborative
  • Provide clinical teaching through individual supervision of graduate students placed at the Ivester House who are seeing therapy and assessment clients.
  • Assist in hiring clinic staff including clinic coordinators
  • Assist with orienting and training doctoral interns, graduate student counselors, and clinic coordinators at Ivester House
  • Serve as on-call clinical supervisor as needed.
  • Provide limited clinical services at the Ivester House clinic (approximately 5 clients per week, which could include psychological assessment clients)
  • Possible supervision of dissertation research/chairing dissertation committees
  • Other duties as assigned

NGMC duties:

  • Curriculum Oversight & Development (7.75 hours per week): Oversees Wednesday didactics and attends all Wednesdays to help with coordination across speakers. Also oversees the following recurring yearly seminars (6 lectures each): introductory psychodynamic therapy (PDT101/201), advanced psychodynamic therapy (PDT301/401), CBT101/201, DBT301/401, and ACT301/401. Additionally, leads a monthly ethics/professionalism series (ETH101-401), a monthly psychotherapy case conference series (PCC101-401), and oversees monthly simulation afternoons (SIM101-401). Also assists in identifying external speakers for the monthly department grand rounds series, and gives at least two faculty development lectures each year.
  • Clinical Supervision & Mentorship (6 hours per week): Screens all resident clinic psychotherapy referrals and triages cases to ensure full resident caseloads. Supervises PGY3&4 psychotherapy clinics and notes, oversees three weekly supervision groups (including leading one on CBT themselves), and coordinates finding weekly individual resident supervisors. Additionally, manages the residency’s four monthly process/T/Balint groups for all classes (including leading one themselves) and the formal mentorship program which pairs all residents with faculty and senior resident mentors. Directly mentors at least two residents.
  • Program Administration & Compliance (2.5 hours per week): Participates in weekly leadership meetings (Wednesdays from 11-12 PM), serves on the Clinical Competency Committee and Program Evaluation Committee, advises on all quality improvement initiatives within the residency, and represents faculty on the Resident Committee on Community. Engages in ongoing scholarly activity and professional development to model and promote excellence in psychotherapy training.
  • Recruitment & Professional Representation (2.5 hours per week): Supports residency recruitment through application review, interviews, and recruitment fairs; attends national conferences to maintain expertise (including maintaining an active membership in AADPRT), represent the program, and implement best practices in psychotherapy education. Recruits and coordinates adjunct faculty members involved in psychotherapy training.

Supervisory Responsibilities:
Supervision of clinical work of Doctoral Psychology Interns as well as other graduate students providing services at the Ivester House at Brenau is required as well as supervisor of Psychiatry Residents at NGMC.

37.5 hours per week. Monday – Friday with some day and some evening hours to cover IH evening hours. Occasional weekend recruitment activities. Hours may be adjusted to meet the needs of the department.

12 months, continuous

Mostly Sedentary work. Work is performed in an office environment and requires the ability to operate standard office equipment related to teaching. Prolonged periods sitting and standing. worker is required to have close visual acuity to grade papers, viewing a computer terminal; extensive reading. Must have the ability to travel short distances, and/or drive a vehicle to deliver and pick up materials. Exerting up to 15 pounds of force to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects. This is your opportunity to get on the rocket ship and join a company that is building a cutting-edge enterprise network and secure cloud platform, and is on a fast track to becoming the worldwide market leader – don’t miss it!

Cato Networks is building Product-Led Growth capabilities that complement its established enterprise, direct-sales, and partner-led business.

We are looking for a hands-on Product Manager to own product-led customer journeys across Cato’s target markets, with a particular focus on SMB while also improving how larger enterprise customers discover, evaluate, activate, adopt, and expand Cato.

For SMB customers, this may include highly self-service journeys—from signup and onboarding through value realization, purchase, and expansion. For larger enterprises, PLG will complement the sales-led motion by helping customers experience value sooner, adopt more effectively, identify expansion opportunities, and create stronger product-qualified demand.

What You’ll Do

  • Own and improve the end-to-end PLG journey across relevant customer segments: discover → evaluate → activate → experience value → adopt → convert → retain → expand.
  • Define segment-specific product-led journeys for SMB and enterprise customers, balancing self-service, sales-assisted, and partner-assisted experiences.
  • For SMB, drive simple self-service onboarding, guided configuration, sensible defaults, in-product education, packaging, upgrade paths, and purchase experiences.
  • For enterprise customers, identify ways to accelerate evaluation, activation, time-to-value, adoption, product-qualified demand, and expansion.
  • Define the key activation and “aha” moments for different customer segments, and improve time-to-first-value and unassisted or assisted activation.
  • Own product requirements related to trials, free experiences where relevant, packaging, entitlements, upgrade paths, pricing UX, purchase flows, and conversion triggers.
  • Define, instrument, and monitor PLG metrics, including activation, time-to-first-value, product adoption, conversion, product-qualified opportunities, retention, and expansion.
  • Use product analytics, customer research, funnel analysis, and experimentation to identify friction, test hypotheses, and continuously improve outcomes.
  • Partner with Sales, Marketing, Channel, Customer Success, Finance, and Business Operations to create seamless product-led, sales-assisted, and partner-assisted journeys.
  • Identify product-usage and behavioral signals that can trigger contextual recommendations, expansion opportunities, partner engagement, or sales outreach.

What You Bring

  • Deep understanding of Product-Led Growth, including SaaS metrics, freemium and trial models, and PLG-driven customer journeys.
  • Strong experience defining and delivering user-facing product experiences, with a solid understanding of UI/UX principles.

New York Edge is seeking passionate and enthusiastic people to fill the role of Step Specialist. Step Specialists (Stepping or step-dancing) should have knowledge and experience in this form of percussive dance. They must be able to produce complex rhythms and sounds through a mixture of footsteps, spoken words, and hand claps. The Step Specialist should have experience teaching or performing in groups of three or more, often in arrangements resembling military formations. Additional knowledge in gymnastics, break dance, tap dance, marching, African and Caribbean dance, or stunts are preferred- but not required. Step Specialists should have good speed when stepping and experience using props such as canes, rhythm sticks, and blindfolds. Specialists should teach basic dance principles and go beyond through the act of demonstration. Students will follow, and the step specialist will challenge students to use their creative thinking in art. Exploring creativity is part of stepping. Step Specialists will utilize and adapt the New York State Arts Learning Standards and the New York Edge curriculum to create engaging activities encouraging participation in New York Edge programs.


ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

  • Establish and enforce rules for behavior and procedures for maintaining order among the students for whom they are responsible.

  • Have the ability to understand and carry out instructions.

  • Organize performance groups and direct their rehearsals.

  • Progressive development of student skills leading to a final project

  • Prior experience teaching and instructing youth preferred

  • May be required to walk up and down stairs.

  • Work is performed mostly within a New York City Public School but may be required to interact with the community at-large during trips or events.



QUALIFICATIONS

  • High School Diploma or Equivalent required; some college preferred

  • A minimum of one year of work-related skill, knowledge, or experience is required.

  • A minimum of one year of teaching experience is required.

  • Must have passion for New York Edge's mission and demonstrated interest in education and youth development.

  • Candidates qualified to lead instruction in more than one activity are also preferred.


WORK SCHEDULE

  • 9-15 hours per week.

  • Monday through Friday -- 2:30 pm - 5:30 pm



The Step Specialist will be required to report to the school building and interact with staff, students, parents, and school administration.

At the time of offer and acceptance, the job requires safety and security clearances through the Department of Education and Department of Health.
