title: Director, Senior Litigation and Regulatory Counsel
description:
About Hamilton Beach

Hamilton Beach Brands is a leading designer, marketer, and distributor of innovative household and commercial appliances trusted by consumers around the world. Founded in 1910 and headquartered in Glen Allen, Virginia, we develop and market a broad portfolio of products under well-known brands including Hamilton Beach®, Weston®, Lotus®, and Hamilton Beach Professional®.

For more than a century, our products have helped simplify everyday life – from preparing meals and beverages at home to supporting foodservice professionals in restaurants, hotels, and commercial kitchens.

Our culture is guided by a shared set of values that shape how we work and make decisions every day: Customer Obsession, People, Good Thinking, Ethics, Passion for Quality, Embrace Change, Teamwork, and commitment to Our Environment and Community.

At Hamilton Beach Brands, we look for people who are collaborative, curious, and motivated to make meaningful impact.


About the Role:

Hamilton Beach Brands is seeking a Director, Senior Litigation & Regulatory Counsel at our Corporate Headquarters located in Glen Allen, VA. This position will report to the Sr. Vice President, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary will manage the Company’s global litigation and claims docket, lead its product safety and regulatory compliance work, advise the business on employment matters, and serve as a senior legal leader and trusted advisor to senior leadership, helping balance legal risk with business objectives. This role is focused primarily on litigation, claims, product safety and regulatory compliance, and also helps lead employment, labor and supply chain compliance matters across the Company’s operations in the United States, Canada, Mexico and Asia, with opportunities to participate in the strategic operations of the Company across all departments in a support capacity. The Senior Counsel will also assist the General Counsel with internal investigations and compliance matters, directly supervise the Legal Affairs and Compliance Administrator, and actively contribute to other Law Department initiatives and projects.

Because its small appliances reach consumers through major retailers and e-commerce channels and its commercial products are used in restaurants, chains, bars and hotels, the Company manages a broad range of product liability, consumer, commercial and employment claims, disputes and regulatory issues, and operates under the oversight of product safety and consumer protection regulators in the United States, Canada and Mexico. The ideal candidate is comfortable confronting novel legal issues in a fast-moving environment, keeps pace with an active claims docket, has the curiosity to dig into product engineering and evolving regulation, and has the initiative to build out and run the Company’s litigation and claims management function with limited supervision.

Salary Range: $160,000.00 To $210,000.00 Annually

What You Will Do:

Litigation and Claims Management

  • Manage the Company’s product liability, commercial, employment and other litigation, claims and dispute-resolution activities before courts, arbitral bodies and government agencies. Responsibilities include: evaluating pre-litigation demands and threatened claims; developing case strategy; selecting and managing outside counsel; overseeing factual development, discovery, briefing, hearings, trials and appeals; managing budgets and external legal expense; guiding settlement negotiations and mediations; and reporting regularly to the General Counsel on significant developments, reserves, and legal, financial, operational and reputational exposure.
  • Lead the Law Department’s processes and systems for litigation and claims management, including intake and tracking, litigation holds and evidence preservation, settlement authority, reserves reporting and outside counsel guidelines. Directly supervise the Legal Affairs and Compliance Administrator, who supports these responsibilities.
  • Defend product liability litigation and claims brought directly by consumers and other claimants or by their insurers through subrogation, including personal injury, wrongful death, property damage and alleged violations of state consumer protection laws. Manage state attorney general inquiries, Better Business Bureau complaints, escalated consumer complaints and product inquiries from major retailers.
  • Manage the tender, reporting and resolution of insurance claims under the Company’s commercial general liability, product liability, marine cargo, property, automobile, employment practices and executive risk programs, with day-to-day support from the Legal Affairs and Compliance Administrator.
  • Communicate with senior leadership and business leaders about ongoing litigation, pending claims and threatened claims. Identify trends across claims, incidents and regulatory matters and report them to the quality engineering team and the business. Provide counsel on crisis management and crisis communications.

Product Safety, Regulatory & Supply Chain Compliance

  • Oversee compliance with consumer product safety and consumer protection laws and regulations, including those administered by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC), Health Canada, Mexico’s PROFECO and similar governmental authorities.
  • Manage regulatory inquiries, required reports and corrective actions, including CPSC Section 15(b) Full Reports, Health Canada mandatory incident reports and recalls, in partnership with the quality engineering team.
  • Support the General Counsel and outside regulatory counsel on U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) matters affecting the Company’s connected medical device business (Hamilton Beach Health and HealthBeacon), including registration and listing, quality management system and medical device reporting requirements, and FDA inspections.
  • Participate in the Company’s Safety Committee and advise during the Product Design Review process, including on product warranties, use and care guides, labeling, warnings and instructions.
  • Provide legal leadership on compliance with chemical, material and supply chain requirements affecting the Company’s products and packaging, including PFAS restrictions and disclosure laws, California Proposition 65, forced labor import prohibitions, including the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA), conflict minerals reporting under Section 1502 of the Dodd-Frank Act, and similar federal, state and foreign requirements. Work closely with Engineering & Quality and Supply Chain Operations teams on due diligence, certifications and related disclosures. Advise on supplier adherence to the Company’s supplier code of conduct and its social compliance, product safety and quality requirements, including supplier audits, corrective action plans and the enforcement of warranty, indemnity and other contractual rights for defective or noncompliant products.
  • Support Trade Compliance and the business on customs, import and related regulatory issues, including U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and FDA detentions, exclusion actions, penalty proceedings, prior disclosures, protests and comparable matters involving foreign authorities, coordinating with outside counsel as needed.

title: SENIOR ENGINEER - SYSTEM PROTECTION
description:
Position Summary Description

Performs transmission and generation design and settings, including managing diverse work assignments requiring highly developed professional judgment and knowledge of transmission and generation protection systems. Essential Functions

  • Designs complex transmission and generation protection schemes to insure BES integrity

  • Prepares, reviews and verifies system protection design and settings, transmission protection schematics and relay elementary diagrams, and relay test plans for new transmission protection systems
  • Serves as subject matter expert for assigned NERC standards
  • Reviews and approves staff and consultant designs and calculations for Seminole protection schemes to assure proper system operation
  • Reviews inventory for relay protection components for facility ratings purposes
  • Analyzes all system disturbances for Seminole and all member delivery points to ascertain cause/effect and remedial action if necessary
  • Develops system protection portion of substation operating instructions and assists System Operations with the development of restoration procedures for unscheduled outages
  • Represents Seminole on applicable SERC and FRCC technical committees relating to protection and control
  • Keeps abreast of new technologies and advancements, as well as participates at some level with outside organizations such as IEEE or NERC standard drafting teams
  • Performs other duties as applicable to the position or as assigned


  • NERC Compliance: Performs NERC Compliance Program roles if/as designated in Seminole's Standard Ownership Matrix (SOM) including ongoing evidence retention in "audit-ready" form. You should also be familiar with Seminole's Enterprise Internal Compliance Program (ENT-GCD-RGC-EP-054) to further your understanding of Seminole's compliance program and your duties and responsibilities in the SOM.

Qualifications and Education Requirements

Bachelors of Science degree in Electrical Engineering from an ABET accredited institution is required. Advanced degree in engineering preferred. Registered or eligible to become a Registered Professional Engineer in the State of Florida. Eight (8) years of progressively responsible experience in electric power utility in the discipline of system protection, emphasis on design and settings. Professional registration as an engineer in Florida or an advanced degree in engineering may substitute for one (1) year of experience.

Core Competencies: Adaptable, Collaborative, Conscientious, Critical-Thinking, Outcome-Driven and Professional

Technical Competencies/Skills:

  • Engineering Design
  • Transmission and Generation System protection
  • System Protection Fault Analysis
  • System Protection Communication
  • NERC Compliance with PRC Standards
  • APEN and/or PSSCAPE for Fault Analysis
  • National Electric Code, Safety Codes, OSHA Rules, and appropriate Florida, RUS, NERC, FRCC and Federal transmission standards and regulations
  • AcSELerator 5010 SEL, GE URPC software
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications

Soft Competencies/Skills:

  • Effective verbal/nonverbal, listening and written communications
  • Self-starter/self-motivated
  • Risk Management
  • Project and time management
  • Organization
  • Multi-tasking
  • Analytical


Physical Requirements

Must be able to follow established protective measures including wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE). Must possess a valid driver’s license and acceptable Motor Vehicle Report.

Working Conditions

Some travel, overnight stays, and work outside of normal business hours to existing and future transmission facilities, substation and generator sites as required. While working in certain areas of substations and/or switchyards, there is the potential for exposure to hazards typical of an industrial working environment.

title: Financial Charges Audit C
description:
POSITION SUMMARY: The Financial Charges Audit Clerk is responsible for auditing patient bills (as directed) by comparing to the medical record chart to determine accuracy of charges. Coordinates with all departments regarding findings of audits; this includes hospital-directed audits and third party audit requests.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  1. Responds to and calendars all patient bill audits within the hospital utilizing hospital medical records, departmental logs, and qualified medical expertise, hospital-directed audits and/or third party audit requests.
  2. Works in cooperation with the HIM Department in order to audit medical record charts to patient billings.
  3. Verifies that charges on itemized statements are valid for services rendered and the charges are accurate.
  4. Reviews for all undercharges and overcharges on all audits.
  5. Inputs into the billing system appropriate credits and debits, balances accounts, and if applicable, requests new bills and forwards them to Billing Services.
  6. Processes necessary charge adjustments with third party representatives and serves as hospital liaison with all outside business involved in audits.
  7. Provides quality control feedback as it relates to the quality, accuracy, and timeliness of other departments as it relates to the billing process.
  8. Keep accurate records on all patients, under scope of responsibility, which includes keeping accurate information on account activity; provides appropriate file documentation as needed to maintain accurate records on status.
  9. Demonstrates an understanding of billing and follow-up policies and procedures in performing job duties and instructing patients and hospital personnel. Routinely uses Patient Accounting Policy and Procedure Manual and other reference materials.
  10. Responsible for reporting the status of all accounts under scope of responsibility. This includes the timely response to all requests and inquiries by the Department Coordinators or Manager.
  11. Performs general clerical functions: answers telephones, types, compiles necessary reports and maintains filing systems for information needed to complete work within the department. Responsible for providing weekly Financial Charges Audit Clerk Report reflecting all activity for the week.

OTHER RESPONSIBILITIES:

  1. Utilizes the HIS Affinity System to its full capacity. Continues to grow in the user of the computer system as its capabilities expand.
  2. Consistently responds to requests from patients for account charge settlement and related information in a timely and courteous manner.
  3. Performs similar job related duties as assigned.

JOB RELATIONSHIPS:

  1. Reports directly to the Patient Accounting Coordinator Billing Services.
  2. Works closely with Billing Services, Patient Financial Services staff, Compliance, Utilization Review, ancillary departments, HIM, and Information Systems.

EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, AND SKILLS REQUIRED:

  1. High school education or equivalent. Experience of three years of specialized billing and medical background is required.
  2. Mathematical ability required to review statistical data on various financial records.
  3. 10 key adding machine and typing experience is required. Accuracy is more important than speed. Knowledge of filing systems and copy machines.

AGE OF POPULATION SERVED:

Adolescent, Adult, Geriatrics

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

  1. Sits, stands, bends, lifts, and moves intermittently during working hours.
  2. Visual and hearing acuity pertinent to communicating with customers.

MENTAL REQUIREMENTS:

  1. Communicative skills necessary to converse effectively with patients and conduct inquires regarding status activity of claims.
  2. Ability to work under pressure. Must be able to deal tactfully and effectively with patients and third party representatives.
  3. Must possess the ability to make independent decisions when circumstances warrant such action.
  4. Is subject to frequent interruptions.
  5. Ability to organize and prioritize work to meet deadlines.

SCHEDULING AND AVAILABILITY:

  1. Regular hours are Monday to Friday, from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Some flexibility required as determined by the Patient Accounting Coordinators or Manager.
  2. This is a full time position requiring attendance at meetings, workshops, and hospital functions as determined by the Patient Accounting Manager.

title: Legal Analyst - Asia
description: At the International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group (WBG) , you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. Through partnerships across 145 countries and more than 182 offices worldwide, we work with governments, private sector, development partners and other stakeholders to invest in people, strengthen markets, and deliver scalable, data-driven solutions that generate more and better jobs and improve lives. In fiscal year 2026, IFC committed a record $105.6 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries. For more information, visit www.ifc.org . The selected candidate's duty station will be determined based on organizational requirements and business needs. To support IFC’s growing activities in Asia, CLED is recruiting a highly motivated and qualified Legal Analyst, to be based in Jakarta, Indonesia or New Delhi, India. The Legal Analyst will work as an integral member of CLED’s Asia team and will support IFC lawyers and business teams across investment, advisory, upstream, and portfolio matters. Duties and accountabilities: • Prepare supporting documentation for internal and external matters, e.g., powers of attorney, proxies, signature designations, counsel retainer letters and Article III notices (notifying member governments of proposed IFC investments). • Assist IFC in-house counsel in preparing and reviewing legal documentation, including standard-form agreements and routine amendments, consents and waivers. • Coordinate effectively with IFC’s external counsel, including supporting engagement and retainer processes, monitoring deliverables, and facilitating communication among IFC counsel, business teams, and other stakeholders as required. • Support the legal execution and closing of IFC transactions, including coordinating signature processes, tracking the completion of conditions to disbursement or effectiveness. • Maintain complete and accurate legal records and coordinate the filing of transaction documents in accordance with IFC guidelines and practices. • Support portfolio matters relating to IFC’s debt, equity and other investments, including routine amendments, waivers, consents, disbursements, restructurings and other post-commitment matters, as assigned. • Support IFC’s advisory and upstream program under appropriate supervision by IFC in-house counsel and follow up on the completion of any such agreements with IFC staff. • Identify and analyze legal and policy issues associated with investment or advisory or upstream projects. • Anticipate and escalate execution, documentation, or process issues that may affect transaction timelines or compliance with IFC requirements. • Contribute to and support CLED’s Knowledge Management or other organizational objectives, including the responsible use of AI-enabled or other legal technology tools, development of templates and guidance materials, and sharing lessons learned. • Contribute to and support institutional matters relevant to the relevant IFC country office and undertake other responsibilities assigned by IFC in-house counsel consistent with the role.

About Us

At ExxonMobil, our vision is to lead in energy innovations that advance modern living and a net-zero future. As one of the world's largest publicly traded energy and chemical companies, we are powered by a unique and diverse workforce fueled by the pride in what we do and what we stand for.

We invite you to bring your ideas to ExxonMobil to help create sustainable solutions that improve quality of life and meet society's evolving needs. Learn more about our What and our Why and how we can work together.

ExxonMobil in Singapore

ExxonMobil is one of Singapore’s largest foreign manufacturing investors with over S$25 billion in fixed asset investments.

We have manufacturing facilities that include an integrated world-scale refining and petrochemical complex in Jurong and Jurong Island, a network of service stations under the Esso brand, operate a lubricant plant and are a supplier of cylinder cooking gas. ExxonMobil provides customers and commercial markets in the region with ground transportation, industrial, aviation and marine fuels, lubricants, petrochemicals and liquefied natural gas (LNG).

As Singapore serves as the AP hub for some of our businesses, we employ about 3,500 people across positions in operations, projects, commercial, corporate support functions and others.

ExxonMobil also contributes to community programs in Singapore that support the arts, education, health and the environment.

For more information, visit www.exxonmobil.com.sg or follow ExxonMobil Singapore on LinkedIn and Instagram.

ExxonMobil Global Trading

ExxonMobil Global Trading is where we trade oil, natural gas, and energy products safely and responsibly around the world. We leverage our expertise in analytics, logistics, origination, and knowledge of energy markets to maximize the value of our global assets and deliver industry-leading results.

This is an exciting time to join our growing trading team and be an integral part of ExxonMobil.

What Role You Will Play In The Team

If successful, you will join ExxonMobil's Global Trading organization as a member of the Front Office technology team supporting commodity trading, commercial optimization, and market analytics activities across global energy markets.

We are seeking a highly motivated Full Stack Developer with strong software engineering, data engineering, and application development capabilities to design, build, and support modern applications that enable traders, analysts, risk managers, and commercial teams to make informed decisions in fast-moving markets.

In this role, you will work closely with trading desks, quantitative analysts, commercial teams, and technology professionals to develop scalable applications, data platforms, analytics tools, and workflow solutions that enhance market transparency, streamline operations, and create commercial value. You will play a key role in building production-grade systems used directly by front-office teams across crude oil, natural gas, LNG, refined products, power, environmental products, and related commodity markets.

What You Will Do

  • Develop, enhance, and maintain front-office applications supporting commodity trading, market analytics, risk management, and commercial optimization activities.
  • Design and build scalable full-stack solutions leveraging modern front-end, back-end, and cloud technologies.

  • Develop and maintain backend services, APIs, and application integrations supporting market data, trading systems, and analytical platforms.
  • Design, develop, and support data pipelines and data platforms that provide timely access to market, risk, operational, and fundamental data.
  • Build tools that support pricing, market analysis, forecasting, position management, and trading workflows.
  • Contribute to application architecture, technical design, and software engineering best practices.
  • Monitor, troubleshoot, and improve application performance, reliability, scalability, and security.
  • Collaborate with cloud, infrastructure, and platform teams to deploy and support production solutions.
  • Implement automated testing, CI/CD processes, version control, and development standards across applications.
  • Identify opportunities to modernize legacy processes and develop innovative solutions that improve front-office productivity.
  • Communicate technical concepts effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

About You

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Engineering, Mathematics, Finance, or a related discipline.
  • Experience developing commercial or enterprise software applications using modern software engineering practices.
  • Strong proficiency in Python and experience building production-grade applications and services.
  • Experience developing front-end applications using JavaScript/TypeScript and modern frameworks such as React.
  • Experience designing, developing, and maintaining REST APIs and backend services.
  • Strong knowledge of SQL and experience working with relational databases such as PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle, or similar platforms.
  • Experience building data pipelines, data workflows, and data-driven applications.
  • Familiarity with cloud technologies including Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with business stakeholders and development teams.
  • Excellent communication skills and ability to operate in a fast-paced commercial environment.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities while delivering high-quality solutions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting energy trading, commodity trading, market analytics, or financial trading organizations.
  • Understanding of commodity markets including crude oil, natural gas, LNG, refined products, power, environmental products, or related energy markets.
  • Experience working directly with front-office users such as traders, analysts, risk managers, or quantitative researchers.
  • Strong proficiency in Python ecosystem tools including Pandas, NumPy, FastAPI, and related analytics libraries.
  • Experience developing applications using React and modern front-end frameworks.
  • Experience building and supporting large-scale databases, data warehouses, and market data solutions.
  • Familiarity with Databricks, Snowflake, Azure Data Platform, or similar cloud-based data technologies.
  • Experience with message-based architectures, distributed systems, and event-driven application design.
  • Understanding of software engineering best practices including automated testing, CI/CD, version control (Git), and DevOps methodologies.
  • Knowledge of market data platforms, trading systems, and real-time data integration processes.
  • Experience developing applications that support trading, risk management, forecasting, optimization, or commercial decision-making.

Your Benefits

An ExxonMobil career is one designed to last and we provide job rotations throughout your career with us. Our commitment to you runs deep: our employees grow personally and professionally, with benefits built on our core categories of health, security, finance, and life.

Currently our employees benefits include: Long Term Savings Allowance, dental reimbursement, annual health checkups and Home Ownership Assistance Plan amongst others and these are updated from time to time.

title: Fullstack Engineer - SDET Depth (Quality Engineer)
description:
You will own the quality net for a client-delivery squad: the system that makes a missing spec, a dropped requirement, or a silent regression impossible to ship unnoticed. You are a fullstack engineer who builds the fastest and hardens everything, and you spend that speed engineering quality in rather than inspecting it at the end.

What you will do:

Build and own the artifact net: a Definition of Ready that stops a story entering build without its acceptance criteria and spec, automated CI checks that fail when a change has no test or breaks a covered path, and a Definition of Done enforced at release.

Own the regression system: test architecture, CI gates, the automated regression and smoke suites, defect management, and release QA.

Build your own modules end to end (API, UI, data, tests), like every engineer on the squad.

Hold stop-the-line authority at release: block a release when the net goes red, and own that call.

Make and defend severity and risk decisions, and surface systemic patterns, not just individual bugs.

Use AI heavily to move fast, and apply the judgment that AI cannot: what to test, what to gate, what a passing test actually proves.

How you will be measured:

quality is a property of the system you build, so that it holds even when you are not in the room, and scales to the next squad without you. You succeed when the team ships predictably and the net, not your vigilance, is what catches the problems.

Must have:

4 to 7 years building production web software, with a track record of owning quality, not only writing features.

Strong test automation: can design a test architecture and CI gates, not just write individual test cases (Playwright, Jest/Vitest, or equivalent).

CI/CD experience: has built or maintained pipelines that block bad changes (GitHub Actions or equivalent).

Sound defect judgment: can classify severity (blocker vs data-integrity vs minor vs cosmetic) and defend the call. Treats a bug that shows the right thing on screen but stores the wrong value underneath as serious.

Uses AI as leverage and verifies it: generates with AI, then curates and catches where AI-generated “passing” tests prove nothing.

Communicates and holds a line: can tell a team a release is not ready, with evidence, under deadline pressure.

Nice to have:

Experience defining and enforcing a Definition of Ready / Definition of Done as tooling, not a wiki page.

Requirements traceability or test-coverage-gap analysis experience.

B2B / client-delivery or consulting-software background (multiple parallel projects).

Exposure to AI-feature delivery (evaluation sets, ground truth, regression on prompt changes).

Not required (and not what we are hiring for):

Manual-only QA background with no automation or coding.

“Tester at the end of the line.” This seat builds quality in from the first sprint and owns its own modules too.

title: Permitting Specialist
description:
Job Summary:

The Senior Geologist/Project Manager will lead the preparation, submission, and management of environmental permits for projects in Arizona and beyond, with a primary focus on AZPDES (Arizona Pollutant Discharge Elimination System) permits for discharges to surface waters (including stormwater, wastewater, and industrial discharges), Section 404 permits under the Clean Water Act for dredge and fill activities in waters of the U.S. (administered by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers), and other related federal, state, and local environmental permits. This leadership role involves overseeing permitting strategies, coordinating multidisciplinary teams, ensuring regulatory compliance, and serving as the primary point of contact with agencies such as the Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ), U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), and EPA. The position requires deep expertise in Clean Water Act regulations, strong project management skills, and the ability to navigate complex permitting processes for infrastructure, development, mining, energy, or industrial projects while minimizing environmental impacts and supporting project timelines.

Duties:

  • Assist in the preparation, compilation, and submission of AZPDES individual and general permits (e.g., for municipal, industrial, construction stormwater, and MS4 discharges), including completing required forms (Form 1, Form 2A/2S), developing Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs), and ensuring compliance with ADEQ requirements.
  • Manage Section 404 permitting processes, including jurisdictional determinations, pre-application consultations with USACE, preparation of permit applications, alternatives analyses, mitigation plans, and coordination for individual or nationwide/general permits involving dredge/fill in wetlands or waters of the U.S.
  • Oversee additional environmental permitting efforts, such as Section 401 Water Quality Certifications, Aquifer Protection Permits (APP), NEPA compliance support, endangered species consultations, and other state/local permits as needed.
  • Develop and implement permitting strategies, timelines, and budgets; identify potential regulatory risks and recommend avoidance, minimization, or mitigation measures.
  • Serve as lead technical expert and point of contact for regulatory agencies; prepare for and participate in pre-application meetings, public notices, hearings, and agency negotiations.
  • Coordinate with internal teams (engineers, biologists, hydrologists, project managers) and external consultants to gather data, conduct environmental assessments, and prepare supporting documentation (e.g., wetland delineations, biological surveys, water quality modeling).
  • Review and interpret federal (Clean Water Act, NEPA) and Arizona-specific regulations; stay current on updates to AZPDES, Section 404 guidelines, and related policies.
  • Mentor junior staff on permitting processes, regulatory compliance, and best practices

Education/Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree (required) in Geology, Environmental Science, Biology, Ecology, Hydrology, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resources Management, or a closely related field.
  • Master's degree in a relevant discipline preferred.
  • Minimum of 8-10+ years of progressively responsible experience in environmental permitting, with at least 5 years supporting complex permitting projects.
  • Demonstrated expertise in Clean Water Act programs, particularly AZPDES/NPDES permitting (stormwater, wastewater discharges) and USACE Section 404 permitting (wetlands, dredge/fill).
  • Proven track record leading permit applications for large-scale projects in Arizona or similar arid/southwestern environments (e.g., infrastructure, mining, energy, development).
  • Strong knowledge of federal and Arizona environmental regulations, including ADEQ processes, USACE permitting procedures, and related requirements (e.g., mitigation banking, jurisdictional determinations).
  • Excellent project management, organizational, and communication skills, with experience preparing technical reports, permit applications, and presenting to stakeholders/agencies.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite; familiarity with GIS tools for mapping and analysis preferred.

Certifications/Licenses:

  • Professional certification preferred, such as: Registered Geologist or Professional Engineer Certified Wetland Scientist (CWS) or Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS) through the Society of Wetland Scientists.
  • Certified Environmental Professional (CEP) or similar.
  • OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER certification (or willingness to obtain).
  • Valid driver's license required, with ability to travel to project sites and agency meetings as needed.
  • Other relevant certifications (e.g., stormwater inspector training, wetland delineation courses) are a plus.

title: Medical Laboratory Scientist I/Technologist I, Certified
location: Salt Lake City, Utah, United States
description:
Schedule:
Wednesday - Saturday (40 hrs/wk)
3:00 PM - 1:30 AM

Training Schedule:
Monday - Friday
7:00 AM - 3:30 PM

Department: Molecular Automated Dept - 652

Primary Purpose:

Provides services of both a technical and non-technical nature in the laboratory service areas. Performs routine and complex laboratory tests in an assigned department of the clinical laboratory to provide physicians with rapid and accurate laboratory test results. Works under the direction of specialist, lead, and/or supervisor.

This position is not qualified for delegation of supervisory duties for NY testing areas.

About ARUP:

ARUP Laboratories is a national clinical and anatomic pathology reference laboratory and an enterprise of the University of Utah and its Department of Pathology. Based in Salt Lake City, Utah.

ARUP proudly hires top talent to create a work environment of diversity, professional growth and continuous development. Our workforce is committed to the important service we provide to over one million patients each month. We always strive for excellence and have a strong desire to have involvement with the advances in medicine and the role laboratory services plays within each patient’s life. We never forget that there is a patient behind every specimen we receive.

We are looking for individuals who want to contribute to ARUP's culture of accountability, integrity, service, and excellence. Consider joining our dynamic team.

Essential Functions:

Performs waived, moderate, and/or highly complex analytic processes without direct supervision for which they are qualified, trained, and demonstrates competency according to established lab standard operating procedures (SOPs).

Operates, calibrates and troubleshoots laboratory instruments and ensures proper functioning of laboratory equipment. Recognizes when professional service is required and requests service if instrument is covered under a service contract. Otherwise, reports service needs to supervisor for resolution.

Performs quality control (QC) procedures as specified in lab section SOPs and maintains QC records and documentation necessary to meet the standards of accrediting agencies.

Follows appropriate specimen collection, handling, transport, and recording procedures.

Processes data, verifies accuracy, and enters data in the laboratory information system, along with appropriate explanatory or interpretive information in a timely manner.

Monitors QC and assists in data collection for Quality Assurance (QA) indicators, as assigned.

Performs internal and external proficiency testing.

Meets output measures as defined by individual group policy. Assists with workload in any section where competency has been verified and is current.

Recognizes critical patient results and follows the defined process for reporting them.

Recognizes unexpected results, errors, and problems with patient tests and escalates as required.

Understands the theory of laboratory procedures and evaluates all potential causes of unexpected test results.

Correlates clinical and laboratory data with pathologic states to determine result validity.

Evaluates exceptions to established criteria and special circumstances related to specimen collection and integrity to determine impact on testing.

Recognizes appropriate and inappropriate selection of basic and complex lab tests.

Prioritizes order of testing and coordinates general work flow in assigned area.

Resolves and documents resolution of all QC results which fail lab criteria and institutes corrective action.

Integrates and relates lab data to investigate possible discrepancies and contributes to the resolution.

Trains new and current employees on procedures and policies.

Provides technical information and/or instruction to clients, new employees, medical students, residents, peers, physicians, and the public as requested and where appropriate.

Maintains adequate inventory of reagents and supplies.

Directs workflow activities and reviews daily data reports as assigned.

Performs assessment of peers performing testing as a qualified observer after two years of experience not including NY testing.

Other duties as assigned.

Physical and Other Requirements:

Stooping: Bending body downward and forward by bending spine at the waist.

Reaching: Extending hand(s) and arm(s) in any direction.

Mobility: The person in this position needs to occasionally move between work sites and inside the office to access file cabinets, office machinery, etc.

Communicate: Frequently communicate with others.

PPE: Biohazard laboratory environment that requires use of personal protective equipment in accordance with CDC and OSHA regulations and company policies.

ARUP Policies and Procedures: To conduct self in compliance with all ARUP Policies and Procedures.

Sedentary Work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects.

Fine Motor Control: Picking, pinching, typing or otherwise working, primarily with fingers rather than with the whole hand as in handling.

Vision: Having close, far, and peripheral visual acuity to perform a variety of tasks such as make general observations of depth and distance.

Color Vision: Perception of and ability to distinguish colors.

Continuing Education: Continual assessment of current literature and best practices.

Education Qualifications:

This position requires an evaluation of education and credentials. This may include but not limited to; all college/university transcripts (including any transferred credits), all degrees conferred, a letter from the school’s registrar stating the date of expected graduation if enrolled in the last semester, and any relevant certifications. Upon request, submit all required documents. To avoid delays please ensure these documents are available.

Note: Applications will be accepted from candidates who are within one semester or quarter of obtaining a Bachelor’s degree in Clinical Laboratory Science, Medical Laboratory Science or Medical Technology and have successfully completed the clinical rotation in the area of job duties. May be hired as a Technician, Medical Laboratory Scientist in Training, the minimum pay rate is $25.41 hr. If hired will have 6 months to obtain certification. Other restrictions may apply.

title: Research Engineer, Foundation Model
description:
Our Mission

At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient.

We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today!

The Role

As a Foundational Models & ML Engineer, you'll build the models that power our autonomous security platforms. You'll train, fine-tune, and deploy VLAs, VLMs, and world models that give our robots contextual understanding and intelligent control, pushing the frontier of how machines perceive, reason, and act in the physical world.

This is a hands-on research-engineering role. You won't be writing papers without products. You'll be shipping models that run on real robots in real environments, with all the messy data, hard constraints, and latency budgets that come with embodied AI. You'll work closely with the autonomy and platform teams to close the loop from data collection to model training to fielded deployment.

What You'll Work On

  • Train and fine-tune VLA/VLM models for robot control, perception, and contextual reasoning.

  • Build data pipelines that turn field-collected video, telemetry, and language signals into training-ready datasets.

  • Run experiments at the intersection of foundation models and embodied AI: behavior cloning, RLHF, instruction following, world modeling.

  • Optimize models for edge deployment: quantization, distillation, latency tuning for robot-grade compute.

  • Close the loop with autonomy: define clean interfaces between learned components and classical autonomy modules.

  • Drive a continuous evaluation harness, from sim benchmarks to field metrics on real deployments.

Who We're Looking For

We're looking for a strong ML engineer or research engineer who has shipped foundation model work into production, ideally in an embodied or multi-modal setting. You think rigorously about data, model design, and evaluation. You're comfortable training large models, but you also care deeply about whether they actually work when deployed under real-world constraints.

Your Background:

  • PhD or equivalent research experience in ML, computer vision, robotics, or related field.

  • Strong PyTorch (or JAX) skills. Comfortable scaling training across multi-GPU and multi-node setups.

  • Familiarity with the current VLA/VLM landscape (π0.7, GR00T, and similar) and the underlying research literature.

  • Experience taking models from research to deployment: optimization, quantization, latency tuning.

  • Solid software engineering hygiene: version control, reproducibility, evaluation discipline.

  • Publications at top ML or robotics venues (NeurIPS, ICML, CoRL, RSS, ICRA).

Nice to Have:

  • Hands-on experience with robotics simulators (IsaacSim, MuJoCo, Gazebo) or real robot data collection.

What We Offer

  • Ownership: you are the first in line to build and lead the team you help hire.

  • Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence.

  • Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow.

  • Team: work directly with PhD-level co-founders in AI, Robotics, and Physics, alongside a strong (and fun) founding team.

  • Compensation: Competitive equity/salary package

  • Culture: a small, international founding team that is serious about building but does not take itself too seriously.

title: Principal Software Engineer
description:
About Dockwa

Dockwa is the operating system for the marine economy.

More than 1,250 marinas run their business on our software and more than 500,000 boaters use our app to find and book a slip. Nearly half a million reservations moved through us in the last twelve months. We own the boater marketplace, marina operations, and the payments layer underneath both.

That distribution is the whole argument. When anyone can generate software, the durable advantage is being the system an industry already runs on. We have that in boating and we just raised to go take it global.

About the Role

We are hiring one principal engineer, and we are hiring them to raise the ceiling of what this team can build.

Engineering is six people today and will be fourteen inside a year. Our surface area is far larger than that: reservations, payments and money movement, dock and slip management, rent roll, boater CRM, service and work orders, accounting integrations, a native iOS app, and now multi-currency for international markets. That math only works if we get dramatically better at building, not just bigger.

You will rebuild how we build. We treat AI as core development infrastructure, not a side experiment. We want someone who pushes the automation of our development lifecycle much further than it is today, proves it on real production work, and pulls the rest of the team up to that bar.

You will own the architecture that makes speed safe. We are twelve years into a system carrying real traffic and real money. Going faster only works if the foundation holds while we stack international, enterprise, and new verticals on top of it. You make those structural calls.

We are not hiring a principal to be the best coder in the room. We are hiring one so that in eighteen months a team of fourteen ships like a team of forty.

Who Thrives Here

The people who thrive at Dockwa have usually founded something, or joined something early and grew with it. They think in outcomes rather than tickets. They have opinions about the product and the business, not only the code. They would rather ship something a marina operator notices on a Saturday morning than win an argument about abstractions.

You should want to steer. There is more consequential work here than there are people to do it, which means you will decide what gets built at least as often as you build it.

What You Need

  • Production software you owned outright, end to end, including after it shipped.
  • Real AI fluency with receipts. Not tool familiarity. Work you could not have delivered without it.
  • Comfort across a full stack. Ours is Rails, React, Postgres, AWS and Swift, but we will take judgment over stack match every time.
  • Architectural decisions you had to live with afterwards, in systems you did not originally write.
  • Evidence you changed how a team worked, not only what it shipped.

How We Hire

Short, collaborative, and built around real problems rather than memory tests or puzzles. We are screening for motivation and judgment over trivia, and we want you to finish the process more excited than you started it.

How We Work

We are a small team that is winning. Problems grow exponentially with each person added, not linearly, so we keep the organization lean on purpose and put people at the source of problems with real ownership.

We automate before we hire. We ship quality at speed and treat those as compatible. We own the full loop from discovery to payment to analytics, because controlling the data is what makes the intelligence products possible.

We move fast, and context does not always land perfectly. It is always fine to ask why.

We have an institutional partner in PSG and an annual plan that’s in our control. We’re investing heavily in product and engineering because the operating system of the marine economy is ours to build and own. Acquisitions are part of how we grow, and we have dedicated budget behind that as well.

Equal Opportunity

We hire for range on purpose. Different vantage points produce better arguments, and on a team this small every viewpoint in the room changes the outcome. Dockwa is an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic.

title: FPGA Engineer (Controls & Signal Processing)
description:
About Enact

The next defining technological breakthrough will be in the physical world. We stand at a historical inflection point: bringing general-purpose intelligence into robotics.

At Enact we rethink the entire robotic tech stack from model architectures and data pipelines, to the actuators and sensors that feed the model. Pushing beyond pure vision and language approaches, we build a proprioceptive nerve system, and the cortex that makes sense of it, to solve dexterity through whole-body force-awareness and deploy robots for thousands of tasks in industry and beyond.

We are shaping a company where brilliant and unconventional people thrive together on solving the hardest challenges of our time. We are truth seekers. We reason from first principles, test our beliefs against reality, and trust that the best ideas can come from anyone. We move fast. We care deeply about our work and colleagues and are driven by passion to change the status quo.

If this resonates, we're excited to hear from you.

In This Role You Will

  • Design, implement, and verify the FPGA fabric at the heart of our custom hardware, from real-time control and signal processing to high-speed sensor and data interfaces.

  • Own the build flow: synthesis, place & route, static timing analysis, and timing closure on real silicon.

  • Develop testbenches, simulation, and co-simulation to verify behaviour at unit and system level.

  • Take designs from RTL through board bring-up, integration, and lab debug under real operating conditions all the way through to production-ready.

  • Keep the design understandable: specifications, timing budgets, and verification plans.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong digital design fundamentals: RTL in SystemVerilog (or VHDL), and a solid grasp of computer architecture.

  • The ability to reason about fixed- and floating-point data paths and pipelines - where precision goes, where it costs you, and how a computation maps onto real hardware.

  • Experience closing timing: static timing analysis, writing constraints, clock-domain crossing, and synchronization.

  • Fluency with at least one vendor toolchain (Xilinx/AMD, Intel/Altera, or Lattice), in a heavily scripted setting.

  • Comfortable reading schematics, reasoning from first principles, and working shoulder-to-shoulder with electronics and mechanical engineers.

  • The ability to take designs from benchtop prototype to production ready.

  • Fluency in English (German not required, though useful!).

Bonus Points If You Have

Having done these before is a plus, not a prerequisite. You'll do much of it in the role:

  • Rust or embedded firmware experience.

  • DSP in fabric: filtering (FIR/IIR), FFT, and fixed-point implementation.

  • Control theory: system identification, plant modeling, and loop tuning.

  • High-speed ADC/DAC interfaces and sensor/communication protocols.

  • Expert knowledge of version control, especially git.

  • Safety-critical or certified design.

  • Experience collaborating across analog, software, and mechanical domains.

What We Offer

  • The opportunity to make a real impact working on some of the biggest challenges of our time

  • A fast-paced learning environment alongside an outstanding, driven team

  • Ownership from day one, with the ability to iterate quickly and see your impact firsthand in an early-stage startup

  • Visa sponsorship & relocation benefits to hire the best in the world

  • A world-class in-person setup in central Zürich, with excellent prototyping, robotics, and technical infrastructure for hands-on builders

  • Competitive compensation and meaningful equity participation

title: Senior Specialist, DevOps
description:
Position Summary

The Snr Specialist, DevOps leads the Group DevOps function and provides technical leadership to DevOps Engineers supporting the development, deployment, and operation of in-house solutions across diverse technology stacks.

Reporting to the Group Snr Manager, Enterprise Systems, the role owns the Group's software delivery platform — source control, CI/CD pipelines, build and release automation, environment and infrastructure provisioning, and platform observability — and establishes the DevOps practices and engineering standards that in-house development teams adopt consistently. The role partners with the Cybersecurity Specialist on platform security across the delivery lifecycle, covering secrets management, dependency and vulnerability management, access control, and secure-by-default deployment patterns. As a further responsibility, the role leads the responsible adoption of AI-assisted coding and automation tools within the development community, defining usage guardrails, review requirements, and evaluation criteria. The role provides direction, coaching, and technical guidance to the DevOps Engineers, partners application, infrastructure, and information-security teams across the Group, and manages tooling and platform vendors at the operational level.

Responsibilities

DevOps Practice and Technical Leadership

  • Provide technical leadership and influence to DevOps Engineers, guiding technical direction, coordinating effort across concurrent development initiatives, and coaching on engineering practice.
  • Define and maintain Group DevOps standards, reference pipelines, environment conventions, and engineering documentation, and drive consistent adoption across in-house development teams.
  • Establish a working rhythm with development, infrastructure, and information-security teams covering intake, prioritisation, and delivery commitments, influencing outcomes through technical credibility rather than reporting lines.
  • Report platform health, delivery throughput, and improvement progress to the Group Snr Manager, Enterprise Systems and IDT leadership.
  • Manage DevOps tooling and cloud platform vendors at the operational level, including license utilization, service quality, and cost.

CI/CD and Build Automation

  • Own the Group's CI/CD pipelines end to end, covering source control, branching strategy, automated build, test integration, artefact management, and release promotion.
  • Strengthen deployment reliability through repeatable, automated releases with versioning, rollback, and change traceability across development, test, and production environments.
  • Automate environment and infrastructure provisioning using infrastructure-as-code and configuration-management practices to reduce manual effort and environment drift.
  • Support diverse technology stacks — web, application, database, integration, and containerised workloads — with pipeline patterns that development teams can reuse.
  • Reduce lead time from commit to production while maintaining change quality, working with development teams on test automation and quality gates.

Reliability and Observability

  • Establish platform observability — logging, metrics, tracing, dashboards, and alerting — so that service health and application behaviour are visible to development and support teams.
  • Agree availability and performance targets for in-house solutions with their owners, and monitor and report performance against them.
  • Own incident response for platform and deployment issues, including support coverage, escalation, root-cause analysis, and preventive action.
  • Ensure backup, recovery, and business-continuity routines are in place and tested for platform components and deployment tooling.
  • Manage capacity, cost, and lifecycle of the underlying cloud and on-premise platform resources.

Platform and Pipeline Security

  • Embed security into the delivery lifecycle, including secrets management, dependency and container scanning, static and dynamic application security testing, and remediation tracking.
  • Implement and maintain access control, least-privilege, and segregation-of-duties arrangements across repositories, pipelines, and environments.
  • Ensure platform configuration, patching, and hardening comply with Group IT security policy and applicable regulatory and audit requirements.
  • Work with information security on vulnerability management, penetration-test findings, and security incidents affecting the delivery platform.

AI-Assisted Development Enablement

  • Lead responsible adoption of AI-assisted coding and automation tools across development teams, defining approved tooling, usage guardrails, and data-handling rules.
  • Establish review and quality requirements for AI-generated code, including human review, testing, licensing, and intellectual-property considerations.
  • Evaluate and pilot AI-assisted engineering and automation tools, measuring productivity and quality outcomes before wider rollout.
  • Build capability through enablement sessions, documentation, and internal guidance so that teams use these tools consistently and safely.

Experience

  • Minimum 8 years of experience in software engineering, infrastructure, or platform engineering, including at least 3 years in a DevOps or platform role supporting in-house application development.
  • Proven experience providing technical leadership to engineers in an influence-based capacity, covering technical review, mentoring, and capability development.
  • Hands-on experience building and operating CI/CD pipelines end to end (e.g. Azure DevOps, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Jenkins), including automated build, test integration, artefact management, and release automation.
  • Experience supporting applications across diverse technology stacks and environments, spanning cloud (Azure, AWS, or GCP) and on-premise deployments.
  • Demonstrable experience implementing platform security controls within the delivery lifecycle — secrets management, dependency and vulnerability scanning, access control, and hardening.
  • Experience implementing observability and monitoring tooling (e.g. Azure Monitor, Grafana, Prometheus, ELK) and operating incident and problem management for platform services.
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code and configuration management (e.g. Terraform, Bicep/ARM, Ansible), and with containerisation and orchestration (e.g. Docker, Kubernetes) is an advantage.
  • Experience introducing AI-assisted coding or automation tools (e.g. GitHub Copilot or equivalent) into a development environment, including guardrails and adoption support, is an advantage.
  • Experience working with a regional or global headquarters IT function within a multinational group is an advantage.
  • Experience in a manufacturing or industrial group environment, including integration with ERP or operational systems, is an advantage.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a related discipline.
  • Cloud platform certification is an advantage, e.g. Microsoft Certified: Azure DevOps Engineer Expert, Azure Administrator or Solutions Architect, or AWS Certified DevOps Engineer.
  • Container platform certification (e.g. CKA or CKAD) is an advantage.
  • Security-related certification (e.g. CompTIA Security+, Microsoft SC-series, CSSLP) is an advantage.
  • ITIL Foundation or an equivalent service-management certification is an advantage.
  • Fluency in written and spoken English; additional Mandarin ability is an advantage given Group operations in China.

Competencies

Technical

  • Strong grounding in CI/CD, release engineering, and build automation across multiple technology stacks.
  • Proficient with infrastructure-as-code, configuration management, containerisation, and orchestration.
  • Working knowledge of cloud and on-premise platform architecture, networking, and identity and access management as they affect application deployment.
  • Practical understanding of secure software delivery — secrets management, vulnerability and dependency management, code scanning, and hardening.
  • Competent with observability tooling and with scripting and automation (e.g. PowerShell, Bash, Python).

description:

Emerge is a fast-growing New Zealand fintech reshaping what modern financial services can look like. Built at the intersection of technology, product, engineering and regulated financial services, the business is creating smart, scalable financial products for people, families and businesses.

The business already has strong foundations in place across transactional accounts, payments and expense management, and is now moving into a wider product suite. That growth creates a rare opportunity for an experienced backend engineer to own high-impact services across real-time financial products and platform growth.

About the role

As Senior Backend Engineer, you will design, build and operate the services that move and account for customer money. You will work across the real-time transaction path, core banking platform and new product capability, with a strong focus on correctness, resilience and production ownership.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can take complex backend work from ambiguity through to production. You will work closely with product and engineering teams, contribute to architecture and technical reviews, and use AI coding tools thoughtfully while owning every line that ships.

You may also support work connected to Emerge’s broader banking-as-a-service and partner delivery priorities, while remaining part of the New Zealand engineering team.

You will:

  • Design and build Kotlin and Spring services across authorisation, ledger, limits, reconciliation and settlement.
  • Extend the core platform for new products across personal, business and partner banking use cases.
  • Own correctness through idempotent operations, safe retries, immutable records and reliable event handling.
  • Keep PostgreSQL performant and safe through strong schema design, indexing, migrations and query performance.
  • Work across AWS infrastructure, observability, alerting and production support for services you own.
  • Participate in design reviews, tech reviews, pull request reviews and incident response.
  • Use AI coding tools daily, while reviewing, directing and owning the quality of what ships.

About you

You are a senior backend engineer with strong technical depth and a high sense of ownership. You think carefully about consistency, failure modes, blast radius and trade-offs. You are practical, delivery-focused and comfortable working through complexity without needing heavy structure. You communicate clearly around risk, progress and technical decisions, and you stay close to what you build after it reaches production.

Where you might be right now

You may be a senior backend engineer in a fintech, payments, banking, SaaS, product technology or regulated systems environment. You may also come from a strong backend product engineering background where correctness, reliability and production ownership matter deeply.

You will bring

  • Significant backend engineering experience, ideally 7+ years, with strong Kotlin or Java and Spring Boot depth.
  • Production experience with PostgreSQL, including schema design, indexing, performance and migrations.
  • AWS production experience, such as ECS, Lambda, S3 or close equivalents.
  • Experience owning backend services through design, build, release and production support.
  • Strong judgement around distributed systems, data consistency, safe retries and failure modes.
  • Practical AI coding tool experience, with a considered view on review, trust and limits.
  • Payments, banking, ledger, reconciliation or regulated financial systems experience would be helpful.
  • Current New Zealand work rights, or a clear low-risk pathway to start without lengthy visa delays.

Why join Emerge?

  • Own meaningful backend services in a fintech with foundations in place and a clear growth runway ahead.
  • Work on real-time financial systems where correctness, reliability and performance matter.
  • Join an AI-forward engineering team that values pace, judgement and ownership.
  • Partner closely with product, engineering and operations as Emerge expands its platform.
  • Make a visible impact as Emerge continues building modern financial products for New Zealand and beyond.

title: Collections Analyst
description:
Position Summary:

The Collections Analyst is responsible for managing assigned customer accounts from both a collections and analytical perspective. Approximately 50% of the role is focused on account analysis, research, and dispute resolution. The Collections Analyst is expected to identify why payment is being delayed, research discrepancies across multiple data sources, and work across internal teams and directly with customers to resolve the underlying issue so payment can be collected. The goal is to become the account expert for assigned customers and bring forward solutions

Key Responsibilities:

  • Analyze assigned accounts, aging, invoices, disputes, payment history, and supporting documentation to determine the root cause of delayed or missing payment and use that information to resolve open issues and obtain payment.
  • Pull, review, and compare large data sets from customer portals, accounting/ERP systems, BI tools, Excel/CSV files, and other sources to identify missing, incorrect, or inconsistent information.
  • Combine data from multiple sources when necessary to research issues such as incorrect bill-to information, missing customer-required documentation, invoice discrepancies, or other barriers to payment.
  • Research customer disputes, determine the action needed, and engage with internal and external partners to resolve.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Finance, Billing, Operations, Account Management, and other teams to correct issues and drive disputes through resolution.
  • Identify recurring account issues, trends, and process gaps and recommend solutions that improve collections and prevent future payment delays.
  • Own assigned customer accounts and become the primary collections subject-matter expert for those accounts.
  • Track, record, and reconcile assigned customer accounts.
  • Contact past-due customers to request payment and resolve outstanding balances.
  • Serve as a customer-facing point of contact for collection issues, disputes, and documentation needs.
  • Work directly with customers and internal Finance partners to review denied payments, determine whether the denial is valid, and take the appropriate action to resolve or respond to the issue
  • Process payments and assist with arranging payment timelines or installment plans when necessary.
  • Maintain a clear understanding of assigned customers' billing, documentation, portal, and payment requirements to proactively identify and resolve issues that may delay payment.
  • Provide required invoice documentation to customers, including resubmitting, uploading, or emailing materials to support payment processing.
  • Identify missing or incorrect documentation and take ownership of obtaining, and resubmitting the information needed to resolve the issue and support payment.
  • Prepare and review customer-specific reports, aging information, dispute details, and account status updates according to required deadlines.
  • Participate in weekly collections meetings and verbally present the status of assigned accounts, including outstanding balances, dispute reasons, actions taken, risks, and next steps.
  • Be prepared to answer questions regarding assigned accounts and clearly communicate what is preventing payment and what is being done to resolve it.
  • Plan and prioritize daily work independently based on account risk, aging, customer needs, and deadlines.

As a 100% employee-owned firm, we deliver comprehensive testing, analysis, and design to reduce uncertainty in construction projects and offer rewarding work, exceptional training, and career development opportunities.

Job Summary

The Environmental Field Scientist plays a critical hands-on role in executing environmental field activities, including site investigations, sampling programs, field monitoring, and data collection. This position focuses on supporting environmental projects through accurate field observations, operation of field instruments, and responsible documentation of site conditions. The Field Scientist works under general supervision while gaining experience in environmental field methods, equipment operation, and project support tasks. The primary duties for this position will be field activities focusing on asbestos, lead, indoor air quality, and industrial hygiene services. Secondary duties will be field activities focusing on soil, groundwater, and due diligence services.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Reasonable accommodations or workable solutions may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

  • Conduct field sampling of soil, groundwater, surface water, stormwater, air, and other environmental media following established procedures.
  • Support installation of monitoring wells and assist with drilling oversight and soil/rock logging.
  • Perform asbestos sampling and inspections, and assist with hazardous building material assessments in support of environmental and due diligence projects.
  • Comfortable climbing, working at heights, and on rooftops on various apparatus: 6’-10’ step ladders, 20’-40’ extension ladders, and a variety of mechanical lifts.
  • Up to 90% of field work will be outside in various weather conditions.
  • On a limited basis, employee may be asked to work extended hours, as well as nights, and weekends, when required and sometimes on short notice.
  • Perform operation, maintenance, and monitoring (OM&M) of treatment systems and collect relevant performance data.
  • Record field measurements and observations, ensuring complete, accurate, and well-organized field notes.
  • Use field instruments to measure organic vapor, water levels, physical soil characteristics, and other environmental parameters.
  • Support site reconnaissance activities, documenting site features, potential environmental concerns, and safety conditions.
  • Assist with GPS/GIS data collection and preparation of site maps and figures using ArcGIS or similar software.
  • Classify soils using the Unified Soil Classification System (USCS).
  • Coordinate field schedules and activities with colleagues, subcontractors, drillers, and project managers.
  • Maintain and prepare field equipment, ensuring proper calibration, care, and documentation.
  • Provide preliminary observations and contribute to technical sections of reports under the guidance of senior staff.
  • Continuously develop knowledge of environmental field methods, sampling protocols, and applicable regulations.
  • Assist in the preparation of permits, documentation, and field-related project deliverables.
  • Seek opportunities to support additional projects and departments to maintain productivity.
  • Perform other duties as assigned to support department and company goals.


Other Areas of Accountability

  • Conduct all field activities in compliance with federal, state, and local environmental, health, and safety regulations, as well as AET’s Health and Safety Policy.
  • Maintain a valid driver’s license and acceptable driving record; some positions may require the use of a personal vehicle and/or compliance with DOT driver requirements.
  • Travel frequently (up to 20%) within the regional area for field assignments; occasional weekend or out-of-town work may be required.
  • Properly use, maintain, and store company equipment and instrumentation.
  • Deliver high-quality field data and support project completion within budget and schedule expectations.
  • Maintain required physicals or certifications associated with fieldwork.
  • Collaborate effectively with AET staff to enhance communication, efficiency, and project coordination.
  • Build and maintain positive relationships with clients, subcontractors, and project partners.


Required Qualifications and Education Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Earth Sciences, Environmental Engineering, Geology, or a related field.
  • 0-3 years of experience in environmental consulting, regulatory compliance, or a related field (internship experience preferred).
  • Knowledge of environmental regulations such as CERCLA, RCRA, and the Clean Water Act is beneficial.
  • Ability to obtain or maintain relevant certifications, such as OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER, within one month of hire.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite; familiarity with GIS, AutoCAD, or environmental modeling software is a plus.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and data management skills.
  • Valid driver’s license and ability to travel to field sites as needed with occasional overnight travel.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience conducting environmental sampling and field investigations.
  • Experience conducting and/or writing Phase I Environmental Site Assessments (ESAs) in accordance with ASTM standards.
  • GIT or EIT certification.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills for technical reporting and client interactions.
  • Attention to detail and ability to work both independently and in a team-oriented environment.
  • Familiarity with environmental site assessment procedures and laboratory analysis protocols.

Pay Transparency

Base compensation is expected to be in the range of $23.00 and $25.00 hourly based on skill set and experience. AET offers a comprehensive benefits package, including health benefits, insurance, Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), long term savings, paid time off, and professional development opportunities. The selected candidate must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. without requiring visa sponsorship now or in the future.


Work Environment

  • Combination of office and field settings. Fieldwork may involve exposure to varying weather conditions, rough terrain, and potential hazardous materials.
  • Must be able to wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) as required for environmental site work.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to stand; walk; use hands or fingers, handle or feel; and reach with hands and arms. The employee is occasionally required to sit; climb or balance, and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.


Third Party Disclosure

Notice to Third Party Agencies: AET does not accept unsolicited resumes from third party recruiting firms. Absent a signed Service Agreement by AET’s Chief People Officer (CPO), AET reserves the right to pursue and hire these candidates without financial obligation to recruiters or agencies.
