This includes providing program, participant, and operational support for the AmeriCorps Seniors Workforce Development Senior Demonstration Program (SDP) activities in Wheeling, West Virginia. Working both independently and collaboratively, the Program Associate partners with internal staff, community organizations, employers, training providers, and volunteers to support successful program implementation and advance workforce development goals.

Working closely with the AmeriCorps program team, the Program Associate supports AmeriCorps Seniors volunteers throughout the West Virginia Northern Panhandle, western Pennsylvania, and eastern Ohio by coordinating participant recruitment, volunteer service, training, mentoring, and employment readiness activities for adults age 55 and older. The Program Associate builds relationships with the local business community to expand workforce opportunities for older adults and support participants in obtaining permanent employment. This position emphasizes providing quality volunteer experiences and specialized training that prepare older adults for permanent employment.

About the AmeriCorps Seniors Workforce Development Senior Demonstration Program (SDP):

The AmeriCorps Seniors Workforce Development Senior Demonstration Program (SDP) is funded by AmeriCorps Seniors and supports older adults in obtaining permanent employment in skilled labor and professional careers. Grantee organizations—including NCOA—provide:

  • Training and/or certification for employment, and support such as mentorship, coaching, transportation, and other forms of support.
  • Mentoring and/or coaching in regular increments, including during pre- and post-employment placement.
  • A competitive stipend to remove barriers for older adults’ service.

Positions at this level typically report to an associate director or director and require experience supporting projects and managing tasks or deliverables. Incumbents are required to exercise judgement within their scope of work based on defined guidelines. Incumbents generally have one or more years of experience in their discipline and a bachelor’s degree or the equivalent, as well as substantive experience at this level. Graduate level degrees may be considered in lieu of experience.

*This grant-funded position is a short-term, temporary position that is funded through June 30, 2028, and designed to be filled by a W-2 employee.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Coordinate day-to-day implementation of the AmeriCorps Seniors Workforce Development Senior Demonstration Program (SDP) to support participant success and achievement of grant objectives.
  • Serve as a case manager for enrolled AmeriCorps Seniors volunteers to provide a path to successful program completion. This includes:
    • Recruiting volunteers and matching them to the appropriate volunteer station.
    • Ensuring accurate data collection and entry into the database.
    • Conducting weekly check-ins with AmeriCorps volunteers.
    • Supporting volunteers who need additional digital literacy training by providing them access to standard curriculum.
    • Enrolling volunteers in appropriate specialized training courses and coordinating any certification testing needed to support their employment objectives.
    • Identifying job opportunities for AmeriCorps Seniors volunteers who have completed their training, curriculum, and volunteer service experience and supporting their transition to permanent employment.
    • Maintaining contact with volunteers who have exited the program to follow up on and track their employment status and income.
  • Support the development and implementation of participant recruitment strategies to maintain consistent enrollment levels and a pipeline of prospective volunteers.
  • Identify appropriate volunteer training sites and maintain communication with partner organizations to support positive training and volunteer experiences for AmeriCorps Seniors volunteers.
  • Work with volunteer station partners to identify service opportunities that meet organizational needs while supporting volunteers’ employment and training goals, including opportunities for job shadowing and skill development.
  • Customize volunteer opportunities to meet the employment training needs of each volunteer and create an individualized training plan for each volunteer.
  • Monitor assigned program activities, participant data, and progress toward performance measures to support quality service delivery, achievement of grant objectives, and compliance with applicable grant and program requirements.
  • Collaborate regularly in-office with other AmeriCorps Workforce Development and Program Evaluation team members to coordinate program activities, share information, and support successful grant implementation.
  • Maintain confidentiality and comply with all applicable AmeriCorps and NCOA program standards, procedures, and data security requirements.
  • Serve as an ambassador for NCOA’s mission, programs, and social impact goals by building and maintaining positive relationships with employers, community organizations, public and private agencies, and other external stakeholders to promote awareness of AmeriCorps Seniors, workforce development initiatives, and older worker issues.
  • Participate in team meetings, work planning, trainings, community events, performance monitoring, and continuous improvement activities to support program and departmental goals.
  • Conduct site visits, attend conferences and community events, participate in partner meetings, and engage in other business travel as needed to support participant services, partner relationships, program implementation, and organizational priorities.
  • Complete required annual National Service Criminal History Check (NSCHC) training and other trainings as required by AmeriCorps and NCOA.
  • Perform other responsibilities as assigned.



PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE/QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 1-3 years of relevant experience in program coordination, program support, or a similar role required; experience in workforce development, employment and training, human services, job readiness, or a related field preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate projects, manage multiple priorities, and meet deadlines while maintaining strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to build effective relationships with participants, employers, community organizations, and other stakeholders.
  • Ability to provide participant-centered case management and support, maintain ongoing participant engagement and follow-up, and respond effectively to individual participant needs.
  • Experience supporting nonprofit or grant-funded programs, including tracking deliverables, organizing reports, monitoring activities, and assisting with day-to-day program operations, preferred.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and experience learning and utilizing web-based data management systems, such as Salesforce or similar platforms.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a collaborative, cross-functional team environment.
  • Experience working with older adults, diverse communities, minority populations, low-income communities, or other underserved populations strongly preferred.
  • Familiarity with workforce development resources and employer networks in the Northern Panhandle of West Virginia, eastern Ohio, or western Pennsylvania, including experience networking with public agencies and community organizations at the local level, preferred.
  • Ability and willingness to travel regularly throughout the service area to volunteer stations, partner sites, and community locations as needed, including occasional same-day or time-sensitive travel.

title: Director Growth Initiatives - 3 Openings
description:
How many people can answer the question, "What do you do for a living?" with the answer, "I help find cures for cancer." At Blood Cancer United, employees take our mission seriously. Whether you work in one of our regions, are an accountant at the national office or a specialist in our Information Resource Center, you work each day on making our bold goal a reality: to enable patients with blood cancer to gain more than one million years of life by 2040. Join us and give new meaning to the word, "job." Summary: Blood Cancer United is a mission centric, locally delivered and nationally powered organization, relentlessly pursuing cancer cures. To help achieve this mission, the Director, Growth Initiatives is a frontline fundraiser responsible for identifying, cultivating, securing, and retaining groups, particularly within the collegiate space, to advance fundraising and mission-driven activities. This role serves as a strategic thought partner and hands-on implementer of cultivation, engagement, and stewardship strategies designed to deepen relationships, grow participation, and achieve sustainable revenue and mission impact.

Core Responsibilities/ Primary Duties:

  • Execute a comprehensive fundraising plan, including targeted strategies for constituent cultivation, recruitment, and stewardship; conduct meaningful outreach to prospective constituents, fundraising groups, and external leaders to secure participation and support.
  • Build and manage a robust prospect pipeline in partnership with the Vice President and key stakeholders by identifying new opportunities through multiple channels and preparing compelling materials to acquire and retain fundraising groups.
  • Engage external leaders across functions to develop mutually beneficial collaborations aligned with partner objectives and Blood Cancer United goals; identify and optimize value propositions that drive mission impact and sustainable revenue growth.
  • Provide expertise, guidance, modeling, and coaching to regional teams in developing and executing account strategies, managing high-level volunteer groups, driving revenue-generating activities, and maintaining fiscal controls.
  • Serve as a strategic thought partner to the Vice President in developing plans for assigned products and initiatives, including communications, timelines, implementation approaches, and performance measures.
  • Lead and complete national campaign projects, including tool development and updates, data collection and analysis, training support, and other national initiatives.
  • Provide high-level expertise across the collegiate space to expand participation, strengthen strategic partnerships, and support campaign and mission funding needs.
  • Represent Blood Cancer United with credibility, professionalism, and mission alignment, exemplifying the One Blood Cancer United mindset and setting a standard of excellence for peers and stakeholders.
  • Achieve annual revenue targets by creating, implementing, evaluating, and adjusting personalized fundraising and account strategies.
  • Produce forecasts and projection reports by evaluating recruitment and fundraising activity, fundraising efficiency, community engagement, campaign satisfaction, and overall campaign performance.
  • Maintain a strong working knowledge of Blood Cancer United's mission, programs, and organizational priorities and support broader organizational initiatives.

Perform other related duties as assigned. Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree or advanced degree preferred.
  • Eight or more years of fundraising or sales experience, including demonstrated success engaging leaders and achieving fundraising or revenue goals.
  • Strong background in constituent recruitment, relationship management, cultivation, and stewardship.
  • Experience using a constituent relationship management system, preferably Salesforce, and proficiency with Microsoft Outlook, Word, and PowerPoint.
  • Experience in negotiation and solution-oriented problem solving.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Advanced knowledge of fundraising, sales, pipeline development, moves management, account strategy, and constituent stewardship.
  • Proven ability to create deep and meaningful prospect pipelines and develop strategic plans that convert opportunities into sustained participation and revenue.
  • Ability to lead individuals or cross-functional teams in pursuing and securing major opportunities through thoughtful account strategy, high-level relationship development, and organization-wide thinking.
  • Strong communication, presentation, organizational, analytical, and collaboration skills.
  • Ability to build and maintain trust and rapport with internal and external stakeholders and to work effectively within a highly matrixed organization.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze performance data, prepare forecasts, and adjust strategies to improve fundraising efficiency, engagement, satisfaction, and campaign outcomes.
  • Enthusiastic, self-motivated, resourceful, and committed to excellence, with the judgment to work independently while collaborating closely with colleagues.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and operate effectively in a dynamic, mission-driven environment.

Work Environment & Physical Demands

  • Weekend and evening work may be required on occasion.
  • Territory travel of approximately 25% to 50% is expected.
  • Physical demands are minimal and typical of similar roles in comparable organizations.
  • The work environment is representative and typical of similar roles in comparable organizations.

As a valued member of Blood Cancer United, you are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package. Our offerings include medical, dental, and vision insurance; life insurance; flexible spending accounts; a 403b retirement plan along with generous paid time off. In addition, we observe federal paid holidays throughout the year, and offer a wellness program and an employee assistance program.

We are excited to share the base pay range for this position is $96K to $135K. The offered compensation may vary based on factors such as geographic location, business need, market conditions, proficiencies, skills, education, and experience. title: Learning & Development Specialist (Program Manager)
description:
Hope Mission Statement

The mission of Hope the Mission is to prevent, reduce and eliminate poverty, hunger, and homelessness by offering immediate assistance and long-term solutions.

Position Purpose and Summary

Hope the Mission's frontline workforce operates in one of the most demanding environments in human services. Every shift, staff navigate trauma, de-escalation, and complex behavioral health needs in shelters serving people in crisis. How well staff are prepared for that environment determines how safe those spaces are, how long employees stay, and how effectively Hope the Mission delivers on its mission. The Program Manager, Learning and Development Specialist is the person responsible for that preparation.

Reporting to the Director of Organizational Development, the Program Manager designs, develops, and delivers training across the Hope the Mission workforce. This includes facilitating onboarding and ongoing staff development, providing shelter-specific training in trauma-informed care, de-escalation, crisis intervention, emergency procedures, and safety protocols, developing management training, creating instructional materials, tracking training completion and outcomes, and coordinating training logistics. The Program Manager collaborates with shelter managers and frontline staff to tailor content to the realities of shelter operations and works with external training vendors and subject matter experts as needed. Travel to program sites is required up to 50% of the time. This is a grant-funded position.

Staff who are undertrained don't just struggle. They leave, they make mistakes, and they sometimes cause harm. Hope the Mission's ability to retain a capable frontline workforce and deliver consistent, quality services depends in part on whether people feel equipped to do the job they were hired to do. The Program Manager builds that capacity, one training at a time, in the rooms where the work actually happens.


Responsibilities

Training Design and Development

  • Design, develop, and update training programs for frontline staff and management using adult learning principles

  • Create instructional materials including presentations, handouts, and workbooks

  • Develop training content specific to shelter operations including trauma-informed care, de-escalation techniques, understanding homelessness, crisis intervention, emergency procedures, and safety protocols

  • Liaise with subject matter experts regarding instructional design

  • Stay current on training design methodologies and best practices

Training Delivery and Facilitation

  • Deliver live and on-demand training programs using a range of facilitation methods including role-playing, simulations, team exercises, group discussions, videos, and lectures

  • Facilitate onboarding training for new staff

  • Provide ongoing training for existing staff across programs and departments

  • Offer site-based training for program teams at shelter and program locations

  • Develop and facilitate management and leadership training programs

Vendor and External Coordination

  • Identify appropriate external training vendors for organizational needs

  • Coordinate and liaise with external subject matter experts as needed

Logistics, Tracking, and Reporting

  • Handle all logistics for training activities including venues, schedules, and equipment

  • Manage and maintain in-house training facilities and equipment

  • Track and report on training completion rates and outcomes

  • Attend meetings and seminars to gather information for use in training programs or to update leadership on training program status

Collaboration and Continuous Improvement

  • Collaborate with shelter managers and frontline staff to tailor training content to the specific needs and challenges of shelter operations

  • Assist with identifying training gaps and developing solutions to address them

  • Perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Behavioral Science, Education, Human Services, or a related field required

  • Minimum 2 years of training experience required

  • Experience in homeless services, social services, or a related field preferred

  • Bilingual in English and Spanish preferred

Skills

  • Design and facilitate training programs using adult learning principles across diverse staff populations

  • Facilitate live training sessions with strong public speaking and group engagement skills

  • Develop instructional materials including slide presentations, handouts, and participant workbooks

  • Tailor training content to the specific needs and challenges of shelter and human services environments

  • Track training completion data and report outcomes to leadership

  • Manage multiple training projects and deadlines simultaneously with strong organizational skills

  • Work autonomously and take initiative with minimal supervision

  • Communicate clearly and professionally in writing and verbally with staff, managers, and external partners

  • Adapt to a fast-paced, constantly changing environment

  • Proficient in Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, and other common web-based applications

Mandatory Requirements

  • Background Screening – Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of background checks as required per worksite.

  • Drug and Alcohol Testing – Candidates must pass pre-employment and ongoing drug and alcohol screenings in accordance with company policy.

  • Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) Check – For roles requiring driving, employment is contingent upon an acceptable driving record.

  • Legal Eligibility to Work – Candidates must provide proof of legal authorization to work in the US.

  • Compliance with Company Policies and HIPAA standards – All employees must comply with company policies, including safety, confidentiality, and conduct standards.

  • Must have reliable transportation..

  • Must have proof of vehicle insurance coverage.

  • Must have a valid CA drivers license.

  • Ability to travel 25% of working hours


Physical, Demands, Environmental Conditions, Equipment

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential job functions. The employee is required to: walk and climb stairs; stand, bend, squat, climb, kneel, and twist on an intermittent or sometimes continuous basis; grasp, push, pull objects such as files, file cabinet drawers, and reach overhead; handle, finger, grasp and feel objects and equipment; reach with hands and arms; be mobile by moving oneself from place to place quickly and easily; repeat various motions with the wrists, hands, and fingers; be able to perform visual activities for (including, but not limited to) administrative and clerical tasks; ability to lift up to 25 lbs.; communicate, receive and exchange ideas, information by means of the spoken and written word; drive vehicles in and around Los Angeles County; be able to enter various buildings that may require climbing stairs; be periodically subjected to outside environmental conditions. The employee may work in proximity to service animals and emotional support animals; use a desktop and/or laptop computer; various office machines. Complete all required forms in personal writing.


Work Environment

The employee may be in contact with individuals and families in crisis who may be ill, using alcohol and drugs, and who may not be attentive to basic personal hygiene, health and safety practices. The employee may experience a number of unpleasant sensory demands associated with the participants’ use of alcohol and drugs, and lack of personal hygiene. The employee must be ready to respond quickly and effectively to many types of situations, including crisis situations and potentially hostile situations. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate in an office setting. Sometimes work may become stressful when working under pressure or in crisis intervention.

In addition to federal law requirements, HTM complies with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment in every location in which the company has facilities. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, placement, promotion, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

HTM will consider qualified applicants with a criminal history pursuant to the California Fair Chance Act. You do not need to disclose your criminal history or participate in a background check until a conditional job offer is made to you. After making a conditional offer and running a background check, if HTM is concerned about a conviction that is directly related to the job, you will be given the chance to explain the circumstances surrounding the conviction, provide mitigating evidence, or challenge the accuracy of the background report. title: Senior Robotics Software Engineer (Zürich, 100%)
description:
We are hiring a Robotics SWE

⏰ Start date: ASAP

📍Zürich, Switzerland (on-site, remote not possible)

🦾 Full-time (100%)

💼 Your role

Deploying robots means more than training the latest policy. As a robotics SWE, you will work across the stack and define how developers, operators, and customers interact with our product. You know that a hardware abstraction layer and subsystem APIs are the foundation to a system in which a growing team of engineers can contribute without slowing down and that doesn't break when hardware changes. You value delivering a polished product just as much as building a reliable, maintainable system.

What you'll be doing:

  • Develop the robotics stack from low-level drivers and behavior trees to health management and software configuration

  • Implement data and telemetry ingestion from the robots to the cloud

  • Build internal tools such as a teleoperation interface, robot fleet management, and data dashboard

  • Build classical robotics autonomy pipelines such as 3D mapping, localization, and autonomous navigation

  • Drive CI/CD pipelines, test frameworks, and developer tooling. You will establish practices ranging from memory safety to architectural guidelines

🤖 You

What you should have:

  • 3+ years in a professional SWE environment, preferably in Robotics, Automotive, or Aerospace

  • Strong modern C++ experience and experience in Python

  • Solid fundamentals of Linux such as systemd, time synchronization, schedulers and networking fundamentals (TCP/UDP)

  • Experience in debugging complex issues using core dumps, debuggers (gdb), and application profiling (perf, ftrace)

  • Experience in test automation (unit tests, integration tests)

  • Worked on embedded platforms and sensor integration

These skills are a plus:

  • Experience in Rust, ROS2, or Zenoh

  • Experience with hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) and simulation-in-the-loop (SIL) testing

  • Experience with NVIDIA Jetson

  • Experience in common robotics algorithms (SLAM, pointcloud processing, control theory, computer vision)

As the first dedicated robotics SWE, you will have a massive impact on our engineering culture. As the team grows, you can remain a high-impact generalist and work across all layers of abstraction or specialize and lead individual subsystems.

Don't worry if you don't hit every check-mark. We value engineers who care about building great products and can learn to get things working. Just give it a go and apply.

title: Client Service Monitor
description:
Hope Mission Statement

The mission of Hope the Mission is to prevent, reduce and eliminate poverty, hunger, and homelessness by offering immediate assistance and long-term solutions.

Position Purpose and Summary

The Client Services Monitor (CSM) works directly on-site and is responsible for keeping participants safe, supporting daily operations, community standards and helping Hope the Mission's Interim Housing programs run smoothly. The CSM plays an important role in creating an environment that is safe, structured, and respectful — one where every participant is treated with dignity and fairness.

This position requires someone who shows up consistently, uses good judgment, and genuinely cares about serving people experiencing homelessness. Many participants in our programs have been through long periods of instability, crisis, and trauma. When a CSM shows up with calm, care, and compassion, it creates a sense of safety and routine that participants can count on as they work toward stable housing.

The CSM reports to the Program Manager or Assistant Program Manager and works alongside site staff to make sure the program runs well, meets contract requirements, and reflects Hope the Mission's values in every interaction.


Primary Duties and Responsibilities

Facility Maintenance and Sanitation

  • Assists with and facilitates routine cleaning of all facility areas to maintain cleanliness, safety, and operational readiness

  • Cleans and disinfects restrooms and shower areas after each use, without exception. Maintains sanitary and safe restroom and sink conditions at all times. Completes deep cleaning of restrooms and common areas.

  • Monitors and maintains hygiene areas and community areas; ensures resources are fully stocked, replenishing as needed.

  • Washes, dries, and prepares towels used for restroom and shower services

  • Monitors laundry rooms, restrooms, and common areas to ensure cleanliness and appropriate use

  • Maintains accurate shower and restroom usage logs

Participant Safety and Monitoring

  • Conducts required wellness checks each shift to ensure participant safety and well-being

  • Monitors participant movement, common areas, and site activity to promote safety and program compliance

  • Conducts routine site walk-throughs and safety checks during assigned shifts

  • Supports contraband control and safety procedures in accordance with agency policy

  • Responds to incidents and emergencies using trauma-informed de-escalation techniques and follows all incident reporting protocols

  • Supports emergency responses — including medical emergencies, overdoses, and evacuations — until leadership or first responders arrive

Participant Services and Engagement

  • Provides direct, respectful assistance to participants, including answering questions, responding to requests, and connecting participants to appropriate staff or resources

  • Assists with participant intake, orientation, and explanation of site guidelines as directed by management

  • Distributes hygiene supplies including soap, shampoo, towels, and related items to participants as needed

  • Supports meal service, supply distribution, and general operational duties as assigned

Documentation and Reporting

  • Completes Daily Activity Reports (DARs) accurately, objectively, and in a timely manner

  • Conducts intake, exit, and case notes in HMIS where applicable

  • Assists with documentation related to participant movements, wellness concerns, or incidents as required

  • Observes and reports safety concerns, maintenance issues, guideline violations, and unusual occurrences to site leadership promptly

Shift Operations

  • Provides support during shift pass-downs and communicates relevant updates between shifts

  • Provides overnight, evening, weekend, or holiday coverage as scheduled

  • Performs other duties as assigned

Transportation (Site Specific)

  • Transports participants to and from established routes and as directed by a supervisor

  • Maintains vehicle cleanliness inside and out at all times

  • Ensures the vehicle has sufficient fuel before and during each shift

  • Completes daily vehicle maintenance checks and reports any issues to the supervisors

  • Logs all mileage accurately and in accordance with departmental procedures

Skills

  • Strong observation and situational awareness skills

  • Trauma-informed communication and de-escalation techniques

  • Ability to maintain professional boundaries with participants

  • Clear, objective, and professional written documentation skills

  • Ability to follow policies, procedures, and chain of command

  • Strong teamwork and communication skills

  • Basic computer and email proficiency

  • Ability to lead with integrity and uphold organizational mission, values, and service philosophy.

  • Ability to cultivate and maintain collaborative relationships with community-based organizations and external service providers. Strong Interpersonal Skills.

  • Maintains professionalism, empathy, and sound decision-making when working in complex or emotionally challenging environments.


Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED required

  • Previous experience in homeless services, shelter operations or social service preferred

  • Knowledge of trauma-informed care and harm reduction principles preferred

  • Ability to work flexible schedules including nights, weekends, and holidays


Mandatory Requirements

  • Background Screening – Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of background checks as required per worksite.

  • Drug and Alcohol Testing – Candidates must pass pre-employment and ongoing drug and alcohol screenings in accordance with company policy.

  • Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) Check – For roles requiring driving, employment is contingent upon an acceptable driving record.

  • Legal Eligibility to Work – Candidates must provide proof of legal authorization to work in the US.

  • Compliance with Company Policies and HIPAA standards – All employees must comply with company policies, including safety, confidentiality, and conduct standards.


Physical, Demands, Environmental Conditions, Equipment

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential job functions. The employee is required to: walk and climb stairs; stand, bend, squat, climb, kneel, and twist on an intermittent or sometimes continuous basis; grasp, push, pull objects such as files, file cabinet drawers, and reach overhead; handle, finger, grasp and feel objects and equipment; reach with hands and arms; be mobile by moving oneself from place to place quickly and easily; repeat various motions with the wrists, hands, and fingers; be able to perform visual activities for (including, but not limited to) administrative and clerical tasks; ability to lift up to 25 lbs.; communicate, receive and exchange ideas, information by means of the spoken and written word; drive vehicles in and around Los Angeles County; be able to enter various buildings that may require climbing stairs; be periodically subjected to outside environmental conditions. The employee may work in proximity to service animals and emotional support animals; use a desktop and/or laptop computer; various office machines. Complete all required forms in personal writing.


Work Environment

The employee may be in contact with individuals and families in crisis who may be ill, using alcohol and drugs, and who may not be attentive to basic personal hygiene, health and safety practices. The employee may experience a number of unpleasant sensory demands associated with the participants’ use of alcohol and drugs, and lack of personal hygiene. The employee must be ready to respond quickly and effectively to many types of situations, including crisis situations and potentially hostile situations. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate in an office setting. Sometimes work may become stressful when working under pressure or in crisis intervention. .

SiTime is the Precision Timing company.


Timing is the heartbeat of all electronics, ensuring performance, resilience and scalability. With more than 4 billion devices shipped, SiTime is changing the timing industry. For more information, visit: www.sitime.com.


Job Summary

  • We are seeking a hands-on Senior PCB Layout Engineer to own the physical implementation of complex printed circuit boards used in characterization, validation, automated test equipment (ATE), production test, and internal engineering platforms. This role partners closely with hardware, signal integrity, mechanical, manufacturing, and test engineers to translate schematics and design constraints into robust, manufacturable PCB layouts. The ideal candidate brings at least 10 years of practical layout experience, strong design judgment, and a proven record of releasing high-quality boards from placement through fabrication and assembly.

It is not necessary to meet all job requirements to be a qualified candidate for the position.

Responsibilities:

PCB Placement, Routing, and Release Ownership

  • Own PCB layout from initial placement and routing through design review, fabrication release, assembly support, and post-build updates
  • Translate schematics, mechanical requirements, stack-ups, and electrical constraints into complete board layouts
  • Route dense mixed-signal, high-speed digital, precision analog, RF, clock, power, and control circuitry.
  • Create and maintain fabrication and assembly deliverables, including Gerber or ODB++ data, drill files, drawings, pick-and-place files, and manufacturing notes
  • Perform thorough design-rule checks and release-package reviews to ensure data accuracy and completeness

Constraint Management and Design Quality

  • Implement controlled-impedance routing, differential pairs, length matching, return-path continuity, isolation, shielding, grounding, and power-distribution requirements
  • Collaborate with electrical and SI/PI engineers to apply routing constraints and incorporate simulation or review feedback
  • Develop practical placement and routing strategies for high-density interconnect, fine-pitch BGA, via-in-pad, blind and buried vias, and other advanced PCB technologies
  • Maintain component footprints, padstacks, symbols, and library data in accordance with IPC guidance and company standards
  • Conduct peer reviews and contribute to PCB layout checklists, standards, templates, and reusable design practices

Manufacturing and Cross-Functional Execution

  • Drive DFM, DFA, and DFT reviews with PCB fabrication, assembly, test, and supply-chain partners
  • Resolve fabrication and assembly questions, document deviations, and incorporate lessons learned into future layouts
  • Work closely with mechanical engineers on board outlines, component clearances, keep-outs, connector locations, thermal constraints, and enclosure integration
  • Support prototype bring-up and root-cause analysis by reviewing layout-related signal, power, thermal, assembly, and reliability issues
  • Communicate design status, trade-offs, risks, and release readiness clearly to project stakeholders

Qualifications & Requirements (Education must be included):

  • 10+ years of hands-on PCB layout experience for complex, high-density electronic systems
  • Expert-level capability in at least one major PCB layout platform, such as Cadence Allegro, Altium Designer, and working familiarity across common PCB design and review tools
  • Demonstrated experience laying out multi-layer high-speed digital, mixed-signal, precision analog, RF, clock, and power designs
  • Strong knowledge of PCB stack-ups, materials, controlled impedance, differential routing, length matching, crosstalk mitigation, return paths, grounding, and power integrity fundamentals
  • Experience with fine-pitch BGAs, HDI, microvias, via-in-pad, blind/buried vias
  • Practical knowledge of PCB fabrication, assembly processes, component land patterns, solder-mask and paste-mask design, panelization, tolerances, and manufacturing documentation
  • Experience applying DFM, DFA, and DFT principles and working directly with fabrication and assembly suppliers
  • Ability to interpret schematics, mechanical drawings, PCB specifications, component datasheets, and constraint documents
  • Strong attention to detail, configuration discipline, and ability to manage multiple board releases and design revisions
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively across engineering and manufacturing teams

Desired Characteristics & Attributes:

  • Bachelor’s degree, technical certification, or equivalent practical experience in electronics, electrical engineering, PCB design, or a related field
  • Experience with boards used for semiconductor characterization, validation, ATE, production test, probe, or laboratory instrumentation
  • Familiarity with SI/PI review or simulation tools and the ability to interpret analysis results and implement layout changes
  • Knowledge of IPC-2221, IPC-7351, IPC-6012, IPC-A-600, IPC-A-610, or related PCB design and workmanship standards
  • Experience mentoring other PCB designers and improving layout libraries, workflows, checklists, or release processes
  • Experience with rigid-flex designs, thermal management, high-current power delivery, low-noise clocking, or low-jitter systems

description:

POSITION SUMMARY INFORMATION: DUTIES AND REQUIREMENTS


Job Summary: The Chief Medical Officer (CMO), Detention Operations is responsible for providing enterprise-wide physician leadership, clinical governance, and quality oversight for GardaWorld Federal Services' (GWFS) government agency healthcare programs. Reporting directly to the Senior Director, Medical Programs, the CMO serves as the clinical authority for detention healthcare operations and ensures the delivery of high-quality, patient-centered, and compliant healthcare services across all federal detention facilities supported by GWFS.

The incumbent is responsible for strategic clinical leadership, operational oversight, regulatory compliance, healthcare quality management, patient safety initiatives, workforce support, and medical program performance. The CMO ensures healthcare services are delivered in accordance with contractual requirements, National Detention Standards (NDS), Performance-Based National Detention Standards (PBNDS), accreditation standards, applicable federal and state regulations, evidence-based medical practices, and organizational policies. The position serves as the principal medical advisor for federal healthcare operations and works collaboratively with government stakeholders, facility leadership, and multidisciplinary healthcare teams to promote operational excellence and continuous improvement.


Duties/Responsibilities:

  • Provide executive physician leadership and oversight for all GWFS government agency Medical Operations programs.
  • Serve as the principal medical advisor regarding healthcare operations, clinical quality, patient safety, regulatory compliance, and strategic medical initiatives.
  • Establish, implement, and maintain enterprise-wide clinical policies, procedures, treatment protocols, and standards of care.
  • Monitor healthcare operations to ensure compliance with National Detention Standards (NDS), Performance-Based National Detention Standards (PBNDS), HIPAA requirements, federal regulations, accreditation standards, and contractual obligations.
  • Oversee clinical quality management, peer review, utilization management, infection prevention, patient safety, and risk management programs.
  • Review and evaluate healthcare outcomes, mortality reviews, sentinel events, serious incident reports, clinical audits, and corrective action plans.
  • Identify operational risks and implement strategies to improve clinical quality, regulatory compliance, healthcare efficiency, and patient outcomes.
  • Conduct executive-level site visits, operational reviews, compliance assessments, and program evaluations across healthcare operations.
  • Collaborate with corporate medical leadership to address clinical, operational, staffing, quality, and compliance challenges.
  • Serve as the senior medical representative in interactions with government agency Headquarters, Contracting Officers, Contracting Officer Representatives (CORs), accreditation organizations, and government stakeholders.
  • Support audits, inspections, accreditation surveys, government reviews, and contract performance evaluations.
  • Monitor healthcare staffing models and workforce readiness to support operational continuity and contractual compliance.
  • Provide strategic oversight of physician recruitment, credentialing, privileging, retention, succession planning, and provider performance management.
  • Develop and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs), healthcare dashboards, quality metrics, and operational performance measures.
  • Prepare executive reports, clinical analyses, medical summaries, performance reviews, and strategic recommendations.
  • Support business development initiatives, proposal efforts, capture activities, program transitions, and healthcare growth opportunities.
  • Promote a culture of professionalism, accountability, evidence-based practice, continuous improvement, and patient-centered care.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.


Required Education, Certifications, Licenses, and Experience:

  • Doctor of Medicine (MD) or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO) degree from an accredited medical school in the United States or its territories, or from a foreign medical school providing education and medical knowledge equivalent to an accredited U.S. medical school, as established by the National Committee on Foreign Medical Education and Accreditation. Graduates of foreign medical schools must maintain permanent certification by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG).
  • Current board certification in Internal Medicine, Family Medicine, Preventive Medicine/Preventive Health, Emergency Medicine, or another relevant clinical specialty. Board certification in Internal Medicine, Family Medicine, or Preventive Medicine is preferred.
  • Minimum of ten (10) years of post-residency clinical practice experience, including at least six (6) years providing direct patient care as a physician.
  • Minimum of seven (7) years of progressive physician leadership experience overseeing healthcare operations, medical staff, clinical programs, quality management, or multi-site healthcare delivery systems, including at least three (3) years providing clinical supervision and leadership to physicians, other medical professionals, and ancillary clinical staff.
  • Current, full, and unrestricted license to practice medicine in at least one U.S. state or territory. The physician must obtain and maintain an unrestricted license in each state where the physician is assigned to provide patient care or exercise clinical authority when required by applicable law or contract.
  • Current Basic Life Support for Healthcare Providers certification through the American Heart Association, or the ability to obtain the certification before beginning clinical duties.
  • Current DEA registration or the ability to obtain and maintain all registrations necessary for the assigned responsibilities and practice locations.
  • Demonstrated experience in detention healthcare, correctional healthcare, federal healthcare programs, public health systems, or comparable complex healthcare environments.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain all required government clearances, facility credentials, and contractual qualifications.
  • Ability to provide proof of U.S. citizenship or legal authorization to work in the United States.
  • Must consent to fingerprinting, background investigations, and any other required suitability or security screening.
  • Must be able to read, write, speak, and understand English proficiently.
  • Extensive knowledge of detention healthcare operations, correctional healthcare practices, and federal healthcare programs.
  • Thorough understanding of National Detention Standards (NDS), Performance-Based National Detention Standards (PBNDS), federal healthcare requirements, and applicable regulatory standards.
  • Knowledge of quality assurance, performance improvement, peer review, infection prevention, patient safety, and risk management principles.
  • Strong executive leadership and physician management skills.
  • Ability to evaluate healthcare operations, clinical performance, staffing effectiveness, and compliance indicators across multiple facilities.
  • Strong analytical, critical thinking, decision-making, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and presentation communication abilities.
  • Ability to effectively engage executive leadership, government officials, healthcare providers, accreditation organizations, and operational personnel.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including PowerPoint, Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams.
  • Ability to analyze healthcare data, identify trends, and develop strategic recommendations.
  • Strong organizational, project management, and leadership skills.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise sound medical judgment in complex operational environments.
  • Ability to travel extensively and provide support across geographically dispersed healthcare programs.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Prior experience serving as a Chief Medical Officer, Corporate Medical Director, National Medical Director, Regional Medical Director, or equivalent executive physician leadership role.
  • Experience supporting government agencies through other federal healthcare programs.
  • Master of Public Health (MPH), Master of Healthcare Administration (MHA), Master of Business Administration (MBA), or related advanced degree.
  • Experience with ACA, NCCHC, Joint Commission, or other healthcare accreditation standards.
  • Experience managing healthcare services across multiple detention facilities or federal healthcare contracts.
  • Experience supporting healthcare contract mobilizations, transitions, and business growth initiatives.

title: Clinical Integrations Interface Analyst
description:
Job Description Summary

‎

Clinical Integrations Interface Analyst is responsible for the analysis, development, implementation, monitoring, and support of healthcare data interfaces that enable reliable exchange of clinical and operational information across systems.

This role partners with clinical, operational, product, engineering, and vendor teams to translate integration requirements into scalable interface solutions. The analyst supports interoperability between electronic health record (EHR) systems, laboratory and diagnostic platforms, health information exchanges, third-party clinical applications, and internal technology platforms.

‎

How will you make an impact & Requirements

‎

Key Responsibilities

Interface Development & Implementation

  • Analyze business, clinical, and technical requirements for new healthcare integrations.
  • Design, configure, test, implement, and maintain interfaces between clinical systems and external partners.
  • Develop and support interfaces using healthcare interoperability standards such as HL7 v2, FHIR, CDA/CCD, X12, and APIs.
  • Perform interface mapping, transformation, filtering, routing, and data validation.
  • Configure and support interface engines and integration platforms.
  • Coordinate interface testing, including unit testing, integrated testing, user acceptance testing, and production validation.
  • Support new customer, partner, facility, and vendor implementations from requirements gathering through go-live.

Production Support & Monitoring

  • Monitor interface queues, message processing, system alerts, and data exchange performance.
  • Investigate and resolve failed, delayed, duplicated, or incorrectly formatted messages.
  • Perform root-cause analysis for integration incidents and implement corrective and preventive solutions.
  • Troubleshoot issues across source systems, interface engines, APIs, networks, and receiving applications.
  • Coordinate resolution of complex interface issues with internal engineering teams, EHR vendors, laboratories, health systems, and other external partners.
  • Participate in production support and incident-management processes as required.

Clinical Data & Workflow Analysis

  • Understand clinical workflows and how data moves between healthcare applications.
  • Analyze HL7 message structures and clinical data elements, including:
    • ADT
    • ORM
    • ORU
    • SIU
    • MDM
    • DFT
    • ACK
  • Validate patient demographics, encounters, providers, orders, results, diagnoses, medications, and other clinical information across integrated systems.
  • Identify data-quality issues and work with stakeholders to establish appropriate remediation processes.
  • Ensure integrations support downstream clinical and operational workflows accurately and consistently.

Integration Documentation & Governance

  • Develop and maintain interface specifications, data mappings, workflow diagrams, testing documentation, configuration records, and troubleshooting procedures.
  • Maintain an accurate inventory of interfaces, endpoints, dependencies, and integration configurations.
  • Document implementation decisions, known limitations, and operational support procedures.
  • Follow established change-management, release-management, security, and integration governance processes.
  • Contribute to the development of reusable interface standards, implementation templates, and integration best practices.

Stakeholder & Vendor Collaboration

  • Serve as a technical liaison between clinical operations, product teams, engineering teams, customers, and external vendors.
  • Facilitate interface discovery and technical requirements discussions.
  • Communicate technical issues and integration concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Coordinate interface implementation activities, testing schedules, production cutovers, and post-go-live validation.
  • Manage technical dependencies and escalate risks that may affect implementation timelines or production stability.

title: Part-Time Senior Backend Engineer
description:
Concorde digitalizes heavy-industry operations, from plant-floor reports to enterprise-grade AI architecture.

Programs & partners

About the team

Concorde Systems is building the intelligence infrastructure for Indonesianindustry, starting with a Computerized Maintenance Management System thathelps industrial teams manage assets and heavy machinery, prevent downtime,and run maintenance operations end to end. We are currently running a liveenterprise pilot at a national plant.

The system you would work on is Concorde Station, our multi-tenant CMMS:organizations use it to track physical assets, run work orders andprocedures, manage parts inventory, and report on maintenance. Our firstpaying client is being onboarded this quarter.

About the role

This is a part-time contract, 20 hours per week from September throughDecember 2026, with the scope fixed before you start. The domain model isstrong: a polymorphic audit-event table, an atomic parts ledger, a workingforms state machine, and seventeen live domains. The system itself, however,is still a prototype: there is no test suite, no CI, and no deploymentpipeline yet. This contract exists to change that.

To set expectations, the role is not: ownership of the full roadmap, arewrite (the architecture is sound and stays), a move to microservices,Kubernetes, or an event bus, or a frontend rebuild (the design system iscomplete).

The stack is Go 1.25 with chi v5, pgx v5, and sqlc on PostgreSQL 16 atSupabase. There is no ORM and there will not be one: SQL is written by handand compiled to type-safe Go. The frontend is Next.js 14, TypeScript, andTailwind. CI/CD from scratch and Supabase operations can be learned on thego.

What you'll do

  • Write the detailed specs together with us before you start
  • Stand up the first CI pipeline and the first real test suite for the API
  • Containerize the service and get a working staging-to-production deploy process running
  • Wire up the RBAC checks that are already fully modeled in the database but enforced nowhere in code

What we're looking for

  • Available and willing to work from September through December 2026 (contract)
  • Real experience writing Go, including at least one HTTP service you personally deployed
  • Comfortable with raw SQL
  • Willing to set up a CI pipeline and a deployment process from scratch
  • Able to read and reason carefully about authorization logic; carefulness matters more than years of experience
  • Enough TypeScript to write a Next.js Server Action against an existing design system; no design work is involved
  • A computer science or electrical engineering background
  • Exposure to Supabase
  • Anything you have shipped and kept alive past the demo

Compensation

This is a paid part-time position: Rp 7.200.000 per month for 20 hours perweek, negotiable and can be discussed.

Beyond the rate: access to premium AI coding tools (Claude), a real, liveproduction system to point to afterward, the opportunity to grow this into along-term partnership, an official certificate or letter of recommendation,hands-on experience building a real tech startup, access to startup networks,communities, and industry practitioners, and flexible onsite workspace accessin Bandung, remote friendly.

Equal opportunity

We do not discriminate on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, or any other status protected by applicable Indonesian law. If you need an adjustment at any stage of the process, whether that is a different interview format, more time, an accessible location, tell us and we will arrange it. Asking for one is never held against you.

How we handle your application

We collect what you send us on this form: your name, contact details, the files you upload, the links you provide, and anything you write in the free-text fields. G&W Products | Fairfield, OH Warehouse

title: Principal Engineer, Test Development
description:
About SiTime


SiTime is the Precision Timing company.


Timing is the heartbeat of all electronics, ensuring performance, resilience and scalability. For decades, quartz devices, non-silicon technology, have kept systems in sync, but they struggle in harsher, more demanding environments. MEMS-based Precision Timing delivers greater accuracy, smaller size and resilience. Today, MEMS timing powers over 400 applications, including high-growth ones in AI datacenters, automated driving, industrial and humanoid robots, wearables and IoT.


Our semiconductor MEMS programmable solutions offer a rich feature set that enables customers to differentiate their products with higher performance, smaller size, lower power, and better reliability. With more than 4 billion devices shipped, SiTime is changing the timing industry. For more information, visit: www.sitime.com.


Job Summary

The Principal Test Development Engineer is the main focal point in the development of a test solution, capable of deciding the technical direction and strategy of the test design and its implementation. He is responsible for developing hardware and software solutions for SiTime’s precision timing devices. From the initial product development kickoff through end-of-life, the ATE Test Development Engineer defines ATE test hardware and software and supports the launch of new products into high-volume production. This includes board-level hardware design, algorithm development, software implementation, and validation on both custom and standard automated test equipment (ATE) platforms.

Responsibilities:

Test Solution Development

  • Define the ATE test flow and test plan for new products
  • Engage with design team on Design for Test (DFT) features
  • Develop, validate, and release production test software for standard mixed-signal ATE platforms such as Teradyne Eagle Test Systems (ETS-88).
  • Provide critical inputs in the development of the test hardware from block diagram definition, schematic drafting, layout considerations, assembly, and verification.
  • Support new product introduction (NPI) activities by developing test methodologies and qualification or characterization plans.
  • Participate in test program debugging, optimization, and correlation activities.
  • Improve test coverage, test time efficiency, and manufacturability to support high-volume production.
  • Lead release-to-production activities, including support for high-volume production.

Test Hardware & System Integration

  • Assist in the design, validation, and qualification of DUT boards, interface hardware, load boards, and test fixtures.
  • Support hardware bring-up, system integration, and debugging activities.
  • Perform tester-to-tester, site-to-site, and platform correlation studies.
  • Conduct engineering evaluations and characterize test system performance.

Validation & Change Management

  • Support validation of hardware and software changes for test systems.
  • Execute qualification plans and document results for test releases.
  • Ensure all changes comply with engineering and quality requirements.
  • Maintain test documentation, procedures, and release records.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with Product Engineering, Design Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Equipment Engineering, and OSAT partners.
  • Support technical discussions, design reviews, and test strategy development.
  • Participate in problem-solving and continuous improvement initiatives across manufacturing operations.

Technical Leadership

  • Serve as the technical lead of a project, providing guidance and assistance in technical discussions
  • Mentor and train junior engineers, associates, and technicians


Qualifications & Requirements:

  • Minimum of a BS degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent experience.
  • At least eight years of related work experience as an individual contributor focusing on key technical areas.
  • Background in ATE development for mixed-signal ICs, including hands-on experience with ATE platforms such as Teradyne's ETS-364, ETS-88, or UltraFLEX is preferred but not required.
  • Knowledge of analog electronics and experience with board-level troubleshooting and debugging.
  • Experience in statistical analysis of test data.
  • Hands-on experience with electronics lab instrumentation; prior experience with metrology systems for evaluating timing parameters is preferred but not required.
  • Excellent programming skills and prior experience with C++.

It is not necessary to meet all job requirements to be a qualified candidate for the position.

Desired Characteristics & Attributes:

  • High level of self-motivation and drive to make an impact.
  • Strong interpersonal and mentorship skills for engineers on the team.
  • Strong sense of ownership, drive for results, and ability to bring items to the finish line.
  • Strong interest in being hands-on in the lab.
  • Ability and willingness to work in a highly collaborative, fast-paced team environment.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Positive attitude and motivation to learn new skills.

Compensation Range:

At SiTime, we believe great work deserves great rewards. We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive compensation package designed to attract top talent.


In addition to base salary, this role is eligible for a quarterly bonus tied to the achievement of innovation goals—reflecting our commitment to recognizing meaningful impact. We also offer equity grants, providing a meaningful opportunity to share in the company’s future growth and success.


SiTime is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We treat each person fairly and we do not tolerate discrimination or harassment against anyone on the basis of any protected characteristics, including race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, pregnancy, political affiliation, protected veteran status, protected genetic information, or marital status or other characteristics protected by law. SiTime participates in the E-Verify program.

title: Union - Foreperson w/ CDL (UVM) (Oregon)
description:
ABOUT ARBORWORKS, LLC

ArborWorks LLC is a nationwide leader in professional vegetation management, specializing in utility line clearance, fire remediation, and large-scale environmental projects. Established in 2003, we have built a reputation for quality and safety by leveraging advanced mechanized equipment and a skilled team of dedicated professionals. Guided by a commitment to innovation, safety, and superior customer service, ArborWorks prides itself on an exceptional safety culture, recognized through industry-leading third-party ratings.


Whether you’re looking to grow your career or contribute your expertise, ArborWorks offers a dynamic environment where team members are valued, and professional growth is a priority. We are passionate about creating safe communities and delivering excellence in every project.


JOB OVERVIEW: FOREPERSON – UTILITY VEGETATION MANAGEMENT (UVM)

The Foreperson – Utility Vegetation Management (UVM) is a frontline leadership position responsible for directing daily field operations for a single vegetation management crew performing utility line clearance and related work. The role exists to ensure work is executed safely, efficiently, and in compliance with utility requirements, regulatory standards, and ArborWorks operating procedures.


As the primary on‑site leader, the Foreperson provides hands‑on direction, coordinates crew activities, and maintains accountability for safety performance, work quality, and daily production. The position serves as a critical link between field crews and management by translating work plans into consistent execution while supporting public safety, system reliability, and wildfire risk mitigation efforts.


JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

Crew Leadership & Job Site Oversight:

  • Lead and direct a single field crew performing utility vegetation management work.
  • Assign daily tasks, coordinate work activities, and monitor job progress throughout the workday.
  • Provide clear direction and on‑the‑job instruction to crew members.
  • Maintain accountability for crew conduct, attendance, and adherence to company expectations.
  • Lead by example to promote professionalism, teamwork, and a strong safety culture.

Field Operations & Work Execution:

  • Perform vegetation management work as required, including tree trimming, climbing, rigging, and ground operations.
  • Operate chainsaws, chippers, and other equipment for clearing, bucking, and limbing activities.
  • Set up job sites, establish work zones, and coordinate traffic control when applicable.
  • Ensure proper handling, cleanup, and disposal of vegetation debris.
  • Participate in pre‑job planning, daily tailboards, and job briefings.

Safety & Regulatory Compliance:

  • Enforce compliance with OSHA, ANSI Z133, utility requirements, and ArborWorks safety policies.
  • Conduct job‑site safety checks and address unsafe conditions or behaviors immediately.
  • Ensure crew members use and maintain required personal protective equipment (PPE).
  • Respond to incidents, near‑misses, or property damage events and report them per company procedures.
  • Reinforce corrective actions and safety expectations with crew members.

Equipment, Vehicles & Asset Accountability:

  • Perform routine inspections of vehicles, tools, and equipment prior to use.
  • Ensure equipment is operated safely and maintained in proper working condition.
  • Report equipment issues, maintenance needs, or damage promptly.
  • Maintain accountability for crew‑assigned vehicles, tools, and equipment.

Quality, Documentation & Communication:

  • Ensure completed work meets utility specifications, trim standards, and ArborWorks quality expectations.
  • Conduct post‑work inspections to confirm job completion and quality.
  • Complete required job documentation, including production reporting, timekeeping, and daily records.
  • Communicate professionally with customers, property owners, inspectors, and utility representatives on site.
  • Escalate customer concerns or operational issues to management as appropriate.



REQUIREMENTS & QUALIFICATIONS

Education:

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.

Experience:

  • Minimum of 12 months of utility line clearance or vegetation management experience.
  • Prior experience in a lead, senior trimmer, or crew‑level leadership role preferred.

Skills & Abilities:

  • Ability to lead and coordinate a field crew in a safety‑critical environment.
  • Working knowledge of utility vegetation management practices and equipment.
  • Ability to perform physically demanding work for extended periods.
  • Strong verbal communication skills for crew leadership and customer interaction.
  • Ability to follow work plans, prioritize tasks, and adapt to changing field conditions.

Licenses / Certifications:

  • CDL A Required.
  • DOT Medical Examiner’s Certificate (Form MCSA‑5876), where applicable.
  • CPR and First Aid Certification (required within 90 days of hire).

Required Training:

  • Groundperson Training
  • Aerial Rescue Training
  • Tree Feller Training
  • Equipment operation proficiency certifications (as applicable)
  • Successful completion of the Foreperson assessment with a minimum score of 70%


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Applicator or Sprayer License (or willingness to obtain within 90 days of hire, where applicable).
  • Bilingual (English/Spanish).
  • Experience with climbing, bucket operations, and advanced rigging techniques.
  • Familiarity with traffic control and roadside right‑of‑way work.



WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Field‑based position performed primarily outdoors in varying weather conditions and terrain.

  • Regular exposure to trees, vegetation, traffic corridors, heavy equipment, and energized power line environments.

  • Physical demands include climbing, lifting, walking, standing, bending, and use of chainsaws and hand tools.

  • Work schedules may include early mornings, extended hours, weekends, and emergency response as operational needs require.

  • Travel within assigned service areas is required.

We are committed to providing an inclusive workplace and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law.

We are leaders in assisting front-line providers and engaging health care partners to improve care delivery and patient outcomes.

Our talented remote workforce spans the country and plays a vital role in our success. We go beyond merely providing a remote work option; we support and embrace it.   • Apply clinical review criteria, organizational policies, guidelines, and screening tools to determine medical necessity of healthcare services

description:
Job Summary

Reporting to the Director of Quality Assurance/Regional Program Director, the CDL Program Director is responsible for providing leadership for the CDL Program. The CDL Program Director provides subject matter expertise and actively participates in curriculum development, revision, and implementation process. As the subject matter expert in a particular program, the CDL Program Director provides product knowledge training to the Account management group, utilizing materials generated via the centralized curriculum development process. This position is responsive to the Account management staff when asked to engage with potential students and actively participates in new student orientation. The CDL Program Director is responsible for hiring, assigning, orienting, developing, evaluating, and recognizing Driver Trainers within the program(s) of study. The CDL Program Director will convene meetings with faculty on a regular basis. The CDL Program Director is also responsible for monitoring and supporting the student population within his/her assigned responsibility. The CDL Program Director plays an active role in the student advising process, including advising students during the provisional period, meeting with students who initiate a complaint, advising students who have career-oriented questions, and consulting with students whose engagement and/or academic progress is in question. The CDL Program Director analyzes student population data, working with faculty and staff to identify students who may be at risk, and contacting students to identify barriers to success and to provide support and information concerning student services. Finally, the CDL Program Director is responsible for continuous improvement of the program. Actively engaged in the development and maintenance of the campus effectiveness plan, the CDL Program Director collects data for purposes of analyzing program performance.

Key Responsibilities

I. Provides Services to Students

  • Supplements Driver Trainer advising for students receiving failing assessments.

  • Provides academic advising/counseling as needed to students. Provides referrals to outside resources when counseling needs go beyond the scope of the school. Provides or arranges for student tutoring when needed.

Makes calls weekly to students who (a) were not called or could not be reached; (b) did not return as promised; or (c) did not offer plans to return by a specific date. Offers appropriate academic advice and demonstrates genuine interest in students.

  • Identifies students needing tutoring.

  • Orients, monitors, supervises, mentors, and assists new Driver Trainers when assigned.

  • Attends weekly day and evening faculty meetings. Meeting topics may include improvement of course offerings, methods of instructional delivery, selection of texts, and such other purposes which serve to improve the quality of the instructional program.

  • Provides information to all departments as trends and changes in program specialty areas occur.

  • Maintains current personal knowledge of federal and state institutional regulations, and accreditation standards related to program area.

  • Participates in preparation of government and accreditation reports and ensures their timely submission and accuracy.

  • Assists the Director of Quality Assurance/Regional Program Director in evaluating data collected from student questionnaires and conducts faculty conferences when necessary to discuss the results and provides recommendations for improvement.

  • Collaborates with peers and associates to ensure coordination of interdepartmental activities.

  • Performs all duties of a full-time Driver Trainer.

Experience and Education Required

  • High school diploma or GED.

  • CDL License with at least 2 years driving experience.

  • 5 years of industry experience in the field of instruction.

  • 2 years of experience in a management or supervisory role.

  • Knowledge regarding faculty development, including requirements, delivery methods, and reporting.

  • Motivation, dedication, professionalism, integrity, and enthusiasm for teaching.

  • Knowledge of industry standards and requirements within the field of instruction.

  • Knowledge of and ability to facilitate learning on course content within the field of instruction.

  • Ability to develop and use collaborative relationships for the purpose of accomplishing work objectives; developing relationships with other individuals by listening, sharing ideas, and appreciating others' efforts.

  • Superior verbal and written communication skills.

  • Interpersonal relationship skills necessary for positive interactions with students, alumni, faculty, and employers.

  • Excellent creative and problem solving skills in dealing with students, alumni, employers, faculty, and staff.

  • Excellent presentation skills and ability to present ideas effectively to individuals or groups in a formal setting.

  • Management skills in planning, organizing, controlling and evaluating programs and policies in a dynamic and changing environment.

title: Senior Robot Platform Software Engineer (Zürich, 100%)
description:

Robotics is the ultimate full-stack challenge. It combines heterogeneous compute, real-time guarantees, and AI models in a box that has to work unsupervised in the field for weeks.   • Experience in test automation (unit tests, integration tests)

These skills are a plus:

  • Experience with NVIDIA Jetson

As the first dedicated platform engineer, you will have a massive impact on our engineering culture. As the team grows, you can remain a high-impact generalist and work across all layers of abstraction or specialize and lead individual subsystems.
