title: Member of Technical Staff - Embedded Systems Engineer
description:
Technology that speaks your language

Domera Labs builds Ami, the first AI companion for seniors. Ami brings the power of a smartphone into a more human form: voice-first and deeply personalized

We at Domera Labs are rethinking human-machine interaction from first principles by introducing a better interface to interact with technology: voice

By combining the most intuitive hardware design with frontier AI, Ami makes AI accessible for the fastest growing demographic worldwide. The goal is to make the everyday life older adults more seamless, while addressing that generation's biggest challenge: loneliness and isolation. With Ami we are building the category leader of a new hardware paradigm by building a full standalone device (and not a gadget) that aims to makes the smartphones of today redundant.

The underlying technology of Ami combines a model-agnostic streaming pipeline consisting of proprietary models and off-the-shelf frontier models to create a hyper-personalized and proactive user experience. The backbone of Ami is built by our foundational lab that builds a social intelligence model that is optimized for social interaction, human behavior and interpersonal skills.

Domera Labs has secured large distribution agreements, a model co-development partnership with a leading AI lab, and ODM manufacturing proposals. We are looking for people who want to build at the intersection of human-machine interaction, mass-consumer facing hardware and shape frontier research with social/non-quantifiable benchmarking.


Core Responsibilities

You own the device: everything between the silicon and the cloud. Our users are 75 years old and there is no screen, no settings menu, and no IT support. If the device does not just work, it fails. Your job is to make that true.

  • Device identity and fleet management: provisioning, unique device identity, secure key storage, and the systems that let us know what every unit in the field is doing

  • The maintenance channel: a reliable service and diagnostics path to the device (BLE, USB-C, or both) for field debugging, factory test, and recovery

  • Out-of-the-box experience: first-boot network onboarding that a senior can complete alone, with no screen and no smartphone as a crutch. This is the single highest-stakes piece of the product

  • Flash and update management: partition layout, A/B OTA with rollback, staged fleet rollouts, and bricking as a category of bug that never happens

  • Base platform behaviors: boot and recovery, factory and soft resets, button and LED mappings, audio feedback, power states and battery behavior

  • The audio front end: working with our ODM and silicon partners on mic array, echo cancellation, wake word, and the latency budget from mic to first spoken token

  • Bringing the device through EVT, DVT, and PVT with our ODM as the technical counterpart on our side

What we are looking for

  • ⁠A builder's mindset: ship > fail > learn > improve

  • Stay focused when multiple priorities compete and the ranking is unclear

  • Work seamlessly across research and engineering

  • Can navigate ambiguity and make progress in fast-moving research environments

  • This is a founding-level position. You will work directly with the founders, shape the architecture from the ground up, and see your work in users' hands within months, not years.

Technical Requirements

  • You have shipped a connected consumer device to production, not just to a demo table. You know what goes wrong between DVT and mass production

  • Strong C/C++ and Linux-based embedded platforms (Yocto, Buildroot, or similar), plus comfort in Python for tooling and test

  • Wireless connectivity in the real world: Wi-Fi provisioning, BLE, and ideally cellular. You have debugged a device that would not join a network in someone's home

  • OTA and flash: bootloaders, secure boot, A/B partitioning, rollback, and staged rollouts across a fleet

  • You debug with a scope and a logic analyzer when the logs run out

  • A builder's mindset: you'd rather ship and measure than debate

  • Bonus: real-time audio pipelines (I2S, DSP, AEC, wake word), on-device ML inference, factory test and manufacturing line bring-up, regulatory certification (CE, FCC), power optimization for battery life, experience in NLU / NLP

We consider candidates across experience levels and lean toward senior engineers who have worked directly with frontier AI systems. Python, deep learning frameworks, or distributed computing are non-negotiable for this role.

What you get

  • ⁠Founding-team equity and a real say in technical direction

  • ⁠A product with signed launch partners, not a demo in search of a market

  • ⁠A small team, short decision paths

  • Cash compensation range of CHF 80 - 100k with significant equity incentives

  • Opportunity to shape the future of hardware and social intelligent AI models


We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, develop and maintain end-to-end data pipelines and ETL processes.

  • Extract, transform and load data from multiple source systems into data warehouse environments.

  • Develop and optimise complex SQL queries, stored procedures, views and data transformation logic.

  • Design and implement data warehouse structures, including dimensional models, fact and dimension tables.

  • Work with business and technical stakeholders to understand data requirements and translate these into effective data solutions.

  • Perform data analysis, profiling and validation to ensure data quality and integrity.

  • Develop, test and deploy data integration solutions across development, test and production environments.

Essential Technical Experience

Strong practical experience in:

  • SQL / T-SQL

  • Data Warehousing

  • ETL / Data Integration

  • SSIS

  • SQL Server

  • Relational databases and data modelling

  • Dimensional modelling / Kimball methodology

  • Data transformation and cleansing

  • Stored procedures and complex SQL development

  • Data quality and reconciliation

  • Performance optimisation

Microsoft / Azure Stack

Experience with one or more of the following:

  • Azure Data Factory (ADF)

  • Azure SQL

  • Azure Synapse Analytics

  • Azure Data Lake / ADLS

  • SQL Server Integration Services (SSIS)

  • SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS)

  • Power BI / SSAS exposure would be advantageous

ADF can also be used alongside existing SSIS workloads, including running SSIS packages through Azure-SSIS Integration Runtime, making a combination of traditional Microsoft ETL and Azure data integration experience particularly useful.

End-to-End Data Engineering Exposure

The successful candidate should be able to demonstrate experience across a meaningful portion of the following:

Source Systems → Data Ingestion → ETL → Data Transformation → Data Warehouse → Data Quality → Data Consumption

They should understand how the different components fit together rather than having experience limited to one particular area of the data lifecycle.

Advantageous Experience

  • Azure cloud data engineering

  • Azure Data Factory

  • Azure Synapse

  • Azure Data Lake

  • Power BI

  • SSAS

  • Python

  • REST APIs

  • Git / Azure DevOps

  • CI/CD and DevOps practices

  • Data governance and lineage

  • Metadata management

  • Automated testing

  • Exposure to modern cloud data platforms or Microsoft Fabric

Candidate Requirements

  • Relevant tertiary qualification in Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Engineering, IT or a related field.

  • Approximately 3–6 years' commercial Data Engineering experience.

  • Strong hands-on experience in SQL and ETL development.

  • Demonstrable experience working with data warehouse environments.

  • Good understanding of data modelling and data integration principles.

  • Experience working within structured development and release environments.

  • Comfortable working independently while collaborating with Architects, Developers, Analysts and business stakeholders.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.

  • Good communication and documentation skills.

  • Exposure to Agile methodologies.

What We Are Looking For

The ideal candidate is not simply an ETL Developer. We are looking for someone who has progressed into a broader Data Engineering role, with a solid understanding of:

  • How source systems provide data

  • How data should be ingested and transformed

  • How data warehouses are designed and populated

  • How to build reliable and maintainable ETL pipelines

  • How to troubleshoot and optimise data solutions

  • How data ultimately supports BI, reporting and analytics

They should have a strong Microsoft foundation, particularly around SQL Server, SSIS and data warehousing, with Azure experience being highly advantageous.

This is a hands-on Data Engineering role suited to someone who can take ownership of development tasks while working within a broader consulting and delivery team.

Technologist Trainee is a training position, preparing the employee to work independently as a limit license scientist (Technologist) and to further gain ASCP certification within five years. Works under the supervision of a Medical Laboratory Scientist, Certified Technologist, or Technologist in providing services of both a technical and non-technical nature in the laboratory services area.

About ARUP:

ARUP Laboratories is a national clinical and anatomic pathology reference laboratory and an enterprise of the University of Utah and its Department of Pathology. Based in Salt Lake City, Utah.

ARUP proudly hires top talent to create a work environment of diversity, professional growth and continuous development. Our workforce is committed to the important service we provide to over one million patients each month. We always strive for excellence and have a strong desire to have involvement with the advances in medicine and the role laboratory services plays within each patient’s life. We never forget that there is a patient behind every specimen we receive.

We are looking for individuals who want to contribute to ARUP's culture of accountability, integrity, service, and excellence. Consider joining our dynamic team.

Essential Functions:

Performs waived and automated analytic processes. This includes qualitative, semi-qualitative, or quantitative tests performed automatically by an instrument.

Oversees calibration on self-calibrating instruments and performs select calibration processes.

Performs selected moderate and high complexity analytic processes (both automated and non-automated)

Operates selected laboratory instruments and ensures proper functioning of laboratory equipment. Performs minor troubleshooting and routine maintenance under direction of a Technologist and/or Technical Supervisor. Maintains records and documentation.

Performs and documents quality control and equipment maintenance within predetermined parameters.

Accurately logs in and processes specimens according to established departmental procedures.

Follows appropriate specimen collection, handling, and transport procedures. Resolves sample handling problems or refers problems to designated Technologists, and/or Technical Supervisor.

Processes data and transcribes data in the laboratory computer system. All results are validated by the qualified personnel (Technologist, Certified Technologist, Medical Laboratory Scientist).

Trains on new procedures to a prescribed level of competency.

Meets output measures as defined by individual group procedures. Assists others in areas of defined competency when assigned workload is complete.

Refers requests for special and unusual tests to the Technical Supervisor and/or Group Manager.

Assists in data collection for QA indicators as defined.

Assists in the performance of validation of equipment and test methods as defined.

Assists in the creation and review of standard operating procedures (SOPs) as defined.

Performs internal and external proficiency testing as defined.

Appropriately stocks and maintains reagents and supplies.

Assists in the training of Technicians as assigned.

Other duties as assigned.

Physical and Other Requirements:

Stooping: Bending body downward and forward by bending spine at the waist.

Reaching: Extending hand(s) and arm(s) in any direction.

Mobility: The person in this position needs to occasionally move between work sites and inside the office to access file cabinets, office machinery, etc.

Communicate: Frequently communicate with others.

PPE: Biohazard laboratory environment that requires use of personal protective equipment in accordance with CDC and OSHA regulations and company policies.

ARUP Policies and Procedures: To conduct self in compliance with all ARUP Policies and Procedures.

Sedentary Work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects.

Fine Motor Control: Picking, pinching, typing or otherwise working, primarily with fingers rather than with the whole hand as in handling.

Vision: Having close, far, and peripheral visual acuity to perform a variety of tasks such as make general observations of depth and distance.

Color Vision: Perception of and ability to distinguish colors.

Continuing Education: Continual assessment of current literature and best practices.

Education Qualifications:

Technologist Trainees at ARUP must have a Bachelor’s degree in the chemical or biological sciences with the following course requirements:

Chemistry

  • 23 semester credit hours of science courses
  • 3 semester credit hours of physics, math, or statistics
  • 16 semester credits hours in chemistry

Cytogenetics and Molecular Biology

  • 23 semester credit hours of science courses
  • 3 semester credit hours of physics, math, or statistics
  • 16 semester credits hours in biological or chemical science

Hematology

  • 23 semester credit hours of science courses
  • 3 semester credit hours of physics, math, or statistics
  • 16 semester credits hours in biological science

Immunohematology

  • 23 semester credit hours of science courses
  • 3 semester credit hours of physics, math, or statistics
  • 16 semester credits hours in biological science

Microbiology

  • 23 semester credit hours of science courses
  • 3 semester credit hours of physics, math, or statistics
  • 16 semester credits hours in biological science

Chemistry: Quantitative Analysis/Analytical Chemistry and Clinical Chemistry or Biochemistry
Cytogenetics and Molecular Biology: Genetics
Microbiology: Medical, Clinical, or Pathogenic Microbiology
Hematology: Hematology
Immunohematology: Immunology

description:

SiTime is the Precision Timing company. Timing is the heartbeat of all electronics, ensuring performance, resilience and scalability. MEMS-based Precision Timing delivers greater accuracy, smaller size and resilience. Today, MEMS timing powers over 400 applications, including high-growth ones in AI datacenters, automated driving, industrial and humanoid robots, wearables and IoT.

With more than 4 billion devices shipped, SiTime is changing the timing industry. For more information, visit SiTime’s career page and company website.

Job Summary

SiTime is seeking a hands-on Finance Transformation Architect to design, build, and operationalize AI agents and automation solutions that transform accounting and finance processes across the organization. This role sits within the Finance & Accounting organization and partners closely with Finance leadership, the Corporate Controller, IT/Data, and internal controls stakeholders to improve efficiency, control, and insight across processes such as procure-to-pay, record-to-report, close, reconciliations, reporting, and analytics. The ideal candidate combines strong engineering and systems thinking with practical finance process knowledge and a bias for secure, auditable, and scalable automation. It is not necessary to meet all job requirements to be a qualified candidate for the position.

  • Create user playbooks, SOP updates, and training materials to support change management and adoption across global Finance and Accounting teams.
  • Partner with IT and Information Security teams to ensure responsible AI practices, privacy, security, model governance, and compliance with company policies.

  • Oracle Cloud ERP experience is preferred, especially within finance modules such as AP, GL, FA, Cash Management, or Projects, along with familiarity with Oracle reporting and integration tooling.
  • UiPath experience is preferred, including Studio, Orchestrator, Document Understanding, ERP integration patterns, and production bot operations.
  • Experience with close, reconciliation, reporting, or data platforms such as BlackLine, Hyperion/EPM, or Snowflake is preferred.
  • Hands-on experience with prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, tool or function calling, evaluation frameworks, and model quality or risk practices is preferred.

  • It is not necessary to meet all job requirements to be a qualified candidate for the position.

Desired Characteristics & Attributes:

title: Danmarks Medie- og Journalisthøjskole (DMJX) søger en ekstern lektor til OSINT-undervisning på Institut for Journalistik
description:
Danmarks Medie- og Journalisthøjskole søger en ekstern lektor med stærke OSINT-kompetencer, undervisningserfaring, samt viden om og erfaring med brug af OSINT i journalistisk arbejde.

Ansættelsen vil fortrinsvis være rettet mod professionsbacheloruddannelsen og kandidatuddannelserne i journalistik på Campus Aarhus, men der vil også kunne forekomme opgaver på andre uddannelser, herunder kurser og videreuddannelse, samt i mindre grad på uddannelserne på Campus København.

Stillingen er tidsbegrænset til tre år.

Dine primære opgaver vil være at:

  • varetage undervisning i OSINT som journalistisk værktøj
  • udvikle, planlægge og gennemføre undervisningsforløb
  • bidrage til løbende at videreudvikle journalistuddannelsen

Vi lægger vægt på, at du:

  • har en relevant uddannelse, gerne på master- eller kandidatniveau
  • har dokumenteret erfaring med anvendelse af de nyeste teknologier og værktøjer inden for både manuel og automatiseret indhentning af data og information. Heriblandt også anvendelse AI til OSINT undersøgelser.
  • har bred og avanceret viden om SOCMINT og GEOINT. Erfaring med verificering af billed- og videomateriale, herunder reverse image search, metadata-analyse og vurdering af manipuleret eller AI-genereret indhold.
  • har erfaring med analytiske OSINT-metoder som netværkskortlægning, geolokation og avancerede søgeoperatører, samt med at anvende disse i praksis på konkrete undersøgelser.
  • har kendskab til de metoder og værktøjer, der særligt anvendes i journalistiske undersøgelser og verificering. Samt forståelse for de juridiske og etiske rammer for OSINT-arbejde i en journalistisk kontekst
  • har kendskab til digital sikkerhed og OPSEC i forbindelse med research (fx anonymisering og sikker indhentning).
  • er en god kollega og holdspiller
  • har undervisningserfaring

Om afdelingen
Vi tilbyder et uhøjtideligt, tværfagligt arbejdsmiljø med spændende arbejdsopgaver og plads til selvstændigt arbejde og medindflydelse. Der er rig mulighed for (tvær)fagligt samarbejde og faglig udvikling. Og så giver vi dig mulighed for at udvikle og uddanne fremtidens journalister.

På journalistuddannelserne er vi omkring 40 undervisere og forskere, der brænder for faget, for undervisning og for at arbejde med de omkring 1.000 dygtige studerende på journalistuddannelsen, cand.public, Erasmus Mundus Master in Journalism, Media and Globalisation, Profilfag og BA-tilvalg.

Løn- og ansættelsesvilkår
Stillingen er på 7,4 timer om ugen og ønskes besat pr. 1. november 2026. Det primære ansættelsessted er Aarhus.

Ansættelsen følger gældende bekendtgørelse om stillingsstruktur for undervisere ved erhvervsakademier, professionshøjskoler, Danmarks Medie- og Journalisthøjskole og visse maritime uddannelsesinstitutioner, for tiden (BEK nr. 414 af 27/04/2025).
Ansættelsen sker i henhold til de enhver tid gældende vilkår i ”Cirkulære om overenskomst for eksterne lektorer og timelærer professionshøjskoler, Danmarks Medie- og Journalisthøjskole, erhvervsakademier og maritime uddannelsesinstitutioner m.fl. under Uddannelses- og Forskningsministeriet (Akademikers forhandlingsområde).

Vil du vide mere?
Har du spørgsmål til stillingen, eller ønsker du flere oplysninger, er du velkommen til at kontakte institutleder Henrik Berggren (mail: hb@dmjx.dk, tlf.: 30623589).

Ansøgning
Ansøgning vedlagt relevant dokumentation uploades via linket ”Søg stillingen” senest den 5. oktober 2026. Undlad venligst at sende personfølsomme oplysninger med din ansøgning.

Angiv venligst, hvor du har set jobannoncen.

Alle interesserede, uanset personlig baggrund, opfordres til at søge stillingen.

Om Danmarks Medie- og Journalisthøjskole
Danmarks Medie- og Journalisthøjskole (DMJX) uddanner fremtidens talenter inden for bl.a. reklame, design, journalistik, foto, kommunikation og medieledelse - og videreuddanner dem, der allerede arbejder inden for områderne.
DMJX samarbejder med ledende uddannelsesinstitutioner over hele verden samt med virksomheder og organisationer for at sikre uddannelser, der er praksisnære og målrettet en verden i forandring. Desuden huser DMJX flere videnscenterfunktioner og bedriver forskning inden for de områder, der undervises i.
DMJX har domicil i både Aarhus og København og har omkring 2.000 indskrevne fuldtidsstuderende, knap 2.000 deltidsstuderende/kursister hvert år, ca. 160 fuldtidsansatte undervisere og forskere, administrativt personale samt et større antal eksterne undervisere.

title: Employability Coach (6-month Full time/Fixed-term/Remote) [United States]
description:
ABOUT GENERATION

At Generation, we believe in the power of employment to change lives. We are a global nonprofit organization that supports adults to achieve economic mobility through employment. Generation trains and places adult learners of all ages into careers that are otherwise inaccessible, working in partnership with governments, employers, and other system actors. We also conduct original research and share data insights on high-priority global workforce transition topics to inform decision-making by workforce system stakeholders. Launched in 2015, Generation comprises a global hub (Generation You Employed, or GYE) and a network of in-country affiliates. To date, the network has 150,000+ graduates and 23,000+ employers across 50 professions and 17 countries.

When learners join Generation, 91% are unemployed, of which nearly half are long-term unemployed. Three months after completing our program, graduates have a 78% job placement rate, rising to 88% within six months. Of our employed graduates, 79% are hired by repeat employers who have previously hired Generation graduates, and 89% are in jobs directly related to the profession for which we have trained them. Employed graduates immediately earn an average of 3-4X their previous earnings. Two to five years after graduation, 77% of our alumni from upper-middle income countries continue to meet their daily financial needs and 63% can save for the future. To date, Generation’s global graduates have earned more than $1.9 billion in wages. Generation graduates typically have a secondary school background, 52% are female, 28% have dependents, and the majority identify with underrepresented communities in their country.

POSITION OVERVIEW

We are looking for an exceptional Employability Coach to support learners into job placement for the Generation’s JobSprint Program.

You will be joining at an exciting time for Generation United States, as we leverage our extensive experience placing learners into jobs to develop and launch a new program offering that can serve a range of jobseekers who require last-mile support to secure employment. The training program is free to learners, part-time, online and mostly asynchronous, with personalized career coaching - by both human coaches (you!) and AI-enabled coaching and feedback tools.

Reporting to the Program Manager, the Employability Coach will support learners as they prepare for and conduct their job search, and you will help facilitate their placement into their new role at one of Generation’s employer partners. The Employability Coach will run both group and one-on-one coaching sessions, utilize an online learning platform and coaching software, and work closely with the Employer Engagement Manager to support placement.

This is a full-time, fixed-term, 6-month position funded through December 2026; continued employment thereafter is contingent upon the availability of funding. While this role is predominantly remote, there may be quarterly domestic travel and/or in-person events. Working hours are primarily from 9 to 5 pm ET; during the training program the Employability Coach will need to be available for 1 evening (ET) group session per week. This role requires regular video presence during working hours; candidates should have a dedicated, distraction-free workspace.

Preference for candidates based in Atlanta, GA or Washington D.C.

RESPONSIBILITIES

The Employability Coach will:

In-Program

  • Become familiar with and follow the course of the program as designed by Generation, in addition to sharing insights based on your expertise
  • Conduct 1:1 coaching conversations to review and provide feedback on learners’ applications/interview materials and guide them in the creation of an “employment essentials toolkit” (i.e., CV, LinkedIn profile)
  • Hold weekly group coaching sessions during 3-week program (1 per week during evening ET hours) and office hours as needed to support learners in understanding content and completing program milestones
  • Review learner progress (e.g., attendance, assignments), grading assignments when needed (e.g., CV review), and inputting data in Canvas LMS
  • Use AI Career Coaching tool to further personalize and supplement coaching; track learner usage / progress on coaching tool
  • Instill confidence during the placement process by supporting learners in career trajectory planning
  • Support Employer Engagement Manager to answer placement questions learners may have and to ensure any essential employment-related documentation is complete and up-to-date for each learner
  • Coordinate with Generation team members on learner needs and ongoing data collection, sharing feedback and implementing recommendations to guarantee quality training for our learners
  • Effectively use digital tools such as Teams, Canvas, Slack, and GDrive to perform daily tasks and collaborate in a remote working environment
  • Avoid legal liability issues through thorough adherence to Generation policy, procedure, and guidelines

Transition to Employment

  • Participate in mock interviews with learners and give feedback to help them become better-prepared and more confident
  • Oversee learners’ transition to full-time employment by closely collaborating with Generation team members to fulfill job recruitment opportunities in line with deadlines
  • Design and deliver events that connect Generation graduates to employers
  • Manage placement activities in partnership with Employer Engagement Manager, including learner usage of Employability Module, scheduling interviews and collecting data on job search and attainment
  • Track unplaced alumni and ensure that they are being notified of relevant job opportunities
  • Ensure consistent communication with learners, graduates, and the Generation team to ensure effective coordination, timely updates, and an overall successful execution of the placement process

ABOUT YOU

Required experience and skills:

  • You have at least 2 years’ experience in career coaching, and/or employment counseling, and/or experience hiring, managing, and/or coaching entry-level recruits from a range of backgrounds
  • You have strong relationship building skills and excellent communication skills (writing + oral expression that can work for different audiences)
  • You are comfortable conducting 1:1 conversations and giving evaluative feedback in an honest, open and nurturing way
  • You are able to develop and maintain relationships with learners built on trust and support
  • You have an up-to-date understanding of employability essentials (e.g., CV, LinkedIn, interviewing skills)
  • You are comfortable with, analyzing and utilizing data to inform operational decisions and learning new technology (including AI-powered tools)

Preferred experience and skills:

  • Experience in workforce development or other educational / training roles
  • Experience working with a diverse set of beneficiaries
  • Proficient with Canvas or similar LMS tools, Salesforce and Google Workspace

Mindset:

  • You are proactive self-starter, able to work autonomously and collaboratively with others in a remote work environment
  • You can work in a fast-paced, changing environment, take ownership and are entrepreneurial
  • You are results driven, able to quantify success by developing metrics/analytics
  • You have a positive, solution-oriented attitude and a drive for excellence
  • You believe in our mission, that fulfilling employment can change lives, and are passionate about doing social good

This role is eligible for a limited benefits package, which may include medical coverage, paid sick leave, paid time off, paid holidays, and access to a retirement plan. Benefits eligibility is based on a fixed‑term six‑month employment period and is subject to plan rules and change.

Finalists for the position will be asked to submit 2-3 employer references (including email and phone number).

title: State Lead, Lead Exposure
description:
Overview

WJCF is an Indian non-profit organisation committed to saving lives by reducing the burden of disease and strengthening government-owned, high-quality health systems. Since 2007, WJCF has combined data-driven approaches and deep public health expertise with strong government partnerships to design, implement, and scale solutions across India’s national and state health programmes. We work for and at the service of governments — supporting the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare and State Departments of Health to build systems that are strong, sustainable, and led by Indian institutions.

As an Indian organisation, WJCF brings an unmatched depth of contextual understanding of India’s health system architecture, policy landscape, and implementation realities across diverse geographies and population groups. This local institutional credibility, combined with global technical rigour, is central to WJCF’s effectiveness as a partner to governments and donors.

Our work is built around four complementary roles: as a Trusted Government Partner, co-designing programmes and strengthening health system architecture; as an Operational Partner, translating strategies into effective on-the-ground delivery; as a Market Shaper, improving the availability and affordability of health commodities; and as an Ecosystem Catalyst, convening governments, development partners, academia, and the private sector to drive solutions at scale.

WJCF’s programme portfolio spans thematic areas like hepatitis, HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, vector-borne diseases), syphilis, cervical cancer, diabetes, maternal and childhood anaemia, immunisation, under-5 diarrhoea and pneumonia, sexual and reproductive health, Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri – Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), hypoxemia and oxygen, safe drinking water, sickle cell disease, presbyopia, lead poisoning, and cross cutting thematic areas like AI and Health, integrated disease surveillance, and climate and health. We currently support programmes across 19 states and union territories, with teams working at national, state, district, and sub-district levels.

Our people are our greatest asset. WJCF brings together a talented, diverse team of professionals from public health, analytics, consulting, healthcare, the development sector, and academia, all united by a shared commitment to improving health outcomes for the people of India. We are entrepreneurial, action-oriented, and deeply grounded in the communities and systems we work in. Our field teams collectively bring hundreds of years of experience managing public health programmes across the country.

WJCF collaborates with a range of international and domestic partners and donors to advance its mission, including an affiliation with the Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI), a global health organisation with which WJCF shares a common mission and values.

Programme Overview

Lead poisoning is one of India's most significant and most solvable public health challenges. India bears the world's highest burden of childhood lead poisoning, with over 275 million children carrying blood lead levels above 5 µg/dL; the national average is 6.2 µg/dL and 23 States exceed the threshold (NITI Aayog and CSIR review, 2022). Lead exposure causes irreversible neurological damage in children, contributes to an estimated one million cardiovascular deaths annually in adults (Larsen et al., 2023), and generates compounding intergenerational risks.

The National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), as the designated national focal agency under the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, is establishing the National Biomonitoring Programme for Chemical Toxicants (NBPCT). WJCF is embedding a Technical Support Unit (TSU) nationally and a state-level teams in select states. The state teams will work alongside the State Health Department, the State Pollution Control Board (SPCB), and allied departments to build the governance architecture, program roadmap, set up an inter-departmental coordination mechanism, develop state-adapted protocols, and operationalise all NBPCT program activities.

Position Summary

WJCF is seeking a highly motivated, entrepreneurial professional with strong credentials and exceptional stakeholder-management skills for the role of State Lead, Lead Exposure. The State Lead will own WJCF's engagement in in the State- building the relationships, governance mechanisms, and technical products for the program.

The role requires developing a deep understanding of the state's health system architecture, pollution control and environmental regulatory machinery, budgeting cycles, and political economy, and use that to convert a nascent national programme into a functioning state response. The State Lead will work across departments that do not routinely work together and will need the policy acumen to navigate a complex multi-stakeholder environment

The incumbent will function under the programmatic guidance of the State Health Department. The ideal candidate should have exceptional interpersonal skills, be able to work independently and comfortably in ambiguity, and have a strong commitment to excellence.

Location: Mohali (at the Directorate of Health Services)

Travel: to program districts within Punjab, and occasionally to New Delhi

Responsibilities

Government Engagement and State Governance

  • Lead WJCF's engagement with state government stakeholders on lead exposure, and secure alignment on the programme's priorities, workplan, and proposed new initiatives.
  • Build and maintain relationships with senior officials across the Department of Health & Family Welfare, NHM, the State Pollution Control Board, and the Departments of Environment, Industries, Mines, Labour and Food Safety.
  • Support the state in constituting a task force on lead exposure. Convene inter-departmental meetings, drive agreement on priority actions, and establish a routine review and follow-up cadence.
  • Conduct a state governance and system gap assessment and use the findings to shape the state workplan.

Programme Management, Learning and Partnerships

  • Lead day-to-day programme implementation at state level – planning and on-ground roll-out of activities- in coordination with the national TSU and State Health Department
  • Manage and mentor the state team, including the Senior Analyst, and build their capability to engage government counterparts independently.
  • Maintain workplan trackers and milestone dashboards, and prepare high-quality progress reports, briefing notes, and strategy documents for government counterparts and donors
  • Identify programmatic, operational, and political risks to implementation, and work with programme leadership to design and execute mitigation plans.
  • Coordinate with development partners active in the state, academic and research institutions as needed.
  • Represent WJCF in state-level technical working groups, review meetings, and forums, and contribute state learnings to national workshops and peer-learning exchanges.

Technical Products, Protocols and Capacity Building

  • Lead the adaptation of national protocols to the state context, and support their validation with technical working groups and technical experts.
  • Drive the process to formalise state operational guidelines, and oversee subsequent capacity-building for clinicians, laboratory professionals, SPCB staff, frontline workers, and district health staff.
  • Contextualise and develop state-specific IEC and training materials from nationally developed content.

Surveillance and Data Systems

  • Map state laboratory and treatment capacity; identify infrastructure and human resource gaps.
  • Support the integration of chemical toxicant surveillance data from the state into the Integrated Health Information Portal (IHIP)
  • Oversee the design and use of state dashboards and analytical products that support state decision-making
  • Consolidate programme monitoring data, verify completeness and quality with district counterparts for for integration into national dashboards.

District-level engagement

  • Secure District Collector level ownership, leverage existing convergence platforms like the District Health Society, District Mineral Foundation, to drive program activities in identified priority districts
  • Build and sustain relationships with senior district administration and allied counterparts to align health, environment, and industry mandates for program objectives.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in public health, environmental health, public policy, health management, development studies, management, or a related field, with a minimum of 7 years of relevant work experience in a demanding, results-oriented environment.
  • Demonstrated experience working with state government stakeholders and strong familiarity with the Indian public health system, including NHM structures, budgeting and planning cycles.
  • Proven experience managing multi-stakeholder coordination - technical working groups, inter-departmental committees, and development partners
  • Strong analytical capability: ability to absorb and synthesise epidemiological evidence, policy documents, and programme data into clear recommendations and high-quality written outputs.
  • Advanced proficiency in project and programme management tools and in maintaining complex accountability trackers and dashboards.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage and mentor a team
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills in English and Hindi. Preference for candidates versed in local languages/dialects.
  • Willingness to travel extensively within and outside the programme state and districts.

Preferred

  • Experience in environmental health, chemical toxicants, pollution control, or occupational health programme areas.
  • Prior experience in a secretariat or TSU role supporting a government programme.

Last Date to Apply: 28 October, 2026

title: Senior Geologist/Project Manager
description:
Job Summary:

The Senior Geologist/Project Manager will lead the preparation, submission, and management of environmental permits for projects in Arizona and beyond, with a primary focus on AZPDES (Arizona Pollutant Discharge Elimination System) permits for discharges to surface waters (including stormwater, wastewater, and industrial discharges), Section 404 permits under the Clean Water Act for dredge and fill activities in waters of the U.S. (administered by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers), and other related federal, state, and local environmental permits. This leadership role involves overseeing permitting strategies, coordinating multidisciplinary teams, ensuring regulatory compliance, and serving as the primary point of contact with agencies such as the Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ), U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), and EPA. The position requires deep expertise in Clean Water Act regulations, strong project management skills, and the ability to navigate complex permitting processes for infrastructure, development, mining, energy, or industrial projects while minimizing environmental impacts and supporting project timelines.

Duties:

  • Lead the preparation, compilation, and submission of AZPDES individual and general permits (e.g., for municipal, industrial, construction stormwater, and MS4 discharges), including completing required forms (Form 1, Form 2A/2S), developing Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs), and ensuring compliance with ADEQ requirements.
  • Manage Section 404 permitting processes, including jurisdictional determinations, pre-application consultations with USACE, preparation of permit applications, alternatives analyses, mitigation plans, and coordination for individual or nationwide/general permits involving dredge/fill in wetlands or waters of the U.S.
  • Oversee additional environmental permitting efforts, such as Section 401 Water Quality Certifications, Aquifer Protection Permits (APP), NEPA compliance support, endangered species consultations, and other state/local permits as needed.
  • Develop and implement permitting strategies, timelines, and budgets; identify potential regulatory risks and recommend avoidance, minimization, or mitigation measures.
  • Serve as lead technical expert and point of contact for regulatory agencies; prepare for and participate in pre-application meetings, public notices, hearings, and agency negotiations.
  • Coordinate with internal teams (engineers, biologists, hydrologists, project managers) and external consultants to gather data, conduct environmental assessments, and prepare supporting documentation (e.g., wetland delineations, biological surveys, water quality modeling).
  • Review and interpret federal (Clean Water Act, NEPA) and Arizona-specific regulations; stay current on updates to AZPDES, Section 404 guidelines, and related policies.
  • Mentor junior staff on permitting processes, regulatory compliance, and best practices

Education/Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree (required) in Geology, Environmental Science, Biology, Ecology, Hydrology, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resources Management, or a closely related field.
  • Master's degree in a relevant discipline preferred.
  • Minimum of 15+ years of progressively responsible experience in environmental permitting, with at least 10 years in a senior or lead role managing complex permitting projects.
  • Demonstrated expertise in Clean Water Act programs, particularly AZPDES/NPDES permitting (stormwater, wastewater discharges) and USACE Section 404 permitting (wetlands, dredge/fill).
  • Proven track record leading permit applications for large-scale projects in Arizona or similar arid/southwestern environments (e.g., infrastructure, mining, energy, development).
  • Strong knowledge of federal and Arizona environmental regulations, including ADEQ processes, USACE permitting procedures, and related requirements (e.g., mitigation banking, jurisdictional determinations).
  • Excellent project management, organizational, and communication skills, with experience preparing technical reports, permit applications, and presenting to stakeholders/agencies.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite; familiarity with GIS tools for mapping and analysis preferred.

Certifications/Licenses:

  • Professional certification preferred, such as: Registered Geologist or Professional Engineer Certified Wetland Scientist (CWS) or Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS) through the Society of Wetland Scientists.
  • Certified Environmental Professional (CEP) or similar.
  • OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER certification (or willingness to obtain).
  • Valid driver's license required, with ability to travel to project sites and agency meetings as needed.
  • Other relevant certifications (e.g., stormwater inspector training, wetland delineation courses) are a plus.

location: Cicatelli Associates Inc, New York, NY, US
description:
Reports To: Deputy Project Director

Employee Status: Full Time, Exempt

Office Location: We strongly prefer candidates who are able to work out of our New York City office location (505 Eighth Avenue, New York, NY 10018). We have a hybrid schedule of working 2 days in the office and 3 days remote. We are also open to candidates based elsewhere in the United States.

GENERAL STATEMENT OF RESPONSIBILITIES

The Practice Facilitator works as part of CAI’s National Technical Assistance Program (NTAP) for Clinical and Preventive Excellence multidisciplinary team, funded by the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), to plan and provide direct, hands-on technical assistance (TA) to the nation's community health center network. This includes partnering with health centers to identify gaps in performance, causal factors, and to identify and implement changes to improve clinical and preventive care health outcomes.

The Practice Facilitator's work is grounded in systems strengthening, implementation science, and continuous quality improvement frameworks using a relational approach to TA, which emphasizes building and nurturing trust-based partnerships with health centers. This approach prioritizes understanding each health center's context and needs, engaging diverse staff perspectives, and maintaining the reliability and consistency needed to sustain long-term, collaborative relationships that lead to meaningful and lasting change.

Specifically, Practice Facilitators use data and information to guide and support assigned health centers participating in 12-month Communities of Practice (CoPs) and 3-Year Outcomes-Focused Cohorts focused on improving health outcomes for patients with chronic disease (e.g., hypertension, diabetes) and strengthen the provision of preventive and supportive services.

MAJOR TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES (include, but are not limited to)

  • Partner with the NTAP project team and subject matter experts in the design and facilitation of CoP and Outcomes-focused virtual and in-person learning sessions.
  • Build and sustain trust-based, collaborative partnerships with assigned health centers, consistent with CAI's relational approach to technical assistance – including building buy-in from health center leadership.
  • Partner with health center staff across roles and levels of authority to assess health center context and capacity and engage differing perspectives in planning and decision-making to ensure technical assistance is tailored for each health center’s unique context.
  • Facilitate data-informed process to identify gaps in client outcomes, causal factors, priority areas for improvement, and strategies to address causal factors to improve client health outcomes.
  • Facilitate development of mutually agreed upon health center improvement plan including documented implementation support strategies (e.g., new workflows, strengthened community partnerships, team-based care models, clinical consultation, protocol development, staff training) tailored to each health center's unique context.
  • Support use of real-time data to inform health centers’ continuous improvement activities.
  • Provide data-driven iterative implementation support through regularly scheduled virtual health center team huddles to support implementation of mutually agreed upon plan and to rapidly identify and address implementation challenges.
  • Support health centers in testing and refining changes to care delivery through Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) cycles and other rapid-cycle improvement methods.
  • Maintain reliability and consistency in fulfilling technical assistance commitments to reinforce health centers' trust and confidence in the partnership.
  • Document technical assistance activities, findings, and health center progress in QuickBase, CAI’s project management platform, and track a defined set of performance measures for each assigned health center.
  • Collaborate with CAI CoP and Cohort Leads, subject matter experts, evaluators, and partner organizations to ensure technical assistance is current, evidence-based, and responsive to health center needs.
  • Identify and communicate emerging issues, barriers, and promising practices to program leadership to inform continuous improvement of NTAP's technical assistance approach.

title: Senior Cloud Backend Engineer – Distributed Systems (Golang / AWS)
description:
The Objective

We are seeking an uncompromising Senior Cloud Backend Engineer to build, scale, and maintain high-throughput, event-driven microservices powering our enterprise platform. Tailored for a mid-to-senior engineering benchmark, this role requires a battle-tested developer who writes clean, idiomatic Go, commands distributed system architecture, and operates autonomously. You will be held accountable for high system availability, zero-downtime deployments, and rigid code quality.

Core Responsibilities

  • Microservices Architecture: Design, write, and deploy resilient, high-concurrency REST/gRPC microservices using Golang, taking full ownership from technical specification to production rollout.

  • Event-Driven Systems: Engineer and optimize asynchronous messaging pipelines using Apache Kafka or RabbitMQ to support high TPS (transactions per second) with sub-second processing requirements.

  • Database & Cache Optimization: Architect scalable relational and NoSQL schemas (PostgreSQL, Redis). Perform deep query profiling, indexing, connection pooling, and deadlock mitigation.

  • Infrastructure & CI/CD: Containerize services using Docker and manage Kubernetes deployments on AWS. Build automated, zero-downtime CI/CD pipelines and configure proactive alerting (Prometheus, Grafana).

  • System Resilience & On-Call: Conduct rigorous unit/integration testing, enforce strict code review standards, and participate in rotational 2nd-line production support to resolve system incidents swiftly.

Strict Qualifying Criteria

  • Production Experience: Minimum 5+ years of software development experience, with at least 3+ years writing concurrent, production-grade Golang services in a cloud-native setting.

  • Distributed Systems Mastery: Proven experience building and debugging distributed microservices architectures handling high load, race conditions, and network failures.

  • Database Expertise: Strong proficiency in PostgreSQL (complex joins, execution plans, partitioning) and Redis caching patterns (write-through, eviction policies).

  • Cloud & DevOps Tooling: Hands-on operational experience with Kubernetes, Docker, Helm, and AWS services (EKS, RDS, S3, IAM).

  • Computer Science Foundation: Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or an equivalent technical field, backed by strong fundamentals in data structures, concurrency, and OOP/functional design principles.

  • Strong proficiency in Node.js, TypeScript, and NestJS; Python proficiency also welcome (or equivalent backend framework)- Must

  • Experience designing scalable backend architectures and data models
  • Deep understanding of API design, authentication flows, and distributed system tradeoffs
  • Experience with relational and/or NoSQL databases, including query optimization
  • Strong understanding of system performance, reliability, and security best practices
  • Experience with testing methodologies (unit, integration, E2E) and observability tooling
  • Hands-on experience using AI development tools in daily workflows, with the ability to validate, debug, and improve AI-generated code
  • Understanding of prompt engineering for engineering workflows and the ability to work effectively in fast iteration environments
  • Strong product and technical intuition, with excellent communication and collaboration skills
  • Nice to have: experience with data platforms, analytics products, or BI tools; large-scale data processing or query optimization; streaming/real-time data patterns; or integrating with LLM APIs

You'll actually love the product you work with: Our customers aren't our only raving fans. When we asked our employees why they chose to come work at Similarweb, 99% of them said "the product." Imagine how exciting your job is when you get to work with the most powerful digital intelligence platform in the world.

You'll find a home for your big ideas: We encourage an open dialogue and empower employees to bring their ideas to the table. You'll find the resources you need to take initiative and create meaningful change within the organization.

We offer competitive perks & benefits: We take your well-being seriously, and offer competitive compensation packages to all employees. We also put a strong emphasis on community, with regular team outings and happy hours.

You can grow your career in any direction you choose: Interested in becoming a VP or want to transition into a different department? title: Medical Records Coordinator (PCN 1578)
description:
The Medical Records Coordinator is responsible for processing requests for patient health information in compliance with HIPAA, state laws, and agency policies, while ensuring accuracy, confidentiality, and proper documentation. This role supports clinical and administrative operations by ensuring timely access to records, promoting documentation integrity, and maintaining compliance with applicable federal and state regulations.

Essential Functions

  • Process and verify requests: Receive and review requests from patients, family members, healthcare providers, insurers, or other authorized parties including subpoenas; confirm legal right to access and validate authorization forms
  • Retrieve records: Locate and assemble medical records from electronic health record (EHR) systems, paper files, or other storage locations.
  • Retrieve Records: prepare responses to Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) and subpoena requests.
  • Ensure compliance: Apply federal and state privacy laws (HIPAA), healthcare facility policies, and applicable regulations to all releases.
  • Redact sensitive data: Remove information not authorized for release in accordance with HIPAA and internal guidelines.
  • Maintain records: Keep detailed, auditable logs of all requests, approvals, and releases; track timelines and compliance status.
  • Communicate with requesters: Clarify needs, provide status updates, and address questions from patients, attorneys, insurers, or providers.
  • Quality checks: Review outgoing records for accuracy, completeness, and compliance before release.
  • Billing and payment: Process invoices and collect fees for record releases per established schedules.
  • Secure storage: Archive released information (digital and physical) in a secure, accessible manner
  • Scan, upload, index, and file documents appropriately within designated systems.
  • Support audits, accreditation reviews, and compliance activities by retrieving and preparing records as requested.
  • Ensure adherence to privacy and confidentiality standards, including HIPAA requirements.
  • Collaborate with clinical, legal quality, and administrative teams to resolve documentation issues and to ensure compliance with regulations.

Programs & partners

About the team

Forward-deployed engineering is where our product meets a plant that has runits own way for thirty years. You write code, but you write it sitting near thepeople who will use it, against data that nobody cleaned for you.

Three people today. We are the shortest path between what a plant actuallyneeds and what gets built, and we are expected to say so plainly when the twodo not match.

About the role

This role is deliberately two jobs that most companies keep apart.

The first is engineering: integrating with whatever a plant already runs,shaping their messy historical data into something we graph can hold, andbuilding the glue that makes a pilot work in weeks rather than quarters.

The second is narrative. After a pilot, someone has to explain to a plantdirector, and to the next prospect, what changed and why it mattered. Thatmeans building the deck, the demo, and the before-and-after story yourself,from the evidence you gathered. We are asking for someone who has done thisbefore and is good at it, because handing it to a marketer who was not thereproduces a deck nobody believes.

What you'll do

  • Integrate our platform with the systems a plant already runs: historians, CMMS, ERP, spreadsheets, and paper
  • Write ingest and transformation code against real, inconsistent operational data
  • Build demos and prototypes fast enough to be useful inside a live customer conversation
  • Turn each deployment into a clear, honest story: deck, numbers, and screen recordings
  • Present that story to plant leadership alongside our founders
  • Bring product gaps back to the core engineering team with evidence, not anecdotes
  • Leave behind documentation the customer's own team can actually use

What we're looking for

  • Three or more years writing production software, comfortable across the stack
  • Strong Python or TypeScript, and confident with SQL and messy data
  • You have built pitch decks or customer-facing narratives before. Please attach one you are proud of, redacted as needed
  • Able to hold a room of plant engineers and managers without hiding behind jargon
  • Fluent Bahasa Indonesia and working English; you will present in both
  • Willing to travel to sites across Java, roughly a week a month
  • Comfortable being the only technical person in the room
  • Experience in industrial, manufacturing, energy, or logistics software
  • Solutions engineering, technical pre-sales, or consulting background
  • Data visualisation skills that survive being projected in a meeting room
  • You have worked at a startup early enough to have written the deck and the code

Compensation

We benchmark against Jakarta and Bandung senior engineering rates, and reviewannually. This role carries equity. Site travel is fully covered. The band isnegotiable and discussed openly on the first call. We will not ask what youcurrently earn.

How we hire

  • Intro call, 30 minutes. Your background, and an honest picture of what a deployment week looks like.

  • Live scenario, 90 minutes. A real plant dataset and a real question from a past pilot. You work it through with us. No whiteboard algorithms.
  • Plant visit, half a day. You come with us to a site and meet the team on real ground.
  • Offer. Usually within two weeks of the first call.

You'll create features used by research scientists, aerospace engineers, intelligence analysts, and economic forecasters, in countries around the world. Palantir's Product Development organisation is made up of small teams of Software Engineers, each focusing on a specific aspect of a product. For example, you might join a team that builds a Foundry front-end application, or a component of the Gotham release infrastructure. We encourage communication and collaboration among teams to share context, skills, and experience, so you'll learn about many different aspects of each product.

Core Responsibilities

As a Software Engineer, you are involved throughout the product lifecycle - from idea generation, design, and prototyping to execution and shipping while also being paired with a mentor dedicated to your growth and success. You'll collaborate closely with technical and non-technical counterparts to understand our customers' problems and build products that tackle them. One of the most effective ways to understand what our users need is to meet them. You may receive an opportunity to tour the assembly line at an auto-manufacturer or join a counter-terror analyst at their desk to really understand their mission and difficulties.

SWE Principles Include

  • Ownership: We see projects through from beginning to end in spite of obstacles we may encounter.
  • Collaboration: We work internally with people from a variety of backgrounds — such as other Software Engineers, Product Managers, Designers and Product Reliability Engineers. We also partner with our business development teams (Forward Deployed Engineers, Deployment Strategists) in order to understand and solve our customers' problems.
  • Trust: We trust each other to effectively handle time and priorities, and don't micromanage. We want people to have the space to think for themselves, while feeling supported by their team.

Technologies We Use

Skills

It doesn’t matter what languages you know when you join us, but it does matter that you can write clean, effective code and learn new languages quickly. Our software is constantly evolving, so we need engineers who can do the same. Alongside peers that bring diverse experience - whether you’re a former university TA, switched to CS recently, or are a hackathon enthusiast — you'll build your skills to apply the best technology to solve a given problem.

Right now, we use:

  • Varying languages, including Java and Go for backend and Typescript for frontend
  • Open-source technologies like Cassandra, Spark, Elasticsearch, React, and Redux
  • Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle, Webpack, and GitHub

What We Value

  • Ability to communicate and collaborate with a variety of individuals, including engineers, users and non-technical team members.
  • Willingness to learn and make decisions independently, and the ability to ask questions when needed.

title: Barnvakt Nanny Järfälla 4 ggr/varannan vecka
description:
Om Nannynu! / About Nannynu!

Vi är ett av Sveriges största, första och mest prisbelönta barnvaktsföretag och stolta över att ha bra villkor i linje med kollektivavtal för alla våra anställda barnvakter.

Vi tror på att leverera barnvakter i världsklass och då vi är ett växande företag söker vi nu Dig som vill ge dig ut på nya äventyr som barnvakt/nanny. Vi ser till att du får jobba i en barnvaktsfamilj som passar in på din profil och att du utbildas i bland annat Barn-HLR och barnolycksfall i samband med att du börjar jobba som barnvakt på nanny.nu. Du kommer att ha tät kontakt med din närmaste chef och ett roligt extrajobb som är en merit för livet!

Om uppdraget / About the assignment

Familj söker en barnvakt till sitt 5-åriga barn, efter schema.

Behovet består av morgonpass fyra dagar i veckan. Barnvakten kommer hem till familjen omkring kl. 05.30 när föräldern behöver lämna hemmet. Därefter ansvarar barnvakten för barnet och lämnar på förskolan. Den optimala lämningstiden är omkring kl. 08.00, men barnet kan som tidigast lämnas kl. 07.00. Förskolan ligger cirka 600 meter från hemmet.

Utöver morgonpassen finns behov av en kväll varannan vecka. Då kommer barnvakten hem omkring kl. 18.00 och stannar tills föräldern kommer hem omkring kl. 22.15, som senast kl. 23.00.

Behovet startar från vecka 42 och gäller bland annat vecka 44 och 46. Upplägget kan variera något mellan veckorna. I vissa fall kan det exempelvis vara en morgon mindre och en kväll extra. Som mest är behovet två pass per vecka utöver de planerade morgonpassen.

Din profil / Your profile

Är du en person som vill underlätta andra människors vardag i form av barnpassning samtidigt som du har ett roligt extrajobb? Vill du ansvara för det finaste en familj har, nämligen barnen, och samtidigt hjälpa föräldrar att få ihop barnpassningen? Vill du skratta, busa och bidra till att barnen får en fantastisk stund tillsammans med en person de kan se upp till? Vill du bli en del av ett företag som levererar barnpassning i världsklass? Då ska du söka jobbet som barnvakt hos en av våra familjer!

Då barnvakt är ett extraarbete ser vi gärna att du har en annan huvudsaklig sysselsättning, t.ex. studier eller deltidsjobb och för att det ska bli en långsiktig relation vill vi att du har en rimlig restid till familjen (vi brukar tänka oss runt 30 minuter).

Sök jobb som barnvakt hos oss idag!

Vi erbjuder / What we offer

Börjar du jobba som barnvakt hos oss så kan vi erbjuda dig ett roligt och meningsfullt extraarbete med goda villkor då vi har kollektivavtal.

Du får dessutom:

  • Nannycertifieringskurs där du lär dig mer om barnvaktsjobbet
  • Kurs i barn-HLR
  • Försäkring till, från och under arbetet
  • Vi vill ha ett löneupplägg som känns bra för alla kompetensprofiler och åldrar därför öppnar vi upp för individuell lönesättning för alla som en har gymnasieexamen. För alla som fortfarande går i gymnasiet har vi en fast timlön på 132,15 - 165,19 kr/timme inkl. semesterersättning.
  • Ob-tillägg samt storhelgstillägg
  • Möjlighet till fast avtal med garanterade timmar
  • Möjlighet till fortsatt arbete inom koncernen


Vid anställning som barnvakt hos oss begär vi utdrag ur belastningsregistret.

Vi intervjuar löpande och tipsar dig att vara snabb in med din ansökan.

title: Community Forestry Associate (San Fernando Valley)
description:
TreePeople is an environmental nonprofit organization that mobilizes individuals, families, communities, philanthropists, and public agencies to work together to create green, resilient communities by providing education on the benefits of planting trees, capturing rainwater, greening schools, and providing fun environmental education activities. TreePeople unites with communities to grow a greener, shadier, and more water-secure region at homes, neighborhoods, schools, and local mountains.


The Community Forestry program engages, inspires, and supports residents to take environmental action in their communities. We are looking to hire three Community Forestry Associates to support community projects throughout the San Fernando Valley region and surrounding communities. This position will perform a variety of field-based activities including tree planting, tree maintenance, volunteer coordination, community engagement, outreach, and data collection. The Associate will work closely with residents, volunteers, community partners, and TreePeople staff to support successful project implementation and department goals.


This is a grant-funded, time-limited position expected to continue through November 3, 2028, contingent upon continued funding and project needs. The position may conclude earlier upon completion of the project or expiration of funding.

ESSENTIAL JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Plant and maintain 15-gallon street trees.

  • Assist with community workshops and volunteer-led events, attend site visits, and help manage and maintain TreePeople tool inventory and trucks.

  • Drive a truck to transport trees and water trees on a regular basis.

  • Support the participation of volunteers in urban tree planting and care events.

  • Assist with the organization of community tree planting and tree care events with local volunteers.

  • Maintain accurate tree planting and maintenance data across TreePeople’s inventory systems, including GPS and site maps, to support project implementation, maintenance planning, and funding compliance.

  • Follow and reinforce established safety procedures during field activities, including proper use of personal protective equipment, tools, vehicles, and safe work practices. Promptly identify and communicate unsafe conditions to the appropriate supervisor.

  • Participate and represent TreePeople at meetings and community events as needed.

  • Support the execution of Community Forestry events by preparing materials, assisting with event setup and breakdown, guiding volunteers through established activities, and reinforcing proper tree care and safety practices

  • Support site assessments for potential tree planting locations by documenting site conditions, planting-space characteristics, infrastructure conflicts, and other field observations using approved data collection systems.

  • Support volunteer and community outreach efforts, including canvassing, participant recruitment, follow-up communication, and distribution of approved educational and outreach materials.

  • Other duties as assigned

  • Strong leadership, team-building, and problem-solving skills.

  • Highly organized, strong work ethic, friendly, smart, proactive and a quick learner.

  • Interested in local climate resilience and environmental issues impacting communities throughout Southern California.

  • Valid CA Driver’s license and clean driving record desired to perform job-related essential functions.

  • Available to work a flexible schedule that will include weekends.

title: Medical Records II
description:
Summary

The Medical Records II position primarily serves as a dedicated resource to assist the CDI team with retrieving medical records to close identified Hierarchical Condition Category (HCC) gaps for new patients. This role ensures that documentation is complete, accurate, and timely to support value-based care, continuity of care, and regulatory compliance.

In addition to CDI-focused responsibilities, the specialist performs the full scope of Medical Records Coordinator duties, including processing internal record requests, reviewing and uploading documents into the Electronic Medical Record (EMR) system, and maintaining accurate, auditable records. This position requires attention to detail, strong organizational skills, and effective communication with internal teams and external providers.

Duties and Responsibilities

  1. Request and retrieve prior medical records from external providers for new patients with HCC gaps identified by the CDI team.
  2. Document all outreach and follow-up related to HCC gap resolution in the EMR.
  3. Prioritize record retrieval based on CDI needs and workflow standards to ensure timely completion.
  4. Collaborate closely with the CDI team to ensure documentation supports accurate coding and continuity of care.
  5. Process incoming faxed, scanned, or mailed medical documents within defined turnaround times by uploading them accurately into the EMR.
  6. Review documents for correct patient identification, date of service, document type, and duplicate status before finalizing upload.
  7. Respond to internal record requests: collect and complete necessary forms, submit external requests (fax, phone, portal), and log all outreach attempts and outcomes.
  8. Prioritize requests based on urgency and departmental guidelines; escalate or follow-up on outstanding requests until closure or defined resolution.
  9. Obtain and upload external medical records (e.g., from hospitals, specialists, imaging centers, prior providers), and update request status accordingly.
  10. Maintain detailed, auditable documentation in the EMR of all actions taken, including request logs, follow-up notes, and final disposition.
  11. Adhere strictly to HIPAA, state privacy laws, and internal confidentiality policies in all record handling.
  12. Comply with productivity, accuracy, and workflow standards set by the department.
  13. Identify opportunities for process improvement, workflow optimization, and system enhancements in record handling.
  14. Perform other duties as assigned to support the Medical Records department and organizational goals.

Qualifications

Education/Experience:

  1. High school diploma or equivalent required; additional education in healthcare, medical administration, or clinical coding preferred.
  2. Experience in clinical documentation improvement, medical coding, or medical records management preferred.
  3. Proficiency in EMR systems, document management, and data entry
  4. Experience handling medical record requests, including retrieval from external facilities and patient record processing.
  5. Knowledge of medical terminology and familiarity with chronic conditions preferred.
  6. Familiarity with HIPAA regulations and confidentiality standards.

Skills:

  1. Strong understanding of clinical documentation and HCC gap identification.
  2. Knowledge of medical terminology, chronic conditions, and coding practices.
  3. Ability to follow standardized workflows and procedures accurately and consistently.
  4. Strong organizational skills to manage multiple tasks and prioritize CDI and medical records requests.
  5. Detail-oriented with the ability to review documents for accuracy, completeness, and correct patient assignment.
  6. Proficient in EMR navigation, document scanning/uploading, and record management.
  7. Effective communication skills for coordinating with CDI team members, medical staff, patients, and external providers.
  8. Ability to use independent judgment to prioritize record requests and follow-ups based on CDI needs.
  9. Familiarity with HIPAA regulations and confidentiality standards in all aspects of record handling.
  10. Basic computer skills, including Microsoft Office applications, email, and document management tools.
  11. Ability to analyze clinical information and support value-based care initiatives through accurate documentation.

title: Construction / Bridge Inspector Engineer – Entry/Junior Level

Moffatt & Nichol specializes in large complex waterfront infrastructure projects and is recognized as one of the worldwide leaders in this field. We are looking for an individual who has a strong foundation in construction principles, has strong inspection and report writing skills and can assist as an NBIS bridge inspector (or ability and willingness to become) certification when construction oversight is light.

About Moffatt & Nichol:

Moffatt & Nichol is a leading U.S.-based global infrastructure advisor specializing in the planning and design of facilities that shape and serve our coastlines, harbors and rivers, as well as an innovator in transportation. For the 5th year in a row, Moffatt & Nichol is Ranked #1 in Engineering News-Record for Marine & Port Facilities in the U.S. Additionally, our firm consistently ranks in the Top 100 Pure Designers in the US and the Top 50 Designers in International Markets.

Moffatt & Nichol's professional staff includes engineers, planners, scientists and architects who serve our global client base from offices in Europe, North America, Latin America, and the Pacific Rim. Duties and Responsibilities:

Construction Inspector:

  • Performs inspection of bridges, transportation structures and other structurers during construction to evaluate contractor’s method, workmanship, quality and compliance with construction documents (drawings and specifications). Inspector will evaluate construction materials for quality and compliance with Contract Documents and perform related work such as data collection, report writing and record keeping
  • Recognizes basic construction or engineering problems, coordinates problems with the engineer of record; makes field measurements of pay items; checks equipment; maintains comprehensive project records including daily diaries, materials notebooks, as-built plans, pay quantity records, progress schedules, work orders, and monthly estimates

  • Reviews and processes contractor’s shop drawing submittals

NBIS Bridge Inspector:

  • Partners with other professionals and departments to gather information for projects
  • Works collaboratively with all members of the inspection group
  • Conducts inspections and assists in supervision of site investigations as needed
  • Prepares or assists in preparation of bridge inspection reports including data entry, writing and photo editing
  • Performs checker review of bridge inspection reports by others
  • Works collaboratively with members of all company disciplines
  • Assists with various project elements including planning, execution and follow-up
  • Performs other duties as required

Other Duties:

Please note this job posting is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Engineering or related
  • Minimum of an Engineer in Training (EIT) required
  • Transportation related construction inspection experience in the United States
  • 1 to 4 years of heavy construction experience and/or inspection oversight on transportation related projects. Desired experience includes: bridges, culverts, and/or roadways
  • Minimum 1+ years of experience serving as a NBIS Inspector strongly preferred; desired bridge inspection certifications: NHI Certification (NHI-130055) and Refresher (NHI-130053), if applicable
  • Inspection experience utilizing special equipment such as snooper/bucket trucks, boats, scaffolding, etc. preferred
  • Ability to read and interpret construction plans, specifications and standards
  • Boater Safety Card preferred
  • Valid driver’s license in good standing
  • Ability and willingness to work in the field 5 days per week Monday - Friday with occasional evenings and weekends. Field hours are project specific and may occasionally require overnight construction inspection as deemed necessary by the project
  • Availability and willingness to travel as required. Overnight travel is not expected but may be necessary on a limited basis
  • Must be available for hire no later than the end of November 2026; sooner is preferred
  • Selected candidate must consent to and pass a post-offer/pre-employment drug screening
  • All new hires will be required to successfully complete and pass a pre-employment (post offer) background check in compliance with NIST 800-171
  • Moffatt & Nichol uses E-Verify and employment is contingent upon the legal ability to obtain employment in the U.S. and to present the required documentation at hire

Working conditions:

The work takes place in both the office and the field which may require occasional extended hours, night shifts or weekends to meet project requirements. Inclement weather may occur.

Physical requirements:

Must be able to navigate field and climb as required to inspect bridges and perform inspection of construction. Site visits may be required which may necessitate navigating unpaved or natural terrain while carrying equipment. Ability to navigate office and utilize standard office equipment. Attend client meetings and travel as necessary.

Base salary range:

$31.00 to $43.00 per hour based on years of experience, level of education obtained, professional registration, and meeting the required qualifications in the job description.

Base salary range only applicable for candidates who will be hired and working in the Virginia market.
